0.content:
Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel (also: Temporary Main Tunnel): The Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel is the main way into the Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue: two huge caves joined by a smaller one. Its name suggests a tunnel dug quickly for one purpose, reaching the deeper mine. Lamps, black mud, Treasure Hoarders and slimes fill it.

The Chasm Exploration Team's noticeboard stands here, and a burnt miner's log hints at what drove the miners out. The deeper tunnels beyond were sealed when the miners dispersed.

Geography: The area is built from two huge caves with a smaller cave between them, and it is described as the mine's main entrance. Lumenlamps and glowing Luminous Seelie give light; Dark Mud, Oozing Concretions and Spoutrock occur here; Cor Lapis and Noctilucous Jade can be gathered.

History: This was a working mine before the Chasm was closed. A damaged log records that an excavation team was to be disbanded, with its collected data handed to a messenger from Huishan Hall, and that Treasure Hoarders might be to blame for something. A second page says the detailed data went to the secretary at Yujing Terrace (the wiki identifies her as Ganyu) so that the long-term effects on the Chasm could be judged, and that a strange black mud had been found.

Dangers: Elite foes are Shadowy Husk Defenders and Mirror Maidens. Common ones are Geo and Hydro Slimes (including large ones) and several kinds of Treasure Hoarders: Crushers, Pugilists, Scouts and Electro, Hydro and Pyro Potioneers.

Travel: Reached through the Chasm after the Chasm Delvers questline opens the Underground Mines (2.6). The Exploration Team Campsite Noticeboard stands here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it remains an abandoned mine passage used by the Exploration Team; later story versions add nothing to it.

1.comment: Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel: Chasm Exploration Team
1.content: The Chasm Exploration Team is a group hired by the Ministry of Civil Affairs to investigate anomalies in the Chasm; its base is the Chasm Exploration Team Camp in the Underground Mines. A noticeboard for the camp stands in the Ad-Hoc Main Tunnel. The team is the focus of the Chasm Delvers world quests, after which Muning makes it an official part of Huishan Hall.

2.content:
Adeptus's Repose (also: Adeptus' Repose, Herblord's abode): Adeptus's Repose is the former home of the Herblord, an adeptus of Chenyu Vale who healed mortals with medicines. It lies in the Southern Mountain of Chenyu Vale, behind an entrance choked with miasma, and holds her medicine jar, a withered adeptal tree and notes she left behind. The Herblord is long gone from here; her later life is as Changsheng, the snake companion of Baizhu.

Visitors can enter either by clearing the miasma around the entrance or through the world quest Silently the Butterfly Crosses the Valley (4.4), in which the Traveler restores the adeptal tree by gathering the scattered butterflies the Herblord once used to adorn her door.

Geography: Adeptus's Repose is a sheltered cave-dwelling in the Southern Mountain of Chenyu Vale, linked to Lingshu Courtyard and Yaodie Valley. Inside are a bookshelf-lined vault, a medicine jar with a mechanism linked to the door, and a tree branch planted in it; to the west lies Lingshu Courtyard.

Places: - The medicine jar and the withered tree: the jar nourishes the tree.
- The stone gate and door mechanism, linked to the jar with adeptal energy.
- A hidden vault with bookshelves holding the Ancient Texts.
- Lingshu Courtyard to the west, the neighbouring courtyard with its Carefree Simulacrum.

People: No one lives here. The Herblord, who once did, left when she lost the power to keep a human form. In the neighbouring Lingshu Courtyard, talking stone statues called Simulacra still scare off intruders in her name.

History: The Herblord was an adeptus with the original form of a giant white snake, who took human form to make medicines and heal the sick. The unsigned notes in the Repose read as private jottings, kept locked away, and the wiki links them to the Herblord: a chatty fish friend (taken to be Fujin), a beast friend who asked for slimming tea (taken to be Lingyuan), and a master about whom the writer had a bad feeling. Fearing something might happen, the writer split off some adeptal energy and put it into butterflies, so that mortals of Chenyu Vale might later follow them to the formulae left behind.

Atmosphere: Still, hidden and a little forlorn: empty medicine containers, a tree that can be revived and butterflies scattered by an absent mistress.

Dangers: Miasma blocks the entrance. Once cleared, the cave is peaceful.

Travel: Enter by clearing the miasma around the entrance, or through the butterflies quest: after the tree is revived, an investigation spot in the water near the ancient tree takes the player to the Repose.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Adeptus's Repose is a quiet, hidden abode with no occupants. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Herblord lives on as Changsheng, with Baizhu. The quest leaves the adeptal tree revived and the vault open.

3.comment: Adeptus's Repose: The Herblord and Changsheng
3.content: The Herblord was a white-snake adeptus of Chenyu Vale who healed mortals. After her fight with the Mistress of Chenyu Vale she was reduced to a small snake and forgot her past. A doctor who had lost his family to a plague found her in her abode and agreed to the "Way of the Dragon-Dragging Jade Snake", which gives powerful healing arts at the cost of the contractor's own health; she became Changsheng. The contract passed down generations until it came to Baizhu, who promised it would end with him.

4.content:
Alcor (also: The Alcor, Flagship of the Crux): The Alcor is the flagship of the Crux fleet, led by Captain Beidou. It sails the open seas and can even push through tempest-torn waters; when at rest it is anchored off Guyun Stone Forest in Liyue. Beidou herself is often ashore on business, leaving the ship to her crew.

Geography: The ship is anchored just off the southeastern end of the island that holds the Domain of Guyun, in the Sea of Clouds. Visitors can climb aboard. The ship carries chests near the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber and on the crow's nest nearest the stern, and a Geoculus sits at the top of the highest crow's nest.

Places: The main deck, where the crew each have their own post (the ironworker Suling, the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber, the surgeon Yinxing and others), and the crow's nests above it.

People: Beidou is captain. Crew on board include Juza (chief mate), Yinxing (surgeon at sea), Huixing (navigator), Suling (ironworker), Mora-Grubber (bookkeeper), and the sailors Furong, Sea Drake and Xu Liushi, plus Little Yue. See their own entries where they exist.

Culture: The Crux carries cargo, takes bounties and, as the wiki notes, also trades illegally. The Liyue Qixing more or less approve of its voyages. After each voyage the crew hold a three-day feast; the chef Xiangling was once hired for it and later became a regular guest.

Atmosphere: A heavily armed ship at rest, with wary sailors who treat strangers as intruders at first. The ship's name is read as an omen of death.

Travel: Climb aboard from the shore at Guyun Stone Forest. Once the world quest A Lone Ship in Guyun is done, the ship becomes a permanent teleport waypoint on the map.

Quests: A Lone Ship in Guyun (World Quest): the Traveler boards and is mistaken for a stowaway by Juza, then helps crew members with errands: Yinxing's letter to Bolai, Little Yue's gift for Changchang, and meat for Juza.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Alcor remains the Crux's flagship; the sources read note no change to its location.

5.content: The Alcor is the Crux's flagship, anchored off Guyun Stone Forest when Beidou is ashore. Juza minds the ship, and the crew do not leave without her orders.

6.content: An armed fleet based in Liyue Harbor, led by Captain Beidou, known for daring voyages and bounties. It divides into the Spear (naval warfare, cargo) and the Shield (survival skills, navigation). Beidou has an unusual relationship with the Qixing's Ningguang, who says she hires Beidou, not the fleet.

7.content:
Baiju Guesthouse (also: White Horse Guesthouse): The Baiju Guesthouse is an inn near the entrance to Liyue Harbor, where the waitress Xiuhua greets guests asking whether they want a meal or a room for the night. It is a modest, ordinary lodging house rather than a grand establishment.

Its name means roughly "White Horse Guesthouse" in Chinese. It is one of the places in the Harbor where travellers can stay, alongside the better-known Wangshu Inn outside the city.

People: Xiuhua is the guesthouse's serving girl; by her own account she is just one of the service staff and "nothing special". She has a twin sister, Yuhua, who waits tables at the Wangshu Inn, and the two sometimes swap places at their respective inns, so a guest may meet one while expecting the other.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1.

Zibai, the White Horse Adeptus, took lodgings here after her soul was restored during the Lantern Rite event story, and told the Traveler she would live there for a while.

8.content:
Beneath the Dragon-Queller (also: Domain Beneath the Dragon-Queller, Memories: Earthshaking Dragon): Beneath the Dragon-Queller is the Trounce Domain under the great blue-veined Dragon-Queller tree at Nantianmen in Liyue. It is the bed of rock deep in the earth where the Geo dragon Azhdaha is sealed. Within the game it is a "memory": after the Traveler and Zhongli re-imprisoned Azhdaha in Zhongli's story quest "No Mere Stone", the fight can be relived here.

The domain's own description calls the rock bed a coffin carved into the heart of the world, and says Azhdaha was in the end unable to unseal itself, so the quaking earth was put to rest. The in-game name of the replay is "Memories: Earthshaking Dragon". It is a weekly challenge rather than an ordinary Artifact domain: one dragon, five elements, and an entrance that shows which elements Azhdaha will draw on that week.

Geography: The entrance is reached through the Dragon-Queller, a huge tree with blue veins growing near Mt. Hulao at Nantianmen, in the Minlin area of Liyue. Its tip points straight at Liyue Harbor. The domain itself is a vast underground chamber of rock "carved into the very heart of the world", with the dragon's tail rising above as the tree.

History: Azhdaha was an ancient Geo dragon who once ruled much of what became Liyue and befriended Morax, the Geo Archon (now Zhongli). As erosion ate at his memory and humans damaged the ley lines of the Chasm by mining, he turned on the people he had sworn to protect. Morax and the adepti fought him from the Chasm north to Nantianmen and sealed his eroded self under the tree, with the help of Azhdaha's own benevolent consciousness.

Dangers: Azhdaha is a colossal Geo dragon who absorbs Cryo, Pyro, Electro and Hydro from the ley lines in a weekly rotation shown at the entrance. In the domain, characters struck by those elemental attacks while unshielded are marked and take continuing damage (the domain's ley line disorder). Players can clear it any number of times but claim the rewards once a week.

Quests: Unlocked by completing "No Mere Stone", the second act of Zhongli's Historia Antiqua Chapter story quest (the quest requires Adventure Rank 40). Its last quest, "Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved", is the story of the fight.

Atmosphere: Cold blue moonlit light on the tree above; below, heavy dark stone, tremors, and the dragon's slow voice. The place feels like an old grave that still breathes.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 Azhdaha remains sealed and the domain is a permanent replay. Nothing later in canon changes this.

9.comment: Beneath the Dragon-Queller: Azhdaha's seal and Jiu
9.content: The Dragon-Queller tree at Nantianmen is part of the seal on Azhdaha. The sealed dragon sent Jiu, a child-looking vessel made of a portion of its power, to guide Chasm miners to the tree and break the seal. A tablet by Mountain Shaper warns travellers off. Jiu is described factually as a small girl whose hatred of Morax was brushed off by those she met.

10.comment: Beneath the Dragon-Queller: Erosion and the Chasm
10.content: Azhdaha's decline is the standard example of erosion in Liyue's story: forgotten faces, forgotten contracts, then violence. The Chasm mining that disturbed the ley lines, and Morax's failed attempt to halt it by sharing his power, are both parts of the account the benevolent half gives in No Mere Stone.

11.content:
Bishui Plain (also: Bishui Plains, Blue Water Plain): Bishui Plain is the broad, river-watered plain of northern Liyue, named for the Bishui River that runs through it ("Blue Water Plain"). It is the first stretch of Liyue most travelers from Mondstadt cross: the road runs through Dihua Marsh, past Wangshu Inn and the Stone Gate crossroads, and on south to Liyue Harbor. In its hills sit the terraced village of Qingce, the haunted Wuwang Hill and the sealed salt-god ruin of Sal Terrae.

The plain mixes the everyday and the uncanny: farmers, merchants and Millelith patrols use its roads, while the same ground holds a serpent god's old seal at Qingce, a hill under permanent gloom and a vanished civilisation's city.

Geography: The Bishui River flows down from Yilong Wharf through Chenyu Vale, drops over a waterfall into central Liyue and widens in Dihua Marsh, where it splits: one arm ends in the lake near Dawn Winery, the other runs through Qiongji Estuary into the Sea of Clouds. Qingce Village sits at the foot of Mt. Qingce in the northernmost hills.

Places: Stone Gate is the crossroads where roads from Dawn Winery (northeast), Wuwang Hill and Qingce (northwest), and Dihua Marsh and Liyue Harbor (south) meet. Dihua Marsh holds a Statue of the Seven on the main road. Wangshu Inn is a tall inn on a stone pillar. Qingce Village is a quiet wooden village with blue roofs. Wuwang Hill lies under grey skies. Sal Terrae is a sealed ruin.

History: Long ago the serpent god Chi nested at what is now Mt. Qingce until Morax slew it and bound its power. Havria, God of Salt, held out at Sal Terrae through the Archon War until her own people killed her. Wangshu Inn already stood in the years after the Cataclysm. Over a decade ago a failed rite at Wuwang Hill killed Hu Tao's father and cost Old Hu much of his life.

Travel: The plain is the main northern entrance to Liyue from Mondstadt: from Dawn Winery and Stone Gate down through Dihua Marsh to Liyue Harbor, with Wangshu Inn as the last comfortable stop. The river is also a working waterway.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the plain is quiet working country along Liyue's northern road.

No change specific to Bishui Plain is recorded in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content. The river still carries trade, Qingce is still a retirement-leaning village, and Wuwang Hill remains fog-bound.

12.comment: Bishui Plain: The Chi of Qingce
12.content: The Chi was a serpent god that nested at Mt. Qingce and took the region. Morax fought and killed it at a great height, but its power kept seeping into the land, so he conquered each of its aspects in turn and taught Qingce's people to carve Geo statues to crush what remained. Adeptus amber around the village does the same. Legend says the Chi's body became Mt. Qingce and its blood fed the Blood-Fed Trees, but Zhongli points out the mountain predates the beast. The Vault of Qingce, behind a waterfall, is rumored to hold the Chi's remains; its large amber crystals are said to be congealed Chi blood.

13.content: Wuwang Hill was an ordinary hill until a calamity over a decade ago. Fetor leaking from the boundary between life and death threatened the area, so Old Hu and Hu Tao's father performed the Art of Homa to burn it away. The younger man did not perform the rite correctly (Hu Tao later attributes it to attachments that pulled his focus away) and died from the fetor; a flood devastated a nearby village. Old Hu managed the fallout at great cost to his lifespan and died before sixty. Today an eerie fog and drifting blue lights remain and the hill is a dare-spot for tests of courage. A Hidden Palace beneath it holds an evil chi sealed long ago with the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method.

14.content: Wangshu Inn is a tall, many-storied inn on a stone pillar at the south end of Dihua Marsh, where traveling merchants trade and stay. Zhongli says it was built tall for visibility and is a strategic point that must be defended. It already stood in the years after the Cataclysm. The keepers, Verr Goldet and Huai'an, are in fact Liyue Qixing agents who report directly to Ningguang, and the commercial inn is a cover for quietly supporting Xiao as he excises plagues. Stall-keepers whisper that the tower hides a secret, but none has proved it.

15.comment: Bishui Plain: Sal Terrae and the God of Salt
15.content: Sal Terrae ("salt of the earth") was founded by Havria, a gentle and relatively weak god who refused to join the Archon War and made concession after concession until only a tiny plot was left. According to the quest-confirmed account, her people's first and last king killed her to show that kindness would not save them, and the blast of her death turned everyone nearby to salt. Some who lived outside the blast fled to Morax's harbor. Havria herself owned a salt chalice that refilled itself and a ruler that could turn the ground to salt. The civilisation's legacy is Yinyuan Hall. A seal still guards the ruin, and in Zhongli's story quest the Traveler helps open it.

16.content:
Blackcliff Forge: Blackcliff Forge is Liyue's most important mining and smelting facility, carved into Mt. Tianheng. It was made by digging out the mountain and linking workshops and furnaces with tunnels blackened by dust. It is known as the birthplace of the Blackcliff and Prototype series of weapons, and white tassels are made there too.

A shift supervisor, workers and a Millelith guard work at the site. The forge's motto is "Let our actions be recognized by hard work. Let our achievements be what speaks first."

Places: The forge is a network of workshops and furnaces joined by tunnels in the rock of Mt. Tianheng, in the Sea of Clouds area above Liyue Harbor. The tunnels are blackened by soot and dust, hence the name.

People: Manager Kuan is the shift supervisor; Jingda and Iron Shoulder are workers; Gummer is a Millelith soldier posted there. The forge motto is repeated by Kuan himself.

History: During the cataclysm period the Yun family, who ran a family forge for hundreds of years, were led by Yun Huang and Yun Hui (seventh and eighth family heads per weapon text). After the monster threat ended, a martial arts renaissance created more demand for weapons than makers could meet, and Yun Hui turned to the master craftsman Han Wu, who drew up the Prototype designs. Over the following centuries the Yun family moved from smithing to Liyue opera, and by Yun Jin's generation few of them still forge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forge remains in use, still producing weapons and white tassels.

No major change is recorded. The Yun family's founding link is told as history; canon does not say who runs the forge today.

17.comment: Blackcliff Forge: Blackcliff and Prototype Series
17.content: The forge's weapons are the Blackcliff Series and the Prototype Series. The Prototype designs were drawn up by Han Wu after research with the Yun family head Yun Hui, about five hundred years ago. White tassels are also produced here.

18.comment: Blackcliff Forge: Cloudforged and the Yuheng
18.content: Cloudforged, a weapon released as a reward of the limited-time event Mutual Security Enhancing Simulation (2024), is described in its text as a prototype of a standard-issue weapon that the Yuheng, Keqing, commissioned from Blackcliff Forge after analysing the ancient mechanisms that guard the adepti's abode on Mt. Tianheng. The same text gives the forge's lore (tunnels blasted black by dust, the Yun family's founder as first digger, mountain tribes sheltering there in war).

19.content:
Carp's Rest (also: Clarion Echo): Carp's Rest is a sealed, cave-like refuge on Mt. Laixin in Chenyu Vale, Liyue, where the adeptus Fujin, a golden carp who once took human form, has rested since the Archon War. It holds the Votive Rainjade, a ritual jade that the Traveler can feed with recovered adeptal energy (Spirit Carp) to strengthen the blessings of the vale's soil and water. Its entrance is closed by Fujin's own power.

Fujin insists it is not a true adeptal abode: she cannot create new adeptal realms the way the southern adepti can, and calls it at best a cave. It appeared in Version 4.4 with the Chenyu Vale region.

Geography: A subarea of Mt. Laixin, the "sacred mountain" where the spirit veins of Chenyu Vale converge, so that whoever controls the mountain can control all the land of the vale. Carp's Rest is reached from the mountain's summit area near Chiwang Terrace; the gate has to be opened with adeptal energy before anyone can go down. Its one point of interest is the Votive Rainjade.

People: Fujin lives here, in her carp form. Her voice answers visitors from below the entrance; she apologises for forgetting to unlock it and admits she is embarrassed to be seen only as a carp. She says the Traveler, Paimon and Lingyuan are the first visitors since the adeptus Herblord left. Lingyuan, her old friend, cannot enter on his own because he lacks her adeptal energy.

History: According to the story told in An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade, Fujin hurled the Votive Rainjade into the waters from Mt. Lingmeng to save Chenyu Vale when its former mistress flooded the Bishui River during the Archon War. Afterwards she "sank into the sea," lost most of her strength, and was confined to Carp's Rest for thousands of years, able to recall the world only through the scent of tea offerings. In the present the Traveler helped her perform the Rainjade Rite; that left her reverted to a carp, which is why she is found here recovering.

Travel: Unlocked by completing The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose, which becomes available one in-game day after An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade (part of the Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade series). Teleportation is to the Mt. Laixin area, then on foot to the gate.

Quests: Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade (Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, in which Fujin first draws the Traveler and Paimon into an adepti space; An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade; The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Carp's Rest is unchanged: Fujin recovers here, and the Votive Rainjade can be fed with Spirit Carp. No later story content was found that alters it.

20.comment: Carp's Rest: The Votive Rainjade and Rainjade's Benediction
20.content: The Votive Rainjade is the jade in Carp's Rest into which the Traveler offers Spirit Carp, fragments of adeptal energy, to raise the "Rainjade's Benediction" and earn rewards. In story terms it stands for the old rite of Chenyu Vale: pour adeptal energy into the spirit veins and the soil and water recover and the weather stays favourable. Fujin says balance has already returned to the water and soil, but more power in the jade would secure good weather and prosperous years ahead.

21.content:
Chasm Exploration Team Camp (also: Chasm Exploration Team Camps, Chasm Exploration Camp): The Chasm Exploration Team Camps (an unofficial, community name) are two campsites that the Chasm Exploration Team, a group hired by Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs, keeps inside The Chasm's Underground Mines in Liyue. They are the team's bases and the places where its members can be found while the Traveler helps survey the mines.

The first camp is established during the world quest Chasm Spelunkers, the third part of The Chasm Delvers series, when the Traveler follows the team to it. The second camp appears after the quest Perils in the Dark. Small cages at the camps hold golden finches, which the wiki notes may be a nod to the mine canaries real miners used to detect dangerous gas; the game does not explain them.

People: Where NPCs stand depends on how far the player has completed The Chasm Delvers and the quest Valor's Afterglow. At the end of those quests, the first camp is home to Hao (a miner of The Chasm) and You Jun, a Millelith sergeant. The second holds Jinwu (the team's safety technician), Khedive (ecologist) and Taliesin (a bard). Jiaming and Tu can be found near the north-westernmost waypoint in the Chasm rather than at a camp.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the camps remain part of the Underground Mines in Liyue, staffed by team members and local miners. No later change to them is recorded.

22.content:
Chenlong Cleft (also: Sunken Jade Gorge): Chenlong Cleft is a hidden cavern in Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale, beneath the stretch of river that flows under Jademouth. The Traveler enters it by jumping into a whirlpool during the world quest Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu. Its Chinese name means Sunken Jade Gorge.

After that quest the cleft can be entered or left only by Teleport Waypoint. It holds a Golden Carp's Leap, Seelie and a Pyro Elemental Monument.

Geography: A cavern below the river bed near Jademouth, part of the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale. Features listed are a Golden Carp's Leap, Seelie and a Pyro Elemental Monument.

History: Chenyu Vale's ancestors, after great changes to the land cut them off from the heavens, took to casting jade into the river and praying for good weather, firm banks and fertile soil. The Votive Rainjade in the depths is the very last such offering ever thrown, according to the adeptus Fujin; the custom was abandoned once the long war to become gods began, though its name survived.

People: Fujin, an adeptus in golden carp form, speaks with the Traveler here and says the jade should be restored. Little Mao, a local child, guides the Traveler to the site, and says a friend in the mountains taught him the stories.

Dangers: In the quest's cavern scenes the Traveler meets Hydro Mimic Squirrels, a Large Hydro Slime, hilichurls and the boar-shaped "Beast Lord of Fuyu".

Travel: Entry: jump into the whirlpool at Jademouth when the quest asks. After the quest, only the Teleport Waypoint takes you in or out.

Quests: The cleft belongs to the second part of the world-quest series "Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade", Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu. The next part is An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade.

Status as of 7.1: Accessible only by waypoint after the quest; unchanged as of 7.1.

23.comment: Chenlong Cleft: Votive Rainjade and the Rainjade Rite
23.content: The Votive Rainjade is the last jade thrown into the river by Chenyu Vale's ancient people. Fujin explains that it grew huge from uncontrolled adeptal energy; the Traveler restores it by gathering scattered energy. The Rainjade Rite is the ritual meant to repel the miasma on the vale and nurse the soil and water back to health.

24.content:
Chenyu Vale (also: Chenyu): Chenyu Vale is the fog-wrapped mountain country of western Liyue, on the border with Fontaine, famous for its tea. Its people live in Qiaoying Village, the tea-making heart of the vale, and trade through Yilong Wharf, a busy river port that Fontainians visit for a taste of Liyue. Long ago a nameless goddess ruled the vale, and three adepti served her: the white snake Herblord, the golden carp Fujin and the suanni Lingyuan. Legends of jade sunk in the river give the vale its name.

The vale has three areas: the Upper Vale (the village, the wharf and the Bishui River), the Southern Mountain (old adeptal and ancient sites around Mt. Yaojun), and Mt. Laixin, the sacred mountain where the vale's spirit veins meet. The first settlers came from the Chasm, and their ancestors were refugees of the ancient civilisation of Lang-Gan.

Geography: Steep, misty karst peaks, terraced tea slopes, waterfalls and jade-green rivers. The Bishui River starts near Yilong Wharf in the northwest, flows through the vale past Qiaoying Village, then narrows and drops by a waterfall into central Liyue. The climate is noticeably more humid than in the Hills of Barsom nearby. Mt. Mingyuan, west of Yilong Wharf, lies directly beneath the floating island of Celestia, which hangs overhead.

Places: - **Qiaoying Village**: the tea village, sending its leaves to Liyue Harbor and to other nations.
- **Yilong Wharf** (also Yilong Port): a trading port across the water from Fontaine.
- **Jademouth**: giant jade slabs in the Bishui River. Legend says an adeptus threw them down to stop a flood.
- **Mt. Laixin**: the sacred mountain. Whoever controls it controls all the land of the vale.

People: Tea growers, roasters and merchants. Grandpa Lu, a village elder, and Uncle Luo, who oversees a tea workshop, speak for Qiaoying, and Jin works at the Chunming Teaworks. The adeptus Fujin and the suanni Lingyuan (nicknamed "Bluey" by the local boy Little Mao) still live in the vale. Yilong Wharf has Fontainian tea merchants, a Millelith sergeant, hired guards and boatmen.

Economy: Tea is everything. Qiaoying's tea is sold in Liyue Harbor and abroad. Fontaine imports it through Lumidouce Harbor, and Fontainian tea merchants trade at Yilong Wharf. People believe the adepti blessed the vale's land and water. A special cauldron in the village, said to be an adeptal mechanism, roasts the leaves and gives them their aroma.

Culture: Jade is sacred here. The vale's ancestors made offerings by throwing jade into the water, believing this sent adeptal energy into the spirit veins, protected their homeland and brought good harvests. The old rites were later forgotten. Families go to Yilong Wharf to honour their ancestors and the dead, and the custom of throwing jade into the water continued even after the old goddess fell and Morax came.

History: When a Celestial Nail destroyed Lang-Gan (in what is now the Chasm), survivors fled and founded the first settlements here. The wiki dates the Chasm's creation to about 6,000 years ago. Fujin, a golden carp adeptus, guided them, taught them jade rites, reshaped soil and water for farming, and planted the first tea tree on the Herblord's land. In the Archon War the Mistress of Chenyu Vale fought Morax. Driven mad, she finally raised a flood down the Bishui River that would have drowned her own people. Her three adepti rebelled. Lingyuan led the people to safety, the Herblord fought the goddess, and Fujin climbed Mt. Lingmeng and threw the Votive Rainjade into the river, creating the Jademouth. The Mistress was sealed away, and Morax brought peace to the vale.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the vale is peaceful and its tea trade thriving. The Traveler and Fujin repaired the damage Lingyuan did, though some miasma remains.

Fujin is recovering at Carp's Rest. With enough of her power restored she can take human form again, and she and Lingyuan are friends once more. The Herblord lives on as Changsheng, the snake who travels with Baizhu in Liyue Harbor. The 7.1 Celestial Nail anomaly centres on the neighbouring Chasm, not on the vale.

25.content: Qiaoying Village is the tea village of Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale, known across Teyvat for its tea. The smell of tea fills its peaceful streets. Grandpa Lu blamed the vale's soil and water when the tea declined. Uncle Luo oversees a workshop where Jin operates the machines, and the Fontainian Hautemontagne maintains them. The village roasts its leaves in an old cauldron said to be an adeptal mechanism, and every year it holds a tea-serving ceremony with floral tea brewed from Spiritscent Flower petals.

26.content: Yilong Wharf is a thriving trading port on the Fontaine border, southeast of Lumidouce Harbor. Fontainians come here to experience Liyue culture without travelling to Liyue Harbor. It has an upper level of teahouses (the Jiulue Teahouse), tea merchants, a storyteller and a Millelith post, and a lower level of street food, anglers and a hydrologist. Families come here to honour their ancestors, and local artisans still make jade ornaments.

27.comment: Chenyu Vale: The Mistress of Chenyu Vale and her three adepti
27.content: The Mistress of Chenyu Vale was an ancient jade goddess whose true name is forgotten. She was among the first gods worshipped by the people of old Liyue. She ruled the beasts, spirits and adepti of the wild mountains, judged between mortals and nature, and controlled the Bishui River. Fujin says she was not evil and made many dreams come true, until the Archon War drove her mad in her bid to become an Archon. Her adepti were the Herblord, a white snake who took human form and healed the sick; Fujin, a golden carp devoted to humans and their tea; and Lingyuan, a wild suanni who never warmed to people. When the Mistress unleashed the flood, they turned against her and saved the vale.

28.content:
Chenyu Vale: Southern Mountain (also: Southern Mountain, Chenyu Southern Mountain): The Southern Mountain is the quieter, older half of Chenyu Vale, added in 4.4. It is a land of tea slopes, butterfly valleys and ruins, where the first tea tree of the vale still grows, where the snake adeptus called the Herblord once kept a courtyard, and where the ancient city of Chizhang once stood under the vale's goddess. A solitary suanni, Lingyuan, ranges over its mountains.

Most of what survives here is memory: empty medicine jars, stone statues that talk in their sleep, shrine foundations and a few withered trees waiting for adeptal power.

Geography: Rugged tea country south of Qiaoying Village. Teatree Slope lies south of the village and north of Yaodie Valley; Mt. Xuanlian rises south of both Yaodie Valley and Chizhang Wall, which lies to its north. Lingshu Courtyard hides in a cave reached from Yaodie Valley.

Places: Chizhang Wall: the ruin of the city governed by the mistress of Chenyu Vale; a desolate shrine foothill. Adeptus' Repose and Lingshu Courtyard: the old home of the Herblord. Teatree Slope: the first tea tree, planted by Fujin. Yaodie Valley: the valley of vibrant butterflies. Mt. Xuanlian: a lone mountain south of the valley.

History: Chizhang was the mistress's city. Her three servants, Herblord, Fujin and Lingyuan, were adepti of wild mountain nature. Fujin planted the first tea tree on land that was the Herblord's. In the Archon War the mistress turned cruel and tried to flood the vale; the three rebelled, and the Herblord, her body torn apart in the fight, was reduced to a small form that could barely survive.

Travel: Teleport waypoints connect the slope, valley and Chizhang Wall. Adeptal energy from Fujin is required for the puzzle mechanisms, such as Carefree Simulacra and Golden Carp's Leap.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Southern Mountain is a quiet, ruined wilderness, its tea tree alive and its butterflies back in their jar.

Fujin returned to her abode at Carp's Rest to recover after restoring the spirit veins; Lingyuan, who presides over the vale, accepted the rite.

29.comment: Chenyu Vale: Southern Mountain: Lingshu Courtyard and the Herblord
29.content: Lingshu Courtyard is the abode of the Herblord, a white snake adeptus who took human shape, made medicines and healed the sick. It lies in a cave off Yaodie Valley, the valley of vibrant butterflies. A talking Carefree Simulacrum there guards the place from intruders and, in the quest, asks the Traveler to return the scattered butterflies to the medicine jar so the withered adeptal tree might revive. It says the Herblord left when she lost the power to keep her human form. The wiki identifies her now as Changsheng, the snake who accompanies Baizhu.

30.comment: Chenyu Vale: Southern Mountain: Chizhang and the mistress of Chenyu Vale
30.content: Chizhang was the ancient city governed by the mistress of Chenyu Vale, an unnamed goddess of the vale's animals and spirits who was not evil according to Fujin and made many dreams come true. When the Archon War began she grew obsessed with becoming an Archon and with survival, and she ceased granting dreams. In a last attempt to defeat Morax she planned to raise the Bishui and flood out the Guili Assembly, which would have destroyed her own vale; her adepti rebelled and she was sealed. Chizhang Wall now holds a shrine style also seen at Cuijue Slope.

31.comment: Chenyu Vale: Southern Mountain: Teatree Slope and the first tea tree
31.content: Teatree Slope is south of Qiaoying Village and was part of the Herblord's lands. Fujin was the first to plant a tea tree in Chenyu Vale, in the Herblord's territory, and the slope is named for it; when it was a sapling someone tied a jade ornament to it. The Jade Leaf tea set text says this variety only grows well here because it remembers a promise between two friends.

32.content:
Chenyu Vale: Upper Vale (also: Upper Vale, Chenyu Upper Vale): The Upper Vale is the northern half of Chenyu Vale, the misty tea-growing valley in northwestern Liyue that borders Fontaine. Its river, the Bishui, runs from the busy border port of Yilong Wharf past Qiaoying Village, famous for its tea, and under the giant jade rings of Jademouth. It was added in version 4.4. Its peaks Mt. Lingmeng and Mt. Mingyuan frame the valley, and a hidden cavern, Chenlong Cleft, lies beneath the river.

The land is blessed by adepti and shaped by an old goddess's war; the tea, the jade ornaments and the river rites all trace back to that history.

Geography: Mountains, rivers and fog. Yilong Wharf is southeast of Lumidouce Harbor across the Fontaine border, and the Bishui runs from it through the vale past Qiaoying Village. Mt. Lingmeng lies west of Qiaoying Village and southeast of Yilong Wharf; Mt. Mingyuan lies west of Yilong Wharf and east of Fontaine.

Places: Yilong Wharf is a prosperous commercial port with upper and lower levels. Qiaoying Village is the tea village with the Chunming Teaworks and a special roasting cauldron. Jademouth is a set of massive jade pieces flanking the Bishui. Mt. Lingmeng and Mt. Mingyuan are the surrounding peaks.

Culture: Tea is the vale's identity. People believe the adepti blessed the land and water; the village holds an annual tea-serving ceremony using the wilted petals of Spiritscent Flowers. Yilong Wharf residents hold ceremonies to worship ancestors and the dead and once threw jade into the water.

History: In ancient times the vale was ruled by an unnamed goddess, the mistress of Chenyu Vale, served by three adepti: the snake Herblord, the carp Fujin and the suanni Lingyuan. Fujin planted the first tea tree and taught early settlers rituals. In the Archon War the goddess tried to drown Morax with a flood down the Bishui; her three adepti rebelled, Fujin hurled the Votive Rainjade into the river, and Jademouth formed.

Travel: The Bishui River links Qiaoying Village and Yilong Wharf and has well-developed waterborne transport; Yilong Wharf is the port for Fontaine. Adeptal energy from Fujin lets travelers use special mechanics such as Golden Carp's Leap.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Upper Vale is peaceful and prosperous, with the tea restored.

Fujin spent her strength on the rite and reverted to her carp form to recover; Lingyuan agreed to it. Some miasma remains. No 6.x-7.1 upheaval here is recorded.

33.comment: Chenyu Vale: Upper Vale: Qiaoying Village and its tea
33.content: Qiaoying Village in northwestern Liyue is famous across Teyvat for its tea, sold in Liyue Harbor and exported; Fontaine imports it through Lumidouce Harbor. A special cauldron, said to be an adeptal mechanism, roasts the leaves. Much tea is planted around the village. People believe the adepti blessed the land and water. A yearly tea-serving ceremony uses Spiritscent Flower petals. In the 4.4 quests, tea quality drops because Lingyuan has tainted the spirit veins; Grandpa Lu blames soil and water, Uncle Luo blames the machine, and the Traveler restores the tea with Fujin.

34.comment: Chenyu Vale: Upper Vale: Yilong Wharf
34.content: Yilong Wharf, also Yilong Port, is a busy trade port across the sea from Fontaine, southeast of Lumidouce Harbor, where Fontainians can sample Liyue culture without going to Liyue Harbor. The wharf has a watchtower and boats up the Bishui. Locals worship ancestors and the dead there and once tossed jade into the water; scholars dispute whether the name means 'jade left behind' or a miscopied 'dragon remnants.'

35.comment: Chenyu Vale: Upper Vale: Jademouth and the Votive Rainjade
35.content: Jademouth is a set of massive jade pieces flanking the Bishui; Little Mao calls it a great jade ring. Legend says an adeptus cast it down to protect people from floods. In the quest account, the goddess of the vale tried to flood the river against Morax; her adepti Fujin climbed Mt. Lingmeng and threw the Votive Rainjade into the water, pinning the river down, and the Herblord fought the goddess while Lingyuan sheltered the people. Chenlong Cleft lies in the cavern under the whirlpool.

36.content:
Chihu Rock: Chihu Rock is the busy, ordinary side of Liyue Harbor: a district on an island at the city's southeast, joined by bridges to Feiyun Slope on the north and to Mt. Tianheng on the west. Its main plaza, main street and docks are where street food sellers, miners, sailors, dockworkers and storytellers go about their day, and where an adventurer finds the Adventurers' Guild and Wanmin Restaurant.

The wiki's location text calls it the harbor's lower-class district, while the in-game viewpoint text treats it as the pulsing heart of the city, the lively scene from which Liyue Harbor draws its energy. The name is Chihu in pinyin, which literally reads as "Eating-Tiger Rock"; no source explains why.

Geography: Chihu Rock sits on an island to the southeast of the rest of the harbor. A bridge runs north to Feiyun Slope (the merchant district) and another west toward Mt. Tianheng. Inside the district the layout is a main plaza, a main street climbing from it, a side alley, a dockyard and the harbor wharves where ships tie up.

Places: - Main plaza: street food stalls, a toy seller, Dongsheng's general goods shop Second Life and Shitou's Jade Mystery; miners and a Blackcliff Forge shift supervisor are seen here in the day.
- Main street: the Adventurers' Guild branch, Wanmin Restaurant, Hanfeng's Ironmongers and Yanshang Teahouse nearby.
- Third-Round Knockout: a storytelling tavern.
- Dockyard and harbor: laborers, a warehouse manager, boatmen, sailors and fishmongers.

People: Chef Mao and Xiangling at Wanmin Restaurant; Katheryne and the branch master Lan at the Adventurers' Guild; Dongsheng at Second Life; Shitou of Jade Mystery; Master Zhang the blacksmith; Chuyi, hostess of Yanshang Teahouse; Degui, who owns Third-Round Knockout, and its storyteller Iron Tongue Tian. Millelith soldiers patrol the streets and docks.

Culture: Chihu Rock runs on food, gossip and trade. Locals eat from stalls, drink at Third-Round Knockout, trade stories in the plaza and bargain at the shops. The storyteller at Third-Round Knockout is a draw; Zhongli is found listening there in several quests.

Atmosphere: Noise, cooking smells, sea air and bargaining, with a mix of locals and travellers. It feels crowded and cheerful rather than refined, a sharp contrast with the high terraces of Yujing Terrace.

Travel: Reached from Feiyun Slope by bridge, or from Mt. Tianheng on the west side. Ships dock along the wharves.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Chihu Rock is a bustling everyday district of Liyue Harbor with no recorded change from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

Shenhe now works as a server at Wanmin Restaurant, referred by Ganyu, and Xianyun, who is the adeptus Cloud Retainer, lives in the city in human form. Yelan runs Yanshang Teahouse from behind the scenes.

37.content: Wanmin Restaurant is a famous restaurant in Chihu Rock, owned by Chef Mao and worked by his daughter Xiangling as head chef. It sells simple, popular Liyue food, ingredients and recipes. Ningguang has financed it, and Shenhe waits tables there after Ganyu referred her. Xianyun is a regular, sitting with Guoba while she waits for her noodles.

38.content: A casino disguised as a teahouse selling only high-grade tea and other goods. Under its original owner, who admitted only wealthy patrons, the hostess Chuyi was curt and unwelcoming and two security guards stood by the door. Childe exposed the owner's fraud over a debt to the Northland Bank and took his Sigil of Permission; after Osial's defeat Yelan took over. She is notorious among its patrons for her gambling skill, and Chuyi is less abrupt under her management.

39.content: A tavern owned by Degui, with the waitress Zhiruo and the storyteller Iron Tongue Tian. Fishmongers Uncle Gao and Uncle Sun drink here at night. Zhongli seems to favour it. The wiki notes the Chinese name is likely an allusion to a classic novel's tavern with very strong wine.

40.content:
Chiwang Terrace (also: Chiwang Terrace (Quest Domain), Chìwàng-tái, Chiwang Peak): Chiwang Terrace is an ancient terrace of ritual on Mt. Laixin, the sacred mountain of Chenyu Vale in southern Liyue, where the vale's spirit veins meet. It is above the clouds and open to the sky, and it is where the old people of the vale were said to speak with the heavens. It became central when the adeptus Fujin and the Traveler stopped her old friend Lingyuan from rewriting the spirit veins there.

Its design matches an altar remembered from the lost civilisation of Lang-Gan, which suggests the terrace is a keepsake of that people, who fled the Chasm and settled in Chenyu Vale. It is known to the wider world only through the vale's local lore and a few adepti.

Geography: The terrace stands on Mt. Laixin, called "the sacred mountain" because the spirit veins of Chenyu Vale converge there; whoever controls the mountain can reshape the land of the whole vale. In the world quest it is a separate quest domain reached by a ritual gate, with the sky and cloud sea around it. Nearby are the cave shelters and murals of Chizhang Wall, and the Votive Rainjade at Carp's Rest, whose offerings are unlocked through a follow-up quest.

History: Lan Yan, whose family comes from Chenyu Vale, says the vale's ancient people used the terrace to commune with the heavens. The wiki ties it to the Lang-Gan altar where Zibai was honoured; see the uncertainties on whether it is a copy or the original. After the Chasm was created by a Celestial Nail, the refugees of Lang-Gan carried their traditions to Chenyu Vale, where later adepti such as Fujin taught the Rainjade Rite of jade offerings.

Quests: "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade" (4.4), the third quest of "Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade", unlocks the terrace. It is also mentioned in Act I of "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon".

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lingyuan has promised not to hinder Fujin's work, the spirit veins are calm, and the terrace is a quiet relic of older rites.

Fujin remains in carp form. Remaining miasma in Chenyu Vale is a separate problem for visitors.

41.comment: Chiwang Terrace: Chiwang Terrace and the Lang-Gan altar
41.content: Chenyu Vale tradition says the ancient people communed with the heavens at Chiwang Terrace. The wiki and the 6.3 event link it to the jade altar of Lang-Gan, where lanterns and offerings were presented to the Three Moons and to Zibai. Whether the terrace is a rebuilt copy or the original altar carried from the Chasm is left open by canon. The event happened during Lantern Rite 2026.

42.content:
Chizhang Wall (also: Chizhang, Chìzhāng Chéngyuán, Ancient City of Chizhang, Huangcong Grounds): Chizhang Wall is a stretch of ruined rampart and cave shelters in southern Chenyu Vale, north of Mt. Xuanlian. The wiki names it the remains of the ancient city of Chizhang, governed by the Mistress of Chenyu Vale. Painted murals and scattered "Records of the Ancestors" tell of villagers saved by a great adeptus, of jade offerings made at Chiwang, and of a people who once left the Chasm.

A Solitary Suanni now haunts the ground. The place matters mostly as an archive: what survives on its walls is the best surviving picture of the vale's ancient people.

Geography: Chizhang Wall lies in the Southern Mountain part of Chenyu Vale, north of Mt. Xuanlian. It is broken stone wall, ruined foundations and a set of cave shelters in the hillside, some with painted murals. A Solitary Suanni is the area's only notable enemy.

History: Fujin says the caves were shelters built by the adepti during the Archon War, so ordinary people caught between floods and fighting would have a safe place. The murals show the people of the vale with their adepti and with the Votive Rainjade rite.

Dangers: A Solitary Suanni patrols the area; the sealed mural cave opens only through the jade mechanism.

Quests: Fujin shows the Traveler these murals in "An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade" (4.4), before they move on toward Chiwang Terrace.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 an abandoned, silent ruin with preserved murals and no inhabitants.

43.content:
Chunming Teaworks: The Chunming Teaworks is the tea workshop of Qiaoying Village in Chenyu Vale. Most of the village's picked tea leaves are sent here to be processed, and its map description says its reputation reaches far beyond the village.

It is run by the veteran Ding Sr. with the younger Ding Jr., and it blends age-old methods with newer machines for drying leaves and roasting tea.

Practice: Fresh leaves need several careful steps before they can become tea. According to Ding Sr., the workshop handles sunning, baking and stirring the leaves in a pan to drive off excess moisture, which deepens the fragrance and makes the tea easier to store. Some varieties are then taken back by the farmers for further work such as piling and fermenting.

People: Ding Sr. is the experienced overseer; Ding Jr. is his junior in the craft. Both are ordinary villagers with no established family or story beyond the workshop.

Status as of 7.1: A working workshop as of 7.1.

Its map description credits it as perhaps the reason Qiaoying Village's tea is so famous.

44.content: Scene use: a visitor is greeted as a would-be tour guest; Ding Sr. gladly explains each step of the processing and is protective of the leaves. The machine room contrasts with the village's traditional image.

45.content:
Cinnabar Cliff: Cinnabar Cliff is a surface subarea of the Chasm in Liyue. It is called a tourist spot, though locals reportedly never go there, and it holds a Statue of The Seven, a Geo Elemental Monument and hostile Fatui Skirmishers.

A quest domain from the Archon Quests, the Unknown Sanctuary, is placed here on the map even though it belongs to Sumeru's story. A self-styled hero called Tang Wuchou, who is really a Treasure Hoarder, stands here.

Geography: Features are a Statue of The Seven, a Geo Elemental Monument, Geograna, Spoutrocks, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars. Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass grow here.

People: Tang Wuchou, a Treasure Hoarder, is found here in the open world; the wiki gives him the self-proclaimed title Guhua Hero, with a question mark, and an idle line imagines a garden of Glaze Lilies. After the world quest The Missing Miner, the miner Uncle He can be found here too.

Quests: The Unknown Sanctuary is a quest domain used in the Archon Quests "A Lamenter at Fate's End" and "Portended Fate". Its description says hilichurls were seen heading there, faithful and unwavering, and a companion tells the Traveler he has never seen anything like it. The domain's enemies are hilichurls and slimes of several elements.

Dangers: A Blazing Axe Mitachurl is the elite enemy. Common foes are Fatui Skirmishers (Geochanter Bracers, Anemoboxer Vanguards and Electrohammer Vanguards), Rock Shield Hilichurl Guards and Geo Slimes.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

46.content:
Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern: Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern is a Domain of Blessing north of Mt. Aocang in Liyue: an ancient altar in a hidden stone cave where monsters that fear Geo guard Artifacts. Its in-game text says Mt. Aocang looks like pretty scenery but hides a cave "connecting to the heavens" that breathes out clouds.

Inside, the ley lines are tuned to Geo. Every party member deals extra Geo damage, and the three trials are all called "Stone Chamber". The enemies are Treasure Hoarders, rock-shield hilichurls and mitachurls, and finally a Ruin Guard.

Geography: The entrance is on the northern side of Mt. Aocang, in the Minlin area of Liyue. Mt. Aocang is the mountain where the adeptus Cloud Retainer (Xianyun) lived in seclusion after the Archon War. Outside the cave, nearby, a ruins treasure with a pillar of light tells the story of a disciple who received a Vision and is linked to a similar one at Guyun Stone Forest.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: the ley line disorder gives all party members +75% Geo damage across the three trials; levels II and III also grant a Geo DMG bonus. Recommended element is Geo. Stage one has Treasure Hoarder Crushers and Pugilists, stage two has Rock Shield Hilichurl Guards and Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls, and stage three a single Ruin Guard.

Atmosphere: Cool, damp stone, still pools, thin clouds drifting through cave openings, and the hum of Geo energy in the walls.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

47.comment: Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern: Mt. Aocang and the Cloud Retainer
47.content: Mt. Aocang is a mountain in Liyue's Minlin region, remembered as the retreat of the adeptus Cloud Retainer after the Archon War and until the events of "A Thousand Moonlit Miles". The domain lies to its north and is not described as belonging to her.

key: Abode of Retaining the Clouds by Borrowing the Wind
48.content:
Cloud Retainer's Abode (also: Abode of Cloud Retainer, Abode of Retaining the Clouds by Borrowing the Wind): Cloud Retainer's Abode is the hidden home of the adeptus Cloud Retainer (later called Xianyun) at the top of Mt. Aocang in Liyue. It is a space of rotating platforms, bridges, wind currents and elemental mechanisms that she says she built and designed herself, and visitors reach it only by laying out a food offering.

It appears twice: in the Archon Quest Custodian of Clouds (Version 1.0), where the Traveler and Paimon come to tell her of the death of Rex Lapis, and in the world quest An Adeptal Summons, where she sends them to fetch her old blueprints. Outside those quests the entrance only notes that the adeptus does not want guests.

Geography: The abode lies at the top of Mt. Aocang in the Minlin area of Liyue. Visitors find a barrier the Traveler cannot pass at first, a pond with a round stone table at its centre, and a door that opens once an offering has been accepted.

Places: Notable spots are the stone table in the middle of Mt. Aocang's pond, the abode's door, the moving platforms and the final archway.

People: The occupant is the adeptus Cloud Retainer, whose human-form name is Xianyun. She is a crane adeptus who values quiet, mechanical invention and good food, and deals with mortals strictly on her own terms. Her disciple Shenhe is listed by the wiki as affiliated with the abode.

History: Xianyun's profile and the Mt. Aocang page place her isolation on the mountain after the Archon War and until A Thousand Moonlit Miles. She says she built the abode herself.

Culture: Offerings are the key. A dish laid at the table earns a hearing; in the world quest a single dish buys only a short audience. The recipes the Traveler finds by the pots are Jewelry Soup, Matsutake Meat Rolls and Mora Meat.

Atmosphere: A calm mountain pond under thin cloud, a laid table with nobody at it, and a closed door; inside, creaking mechanisms, drifting platforms and sudden wind currents, all under the eye of an unseen and faintly irritable adeptus.

Dangers: The main hazard is falling into the void and the occupant's temper, not guards. Slimes and a few hilichurls patrol the platforms. Failing the timed challenge in An Adeptal Summons, or falling off, sends the party out of the domain.

Travel: Climb Mt. Aocang to the pond and table, offer food, and enter through the abode's door. Outside the two quests the domain cannot be entered.

Quests: Custodian of Clouds (Archon Quest, Chapter I Act I, Version 1.0) and An Adeptal Summons (world quest, requires Farewell, Archaic Lord). Xianyun's A Thousand Moonlit Miles (4.4) opens at Mt. Aocang.

Status as of 7.1: As of Version 7.1 the abode is available only as a quest domain, and Xianyun lives in Liyue Harbor. Mt. Aocang is still used by the adepti in later content: Zhongli, Xianyun, Madame Ping, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver gather there at a Lantern Rite, and seal it off during a later quest.

49.content: Cloud Retainer is the adeptus name of Xianyun, a crane adeptus who built the abode on Mt. Aocang. She prizes mechanical invention, her privacy and food offerings. Her own entry holds her biography; this one covers only her home.

50.comment: Cloud Retainer's Abode: Mt. Aocang offerings
50.content: Visitors to the pond at Mt. Aocang earn an audience with Cloud Retainer by cooking the dishes whose recipes lie by the nearby pots. Pilgrims who once came to be disciples were told to bring ninety-nine different Qingxin dishes over ninety-nine days.

51.content:
Cuijue Slope: Cuijue Slope is a stark hillside in Minlin, Liyue, ringed by nine tall stone pillars around a central temple. Walking near them turns the sky dim and grey. Local lore offers almost nothing about them beyond a tablet saying they were raised to hold nine human desires at bay, so that war would never return, and that whoever breaks them should take the treasure inside and protect Liyue.

Opening the pillars needs Stones of Remembrance, which the player gets by making offerings at Liyue's Statues of the Seven. The treasure chamber's chief prize is a very old ring.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin. The Nine Pillars of Peace stand in a valley with a temple at the centre. Near the pillars the sky turns dark and grey and the land outside the slope takes on an unnaturally dim look, an effect that fades with distance. From the slope, Dragonspine and Wangshu Inn can be seen in the distance.

Places: The Nine Pillars of Peace (a point of interest in their own right) and the ruined temple at their centre.

History: The tablet at the centre states the purpose in the builders' own voice. All turmoil comes from human vice; nine pillars are raised to suppress conflict so that armies are never again raised against each other. Inside the temple a second inscription names the nine desires: greed, nostalgia, vision, jealousy, anger, lust, self-aggrandizement, competition and turmoil. They can "heal the world, or do it great hurt," and the pillars are laid down to end the conflicts that plague it. A warning follows: if a later visitor breaks the pillars and enters, war will consume the world again, so any reader who does so should take the treasure and bring peace to Liyue.

Dangers: Ordinary hilichurls, Fatui skirmishers, Treasure Hoarders and Abyss mages roam the slope. Inside the temple the Traveler faces an inactive Ruin Guard that wakes when approached, plus Geovishap Hatchlings and a Ruin Hunter in waves.

Quests: Nine Pillars of Peace (World Quest, available once the Prologue's first act is done). The player sets nine Stones of Remembrance, wins the chamber's prize and then chooses whom to sell the Dull Ring to, Bolai or Linlang, both in Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the slope is unchanged and still open to exploration. No later story content was found that alters it.

52.comment: Cuijue Slope: Nine Pillars of Peace
52.content: The pillars are a sealed monument whose builders meant them as a lock on human conflict. Breaking one by inlaying a Stone of Remembrance cracks the mask on its face and breaks away a section to reveal glowing geometry beneath. The temple's chamber holds the treasure and the Dull Ring. The inscriptions treat the pillars as a deliberate gamble: a peace maintained by sealing away what could end it.

53.content:
Dihua Marsh (also: Marsh of Rustling Reeds): Dihua Marsh is a wetland of rivers and silvergrass shaped by the Bishui River in Bishui Plain, Liyue, between the Stone Gate to the north and Wangshu Inn to the south. It lies on the main road between Mondstadt and Liyue, so merchant caravans stop and rest here. A Statue of the Seven stands at its northern end.

The name comes from the silvergrass (dihua) that grows in the shallows. The marsh is also remembered as the final resting place of many wandering fighters.

Geography: An alluvial plain made by the Bishui River, with a web of rivers supporting a wide ecosystem of plants and animals. Stone Gate lies to the north, Wangshu Inn to the south and Sal Terrae to the east. A waterfall in the northwest is well known to travelers, and the marsh sits near Mt. Qingce. The area's local specialty is Cor Lapis.

Places: The Statue of the Seven on the northern end, along the main road, and Wangshu Inn, a tall inn that the official description calls a symbolic structure visible from all directions.

People: Open-world residents include the Millelith soldier Qiaoxi and several travelers and merchants, among them Hui, Hulu, Mengmeng, Strong and Yu.

Travel: The marsh is the road from Mondstadt into Liyue, so caravans rest in its shallows and at the inn rather than push on into the hills. Official text describes the setting as awe-inspiring to newcomers.

Dangers: Hilichurl camps (fighters, shooters, grenadiers, Anemo samachurls), a Cryo Whopperflower and a Cryo Abyss Mage.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the marsh is unchanged and remains a rest stop on the road between Mondstadt and Liyue. No later story content was found that alters it.

54.comment: Dihua Marsh: Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh
54.content: Wangshu Inn stands within Dihua Marsh, built tall for visibility. Zhongli calls it a strategic location that must be defended, and the inn has existed since at least the years after the Cataclysm, nearly 500 years ago. Seen from the top, it reaches all the way to Mt. Qingce and Jueyun Karst in clear weather. Its fuller history belongs to its own entry.

55.content:
Domain of Guyun: The Domain of Guyun is an Electro-themed Domain of Blessing on the largest island in Guyun Stone Forest, in Liyue's Sea of Clouds. Ancient ley line altars here guard Artifacts behind rounds of slime and Abyss enemies. Its description speaks of delusions and disappointments of an ancient ambition to lead humanity, gathered in the caverns under Guyun.

It has six levels, with ley line disorder built around Electro-Charged, Overloaded and Superconduct reactions. The level names are all "Spring", the translation of Jingzhe, the season when thunder wakes the sleeping insects.

Geography: The domain lies on the largest of the seven islands in Guyun Stone Forest. The northernmost island houses the Geo Hypostasis.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: ley line disorder boosts Electro-Charged damage by 150% with 100% larger area at levels I and IV, and makes Overloaded (II, V) or Superconduct (III, VI) trigger an Energy Blast that damages nearby opponents. Recommended element is Electro; Cryo helps at level VI.

Atmosphere: Thin air, low clouds, crackling static, and sheer stone pillars; the altar's walls feel old and a little bitter.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

56.comment: Domain of Guyun: Osial and the Guyun legend
56.content: Legend places Rex Lapis' defeat of the god-and-sea-monster Osial at Guyun Stone Forest, with the cliffs as remnants of his stone lances. Roald's diary suggests that anyone who spends a night there may experience Osial's memories of that defeat.

key: the nameless fishing village near Wangshu Inn
57.content:
Downriver (also: Downriver village, Xiàchuān, the nameless fishing village near Wangshu Inn): Downriver is an abandoned fishing village in Minlin, Liyue, a little west of Wangshu Inn. Its remaining houses are empty and falling apart. The village matters in canon as the place that took in the orphaned Beidou as a small child and later drove her out, long before she became captain of the Crux.

It is a Point of Interest rather than a settlement anyone lives in. Its name was first spoken in Beidou's hangout quest "Life on the High Seas" (the story event "When the Crux Shines Bright"); before that, the place appeared on the map and through two signboard messages left by former residents.

Geography: In Minlin, west of Wangshu Inn and visible from the inn. A scatter of old, weathered fishing houses; the village chief's former house is the best-known of them.

History: Fishing families moved here from an older village called Upriver, bringing generations of fishing know-how. Beidou arrived as a homeless child of about five or six and was taken in by the village chief. Roughly a year or two later the chief died of illness during winter, the catch and harvest shrank, and the villagers blamed her and drove her out. Over time everyone else left too.

The name Downriver came from this link to Upriver; Beidou says Upriver is long gone and that soon nobody may remember either name. In her telling, the village was never impressive but was lively and home to several families, and she learned a lot about fishing from them.

Her account of her arrival: she had been wandering the streets, found half a Rice Bun and was robbed of it by a stray dog, and chased it into this neighbourhood. Fishermen who saw her stop her and fed her. The dog collapsed and did not get up again, with the bun still in its mouth. The villagers were wary of the dirty child, but the chief took pity on her and brought her to their home.

Atmosphere: Silent and sun-bleached: sagging roofs, empty doorways, water close by and no voices. Beidou calls it a place that has "certainly seen better days".

Places: Two signboards are the only written traces of the villagers. One, addressed "To Zhong", says fishing has grown harder, sales have dropped, and the villagers have decided to leave as a group and look for work elsewhere. Another message, also to Zhong, complains that the writer's letters were never answered and says the girl has left some things for Zhong in the usual place, by the main house.

Dangers: Nothing specific in canon beyond decay. Treat it as a quiet, safe, melancholy stop on the road near Wangshu Inn.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Downriver is still empty and crumbling. No later event is recorded there.

58.content: Beidou, captain of the Crux, was a homeless child of about five or six when she was taken in at Downriver by the village chief. After the chief died and the fish dwindled, the villagers blamed her and drove her out, using the saying that Nandou controls life and Beidou death. She revisits the ruined village with the Traveler in "Life on the High Seas".

59.content:
Dragon-Queller (also: Hidden Dragon Tree): The Dragon-Queller is a huge tree with glowing blue veins standing near Mt. Hulao at Nantianmen in Liyue. It is the seal that holds the Geo dragon Azhdaha, whom Morax and the adepti imprisoned there long ago after his erosion made him a danger to people. The developers describe the tree as Azhdaha's own tail.

Geography: The tree rises beside Mt. Hulao in the Nantianmen area of Liyue's Minlin region. Its branches carry a cold, moonlight-coloured glow, and one great blue branch at its tip points straight toward Liyue Harbor and cannot be climbed. Bright yellow flowers grow around its base; the same flowers are found in the lair of the Primo Geovishap. Its roots reach deep into the earth and, according to the dragon's own account, connect to the ley lines. A tunnel beneath it leads to the dragon's prison, which is entered as a domain.

Places: Stone Monolith: a tablet set before the tree by the adeptus Mountain Shaper as a warning to passers-by. Its text, paraphrased, thanks the merciful adepti for life enduring in Heaven and Earth and states that an evil dragon lies here and must not be disturbed.

Beneath the Dragon-Queller: the prison itself, reached through the tunnel under the tree. Players fight Azhdaha there as a weekly boss; the story treats the fight as a memory of the encounter, because Azhdaha was re-sealed.

History: Azhdaha, an ancient earth dragon born of elemental crystallisation, once befriended Morax and humanity. Erosion made him forget Morax and lash out, and miners damaging the ley lines of the Chasm worsened his suffering. Morax and the adepti Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and a third, unnamed adeptus fought him in a battle that began in the Chasm and ran north to Nantianmen, where, with the willing acceptance of his remaining conscience, they sealed the eroded dragon in the Dragon-Queller. The clash of elemental energy in that battle also created Dragonfall.

Atmosphere: A still, cold place. The tree glows with a moonlit light, the earth around it feels thick with held-back power, and the monolith's plain warning is the only human sign. During the miners' disappearance, Geovishaps and other creatures nearby were unusually aggressive.

Dangers: The seal itself is the danger: if it breaks, Azhdaha can draw on the ley lines again and attack Liyue.

Travel: The tree stands in the Nantianmen area near Mt. Hulao, on the way toward Lingju Pass, and its tip branch points at Liyue Harbor.

Quests: No Mere Stone (Zhongli Story Quest, 1.5), whose final part is Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved, is the main source. The domain unlocks on its completion.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the dragon remains resealed after the events of 1.5. No later content found in this research changes the seal's state.

60.content: The Dragon-Queller is the blue-veined tree beside Mt. Hulao at Nantianmen that seals the crazed Geo dragon Azhdaha. A Mountain Shaper tablet at its foot warns people not to disturb the evil dragon beneath.

61.content: The prison chamber under the Dragon-Queller, entered by a tunnel at the tree. It is a bed of rock carved into the heart of the world. The Trounce Domain relives Azhdaha's fight as a memory; in the story he has been resealed.

62.comment: Dragon-Queller: Azhdaha at the Moonchase Festival
62.content: During a flashback in the Moonchase Festival event, Azhdaha is shown gazing at the night sky with Marchosius riding on his shoulder. This is limited-time event content and does not show the Dragon-Queller.

63.content:
Dunyu Ruins (also: Dùnyù-líng, Fleeing Jade Mausoleum): The Dunyu Ruins are old ruins sunk in a dead lake in Lisha, a region of Liyue. They are hilltop terraces, stairways and a Statue of the Seven's camp, with a Geo totem that drains the lake, and one of three places where the quest item "Nameless Treasure" is hidden. Little is known of who built them.

A Treasure Hoarder's notes suggest the ruins are tied to adepti who died in an ancient war, but this is not confirmed.

Geography: Ruins on terraces around a lake in Lisha. Walls, stairs, Ruins Torches and rock piles are scattered between buildings. Activating the Geo totem after lighting torches drains the lake to reveal the Geoculus, a barrier guarded by three Seelie courts, and a chest with a Nameless Treasure. The expedition description says the ruins are suspended in time inside the dead lake.

People: The astronomer Ziwei and the miner Iron Ingot are the named NPCs here. Treasure Hoarders and the Fatui roam the ruins.

History: Little is certain. The Treasure Hoarder Liuliu wrote in a Ruins Investigation Log that research suggested the ruins are linked to adepti who fought and died in an ancient war and that "treasure is hidden within the rocks, concealed beneath the waters". Liuliu also heard mournful groans at night, put down to the north wind blowing past Nantianmen.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers (Pyroslinger Bracer, Cryogunner and Hydrogunner Legionnaires, Anemoboxer and Electrohammer Vanguards), Treasure Hoarders, slimes, and elite Ruin Guards and Fatui Pyro Agents.

Quests: "Hidden in Nameless Treasures", a Hidden Exploration Objective whose items come from Lingju Pass, Qingxu Pool and these ruins.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins are a minor exploration site with no developing story.

64.content:
Dwelling in the Clouds (also: Jadevoid): The Dwelling in the Clouds is a small floating island high above Qingyun Peak in Minlin, Liyue, built on a foundation of Plaustrite. It was made by the adeptus Cloud Retainer as a private place to meditate, and is reached by solving the Three Cranes Puzzle on the peak below.

Its memorial text, written in Cloud Retainer's voice, says it was meant as a sanctuary away from the world; the adepti later took it over to seek ultimate truth in seclusion and, with Taishan Mansion sealed, returned it to her.

Lore: Cloud Retainer built it long ago for meditation and reflection. Other adepti, with Rex Lapis' approval, later persuaded her to offer it as the site of the trial of "heaven" for those seeking the adepti's path, and she added a small pavilion. Its Plaustrite foundation and the trial of crossing the void to follow that path gave it the name "Jadevoid", a name that came to cover all places where the adepti reside.

Travel: The island is unlocked by the Three Cranes Puzzle on Qingyun Peak, whose monument speaks of the one who may ascend kowtowing atop three mountains and of auspicious signs sent by three divine birds. Qingyun Peak is also home to the adeptus Moon Carver.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is a quiet retreat held by Cloud Retainer; no later events have changed it.

65.content:
Emerald Maple Inn: The Emerald Maple Inn stands west of the Statue of The Seven and overlooks Luhua Pool, in the Sea of Clouds area of Liyue. Its owner, Mr. Zhu, struggles to attract customers because of its remote location.

Mona used to be a regular before moving to Mondstadt, because the prices were low.

People: Mr. Zhu is the innkeeper and sells simple dishes and tea. He greets visitors warmly but is quickly drawn into complaining that he picked a bad spot: it lies between the Wangshu Inn and Liyue Harbor, so travellers from the north stop at the Wangshu Inn, while those coming from the south typically arrive only after drinking heavily in the Harbor. He says he wishes he had listened to his father and stayed home.

Status as of 7.1: Still open as of 7.1, as quiet as ever.

66.comment: Emerald Maple Inn: Mr. Zhu's luck
66.content: Mr. Zhu's running joke is that opening an inn here was a terrible idea. Play him as courteous but resigned, hopeful for any guest, and prone to a sigh when asked about business.

67.content:
Fanmu Carpenter (also: Fanmu Carpenter's): Fanmu Carpenter is a carpentry workshop in Qingce Village, owned by Master Lu. In the game he sells blueprints for furnishings.

He calls it one of the oldest carpentry workshops in the village. Its Chinese name is read Fanmu-tang.

History: By Master Lu's account the workshop began as the property of his grandfather's grandfather and has stayed in the family ever since. He says it built the residence of Chang the Ninth and the village mill, and that even the Qixing come to it when they need furniture made to order.

People: Master Lu is genial, proud of the family trade, and boasts that he can build anything from a yo-yo to a house. Dayu is the younger carpenter in his orbit.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

68.comment: Fanmu Carpenter: Master Lu and the apprenticeship
68.content: Master Lu wants an apprentice. He is warm and weary, speaks fondly of the family workshop, and will say anyone may come back and take up the craft if he is still around.

69.content:
Feiyun Slope: Feiyun Slope is Liyue Harbor's prosperous merchant district and the way into the city for anyone arriving by the main road from the north. It sits between Chihu Rock to the southeast and Yujing Terrace to the west, and climbs in tiers of boulevard, bookshops, teahouses and bank offices. Wealthy merchants, guild servants, clerks of the Ministry of Civil Affairs and foreign traders all do business here.

The in-game viewpoint text describes it as where merchants who have "made it" live in comfort and carefree prosperity, with lights that never go out. The Ministry of Civil Affairs, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Snezhnayan Northland Bank all have premises on the slope.

Geography: Feiyun Slope is the centre of Liyue Harbor, connecting the other two districts. Visitors from the north road arrive through its entrance; from there a boulevard rises in levels. The northern wharf, with a Maritime Authority office, is at the lower edge, and the Northland Bank and Heyu Tea House are on the top level.

Places: - Entrance: Baiju Guesthouse, Xigu Antiques, peddlers and the ship owner Bibo.
- Boulevard: Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk (two eateries), Mingxing Jewelry, shops and the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.
- Ministry of Civil Affairs: the city's civil administration.
- Wanwen Bookhouse (middle level), Northland Bank and Heyu Tea House (top level).

People: Merchants such as Changshun and Bolai; shopkeepers Linlang and Xingxi; Jifang; Fan Er'ye; the fortune teller Qiming (at night); the undertaker Ferrylady; the Northland Bank staff; clerks and Millelith soldiers such as Cai Le, Cai Xun and Yicheng; and the foreign merchant Ivanovich.

Governance: The Ministry of Civil Affairs, an organ of the Liyue Qixing, administers the city from here. It watches for dangerous people through lists compiled by Yelan, issues bounties, seals dangerous areas such as the Chasm mines after an accident and organises the Lantern Rite budget and safety.

Culture: Feiyun Slope shows Liyue's trading culture at its most prosperous: guild servants, shop owners, clerks, and foreign merchants, with opera and storytelling at Heyu Tea House and fine meals at Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk.

Atmosphere: Lights that never go out, a steady hum of bargaining and a sense of ease. It feels richer and more orderly than Chihu Rock, with foreign merchants mingling among guild clerks and Millelith.

Travel: The main road from the north ends at the district's entrance. From here a bridge leads to Chihu Rock and a crossroads to Yujing Terrace. A northern wharf with a Maritime Authority office lies along its edge.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Feiyun Slope remains Liyue Harbor's busiest commercial district. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Northland Bank still operates here, and the Qixing still govern through the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Hu Tao runs Wangsheng with Zhongli as consultant.

70.comment: Feiyun Slope: Ministry of Civil Affairs
70.content: A government body under the Liyue Qixing, headquartered in Liyue Harbor and made up of various departments. It handles intelligence and records, public safety on roads, villages and festivals, the Lantern Rite's budget and fireworks, and keeps watch lists that include dangerous individuals, among them the Traveler and some reclusive adepti. Yelan, officially in its employ, is in practice an intelligence agent who works closely with Ningguang. It sealed the Chasm mines after an accident.

71.content: Liyue Harbor's funeral parlor, which also conducts rites for adepti. Hu Tao is its 77th director and Zhongli its consultant; Ferrylady is the undertaker seen on the boulevard at night. The wiki notes that Wangsheng has ties to the Fatui; Childe says it ostensibly does not take on shady work such as assassination. During the Rite of Parting arrangements the Traveler asks Ferrylady where Zhongli has gone.

72.content:
Fengtai General Goods: Fengtai General Goods is the general store of Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale, run by Fengtai. It stocks everyday items and local specialties, and sells commemorative jadeware.
