It is open at all times of the day and its stock restocks at different intervals.

People: Fengtai welcomes customers with a cheerful pitch about everyday items and commemorative jade jewelry. He says there is a build-to-order jadeware service, but it requires a reservation and the time taken depends on the design's complexity. He believes that "you don't choose a piece of jade, it chooses you".

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

73.comment: Fengtai General Goods: Jade carving in Chenyu Vale
73.content: In Chenyu Vale makers and sellers are separate so craftsmen can focus on the work. Fengtai represents the selling side for his master.

key: The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale
74.content:
Fuao Vale (also: Fu'ao Valley, The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale): Fuao Vale is a surface subarea of the Chasm in Liyue. It contains the Lost Valley, a domain on ancient ritual grounds that Ruin Machines have taken over, and a viewpoint whose caption says the site was the battlefield where Rex Lapis fought Azhdaha.

A sign here warns visitors to treat a relic of those old battles, left by Rex Lapis, with care. The valley's Chinese name is usually glossed as Valley of the Prostrate Ao, the Ao being a legendary turtle.

Geography: Features: the Lost Valley domain entrance, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars, a Pressure Plate and a Mountainator blasting cannon. Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass grow here.

History: The Lost Valley's description says the ritual grounds were buried beneath the earth during a cataclysm that tore heaven and earth apart, raised again when an alien object fell, and finally uncovered by a destructive battle that came of a betrayal. Those who once used the place are gone.

Quests: The viewpoint "The Ancient Battlefield of Fuao Vale" appears once the world quest Surreptitious Seven-Star Seal Sundering reaches about step 8.

Dangers: Enemies near the valley include Geo Samachurls, Anemo Slimes and Treasure Hoarder Scouts. Inside the Lost Valley domain, Ruin Machines have overrun the ritual site.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

75.content: The Lost Valley is a Domain of Blessing in Fuao Vale that gives artifacts when cleared. In-world it is described as ancient ritual grounds buried in a cataclysm, lifted by the descent of an alien object, uncovered by the battle after a betrayal and now held by Ruin Machines from outside.

76.content:
Glaze Peak: Glaze Peak is a rocky subarea on the surface of the Chasm in Liyue. Spoutrocks, loose rock piles and tall unique rock pillars mark it, and its slopes hold Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

The Chinese name is Liuli Peak.

Geography: Features are Rock Piles, Seelie, Spoutrocks, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars. Gatherable specialties are Cor Lapis, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

Dangers: A Stonehide Lawachurl is the elite enemy. Dendro Slimes and Treasure Hoarders (Hydro and Pyro Potioneers) roam as common foes.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

77.content:
Golden House (also: Liyue Mint, Teyvat Mint): The Golden House is Liyue's mint, and the only mint in Teyvat. Every Mora coin in circulation was struck here. It stands on Mt. Tianheng above Liyue Harbor. The Liyue Qixing run it, a steward manages it, and Millelith soldiers guard it. Minting needed the Geo Archon's power, so the mint has stood idle since Rex Lapis "died" and gave up his Gnosis. The Mora that already exists stays in circulation.

During the Liyue Archon Quest the Qixing hid Rex Lapis' body, the Exuvia, inside the Golden House. The Fatui Harbinger Childe broke in to take the Gnosis from it, fought the Traveler there and found the body empty.

Places: Inside, the building is even more lavish than its exterior and holds great piles of Mora. It has at least two levels: during the duel in Heart of Glaze, Childe smashed through the floor and the fight continued on the level below. The Exuvia was laid out in the hall where the duel began.

People: Gongming is the steward. She is proud and wary, insists visitors state their business, and calls the place one of paramount importance to Liyue. The guards are Millelith soldiers, among them Youxu, Zexuan, Zhe'yuan and Zheng.

Governance: The mint belongs to the Liyue Qixing's administration. Before the Archon Quest, Gongming noticed that some of her recent orders from the Qixing went far beyond her usual authority. They were part of the measures the Qixing took after Rex Lapis' apparent death: the Exuvia was moved here, and Childe later said the Qixing had stopped the mints.

History: Mora is named after its creator, Morax, known in Liyue as Rex Lapis, and the Golden House struck it with his power. After his body fell at the Rite of Descension, the Qixing secretly moved the Exuvia here. Using what he learned from the preparations for the Rite of Parting, Childe found the hiding place. He knocked out the Millelith guards and was waiting by the body when the Traveler and Paimon arrived. Childe fought the Traveler, reached into the Exuvia and found no Gnosis in it. He assumed the Traveler had taken it, used his Foul Legacy transformation and smashed the fight down to the lower floor. He lost, realised the Exuvia had been a decoy, and left to carry out his backup plan: releasing Osial. Afterwards Zhongli revealed himself as the Geo Archon and gave the Gnosis to Signora for the Tsaritsa. At the Rite of Parting he told Paimon that existing Mora would not vanish, but the Golden House would have to cease operations for a long time.

Economy: In-world, Mora is the currency accepted throughout Teyvat. It is also a catalyst for physical transformation, which is why crafting and forging consume it. Since the Golden House was Teyvat's sole mint, its closure means no new coin enters circulation. Zhongli called this a serious financial problem and, characteristically, left it for the Qixing to debate.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Golden House still stands under guard but does not mint Mora.

The Geo Gnosis went to the Tsaritsa through Signora, and no canon source up to 7.1 shows minting resuming or another way of minting being found.

78.comment: Golden House: The Duel in the Golden House
78.content: Heart of Glaze is part 4 of the Archon Quest act A New Star Approaches (Chapter I, Act III). With Liyue Harbor in turmoil between the Qixing and the adepti, the Traveler realised that Childe had gone to the Golden House after the Exuvia. Inside, the Millelith guards lay unconscious and Childe was waiting by the body. He fought the Traveler for the pleasure of the fight. After reaching into the Exuvia and finding no Gnosis, he unleashed his Foul Legacy transformation, then lost and released the sealed god Osial on Liyue Harbor with mass-produced Sigils of Permission.

key: Plains of the Returning and Departing
79.content:
Guili Plains (also: Plains of Returning and Departing, Plains of the Returning and Departing, Ruins of Guili): The Guili Plains are a stretch of ruins and open country in the Qiongji Estuary area of Liyue. This was the centre of the Guili Assembly, an ancient realm ruled jointly by Guizhong, the God of Dust, and Morax, who is now Rex Lapis and lives incognito as Zhongli. About 3,700 years ago, during the Archon War, a great battle laid it waste and Guizhong died. Morax then led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor. The plains are now a deserted wilderness of broken stone, frequented by hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and the occasional scholar.

The name comes from the two gods: the "Gui" of Guizhong and a "Li" from the name Morax went by at the time. It is read as "the Plains of Returning and Departing." The ruins still hold stone tablets and jade plates inscribed in the Assembly's era, including Guizhong's Four Commandments.

Geography: The plains are a subarea of the Qiongji Estuary, the coastal country north of Mt. Tianheng and Liyue Harbor. The main road between Mondstadt and Liyue Harbor runs past them. To the north lie Wangshu Inn and the Dihua Marsh. The Conch Lodge country of Yaoguang Shoal is on the nearby coast, and Mingyun Village is further east. Violetgrass grows here.

Places: - **Ruins of Guili**: the scattered ruins of the old settlement, with a viewpoint looking over them. Five inscribed stone tablets (north, east, middle-south, southwest and west) and two more ruin inscriptions record the Assembly's founding and fall. Four jade plates in the northern, eastern, southern and western ruins each explain one of Guizhong's Four Commandments.
- **Domain of Forsaken Ruins**: a one-time domain hidden in the area. Its description calls it a cloud-wrapped paradise that one finds only by luck, serene outside and dangerous within.

History: Stone Tablet Compilations: Vol. I, compiled by the historian Zichang from ancient tablets, tells the story. Guizhong, the Lord of Dust, was Rex Lapis' ally and built the Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng. She brought her people north of the mountain and taught them farming, and farming towns spread across the land. She told Rex Lapis that her people had left their home yet felt as though they had returned home. So she named the area the Plains of the Returning and Departing, and he praised her for it. In the Archon War the adepti fought to defend the plains, but the war ravaged them and Guizhong was killed. Rex Lapis then led the people south of Mt. Tianheng for good, and the plains became a wilderness.

Culture: Guizhong's Four Commandments are the plains' lasting legacy: "Teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition." Their convergence was to be called the Guili Assembly. Soraya reads them as Guizhong's wish for her people to be wise, moral, strong and united in protecting their home.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Guili Plains remain uninhabited ruins under Liyue's protection. Nothing of the Assembly survives except stones, inscriptions and memory.

Zhongli still lives in Liyue Harbor, and Guoba, the diminished Stove God Marchosius, lives with Xiangling. In 5.7, Skirk found that god remains sealed beneath the plains had been dug up and taken; Rifthounds were found there collecting remains. No later version reports further change here.

80.content: Guizhong's Four Commandments survive on the stones of the Guili Plains: teach with wisdom, be bound by virtue, fortify the bones, unite in ambition. Their convergence "shall be known as the Guili Assembly." A jade plate in each of four ruins (north, east, south, west) explains one commandment. Someone who stayed behind after the Assembly fell hid a treasure where the four meet, so that treasure-seekers would carry the words forward. Soraya and the Traveler recovered both in Treasure Lost, Treasure Found.

81.comment: Guili Plains: The Fall of the Guili Assembly
81.content: About 3,700 years ago, in the Archon War, a battle on the Guili Plains destroyed the Assembly. The tablets recall black dust choking the heavens and a thousand rocks splintering. The adepti could not hold back the war, and Guizhong was killed. A flood followed, and Morax, Marchosius and the adepti led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng through more than ten days of storm to found Liyue Harbor. Morax raised the Millelith there. The enemy in that battle is never named.

82.comment: Guili Plains: Soraya, Scholar of Guili
82.content: Soraya is a Sumeru Akademiya researcher who studies Liyue's history, especially Guizhong. She leaves the fieldwork in the Guili ruins to the Traveler and admits she tires after a few seconds of running. She despises Treasure Hoarders for selling relics. After the Four Commandments were recovered, she said that if she met Guizhong she would recite them perfectly, to show that the people had not forgotten.

83.content:
Guizhong Ballista (also: Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism): The Guizhong Ballista is a huge ancient crossbow on Mt. Tianheng in Liyue. The God of Dust, Guizhong, designed it with the adepti, Cloud Retainer among them, to defend Liyue against dangerous enemies. It can fire by itself at anything it sees as a threat.

Geography: It stands among old ruins at Mt. Tianheng in the Sea of Clouds, at the pass that the Guili Assembly once guarded. A supply post nearby holds spare parts. Structural pieces such as the beams and bow limbs are lacquered and folded away in a store room, and the fine parts (trigger, fasteners, fletchings, bowstring) sit in a separate container.

Places: Supply post and maintenance notice: a notice outside the post explains that the Ballista is a work of divine conception made real by mortal craftsmen, and asks any future repairer to treat each part as their own body, in case an ancient evil returns to threaten the land.

History: Guizhong first designed the machine under the name Obscuro Vulpes Mechanism, and Rex Lapis judged it superior to Cloud Retainer's own mechanical creation. Guizhong and Cloud Retainer disagreed about ideals, but after Guizhong fell in the Archon War, Cloud Retainer finished the Ballista in her memory. It was built to defend against invaders from Tianheng Pass; the Guili Assembly moved its people north of the mountain.

Atmosphere: A weathered siege-weapon slumbering over a quiet ruin. The wood is old and lacquered, and the notices left by its makers speak of duty and long peace.

Dangers: It can fire on intruders by itself. Treasure Hoarders have broken it before in order to reach treasure hidden in the ruins.

Travel: The site lies on Mt. Tianheng in the Sea of Clouds, Liyue. After the Cocogoat quest the Traveler returns here while looking for a way to reach the Jade Chamber.

Quests: Pursuing the legendary adeptibeast Cocogoat for Qiqi, the Traveler, Paimon and Zhongli arrive hoping to use the Ballista as a scanner. They find it broken, Zhongli repairs it with gathered maintenance parts, and the activation draws the ire of the Treasure Hoarders led by Freckle Huang, who had damaged it. The hoarders are driven off. Later the Ballista is found mysteriously repaired in a day, and the Millelith guard it while the Qixing investigate until Keqing intervenes in a dispute with Paimon.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the original Ballista remains at Mt. Tianheng. The wiki records no change after Beisht's defeat, other than the presumed dismantling of the temporary copies.

84.content: The Guizhong Ballista is the ancient autonomous crossbow on Mt. Tianheng, designed by Guizhong with the adepti and finished by Cloud Retainer after Guizhong's death. It exists to defend Liyue from the worst enemies.

85.content:
Guyun Stone Forest (also: Guyun Tower): Guyun Stone Forest is an archipelago off Liyue's coast: seven large islands and smaller ones, crowded with jagged stone pillars that legend says are the remains of the lances Rex Lapis hurled to pin the sea god Osial to the ocean floor. People in Liyue say it is more a vista to behold than a place to visit. It holds the Domain of Guyun, a Geo Hypostasis on its northernmost island and, anchored off its shore, the Crux fleet's flagship Alcor.

The in-game text calls the pillars "proud, lonely stone mountains" and says that sensitive listeners sometimes hear a strange, stirring rhythm coming from the deep below. The expedition notes add that the forest is said to be a graveyard of the old gods. The Chinese name means "Lone Cloud Pavilion"; some English voice-over lines call it Guyun Tower.

Geography: Seven large islands and small offshoots in the sea off Liyue Harbor. The northernmost island houses the Geo Hypostasis and an island in the southwest the Domain of Guyun. Tall stone pillars rise from the islands. The shallow seas around them yield sea salt.

Places: - The Geo Hypostasis' island in the north.
- The Domain of Guyun in the southwest, an altar of ley lines.
- The Alcor, flagship of the Crux fleet, anchored offshore.
- Ruin-treasure monuments on the southern islands.

People: The crew of the Alcor, including the chief mate Juza, the navigator Huixing, the ironworker Suling, the bookkeeper Mora-Grubber, the surgeon Yinxing, and sailors such as Furong, Xu Liushi and Sea Drake. Captain Beidou normally commands the ship but has often returned to Liyue Harbor, leaving it to her crew.

Culture: Liyue folk treat Guyun as a place to look at rather than visit. The tale of Rex Lapis' victory over Osial and other sea monsters is a much-loved legend, and Liyue folk tell it in different versions.

History: Guyun is the battlefield where, about two thousand years ago in the Archon War, Rex Lapis defeated the god Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, a sea monster who could raise waves as tall as Liyue's mountains. Rex Lapis pinned him to the sea floor with giant lances of stone, and the pillars are said to be what remains.

Atmosphere: Cool shade under towering pillars, sea wind and the sound of waves, with beaches below. Those who sleep here are said to dream of being the sea monster, pinned and furious.

Dangers: Hilichurls and shooters, Abyss mages, Fatui agents, Geovishap hatchlings, Ruin Guards, and the Geo Hypostasis. Osial's strength did not fade in two thousand years of imprisonment, so the seal over him matters.

Travel: Roald borrowed a boat to reach the islands; in practice they are reached by boat and by gliding between them. The Alcor lies just off the islands, and the Domain of Guyun is in the southwest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Guyun Stone Forest is a silent archipelago with Osial resealed and the Alcor anchored offshore. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

Osial was resealed at the end of the 1.1 Archon Quest, and Beisht was driven off in the 2.4 Interlude.

86.comment: Guyun Stone Forest: Osial and Rex Lapis' Stone Spears
86.content: Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, was a god and sea monster of the Archon War, strong enough to raise tsunamis tall as mountains. Rex Lapis defeated him at Guyun and pinned him with stone spears, which became the pillars of Guyun Stone Forest. In 1.1 Childe freed him with Fatui Sigils of Permission to lure out the Geo Archon; the adepti and Millelith fought him and Ningguang dropped the Jade Chamber on him. A fragment of the spear, a Monolith Fragment, was recovered afterwards. Osial's "wife" Beisht later sought revenge.

87.content: The Alcor is the flagship of the Crux fleet, anchored off Guyun Stone Forest. Beidou usually captains it but lately lets her crew run it. Boarding it begins a world quest, A Lone Ship in Guyun.

88.content:
Hanfeng's Ironmongers (also: Hanfeng Ironware): Hanfeng's Ironmongers is a blacksmith in Liyue Harbor, marked on the map with a forging icon. It was founded by Hanfeng, nicknamed "Cold Blade", and is now run by his son, Master Zhang.

Its map description says Liyue has known the smithy for hundreds of years, that it is a favourite with the people of Liyue, and that with the right materials it never disappoints a customer. It quotes the saying "May the flames spread to all, and never be extinguished".

People: Master Zhang is the blacksmith; he sells basic weapons and will forge to order if the customer brings the right materials. He says repairs are free, and asks to be told whenever a customer finds good ore. Through repairing people's gear he has built up a network that feeds him tips about ore, including odd crystal ore veins he cannot yet work.

Status as of 7.1: Open and operating as of 7.1.

89.comment: Hanfeng's Ironmongers: Master Zhang and Hanfeng
89.content: Hanfeng retired to Qingce Village, while his son, the blacksmith Master Zhang, runs the Liyue Harbor forge. They rarely meet and each worries about the other.

90.content:
Heyu Tea House (also: Heyu Teahouse): Heyu Tea House is a teahouse in the upper part of Liyue Harbor, on Feiyun Slope, just below the Northland Bank and the upstairs part of Xinyue Kiosk. Yun Jin and the Yun-Han Opera Troupe perform there. Its owner is Fan Er'ye, a retired opera star who bought the place with the wealth from his performing days.

Besides opera, the house has a storyteller, Tea Master Liu Su. Fan Er'ye is there at all hours and is passionate about the stories and shows on his stage.

Places: Fan Er'ye describes the house to the Traveler: the stage, the tables and chairs, private rooms upstairs, performers and kitchen staff. He says he made it what it is. The stage is the focus; the Yun-Han Opera Troupe performs there, and a storyteller tells tales for customers.

People: Fan Er'ye is the boss. Tea Master Liu Su is the storyteller. Yun Jin directs the Yun-Han Opera Troupe, which performs here, and Changhu and Gentry Maocai are also seen there by day. Granny Ruoxin, now of Qingce Village, once performed at the house with Fan Er'ye.

History: Ruoxin fell in love with an adventurer and planned to leave her luxurious life for Mt. Qingce. He left on an expedition and never came back, and she now lives in Qingce Village. Fan Er'ye wishes he had had the courage to tell her how he felt.

Culture: The teahouse is part of Liyue Harbor's opera and storytelling life: a place to watch Liyue opera, listen to a storyteller and drink tea in company.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Heyu Tea House is open, with Fan Er'ye as owner and Yun Jin's troupe performing there.

Fan Er'ye can be found there at all times of the day, and his dialogue changes with the time. No change of ownership is recorded.

91.comment: Heyu Tea House: Fan Er'ye and Granny Ruoxin
91.content: Fan Er'ye, owner of Heyu Tea House, is a retired opera singer and actor of renown who performed with Ruoxin, now called Granny Ruoxin of Qingce Village. He admits he wishes he had told her how he felt. Ruoxin fell for an adventurer who never returned from an expedition.

92.content:
Hezhe Post (also: Hezhe Station): Hezhe Post is where the Communications Office conducts its business at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale. It handles registration, inspection and shipping applications for people and goods entering, leaving or moving within Liyue.

The Communications Office is one of the Eight Trades under the Liyue Qixing, and specialises in transportation.

Practice: Fangju lists four main tasks of the post: registering people and goods entering and leaving; inspecting and, if necessary, quarantining them; taking applications for delivery inside Liyue's borders; and providing ad-hoc storage. Outlanders who want to do business in Liyue and arrive at the wharf register here, and staff inspect and disinfect their goods.

People: Fangju and Lixing are Communications Office staff; Fangju is a steady, cautious clerk who describes himself as a lowly staff member and recommends the Ministry of Civil Affairs for more detail. Sai Jinzhuan also stands near the post and has idle lines about disobedient underlings.

Status as of 7.1: Open and active as of 7.1.

93.comment: Hezhe Post: Registering at Yilong Wharf
93.content: The post is the bureaucratic front door to Chenyu Vale for foreign merchants: register, be inspected, then choose delivery or storage.

94.content:
Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula (also: Guizang Formula Hidden Palace, Huaqing Guicang Hidden Palace): The Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula is a hidden treasure chamber under Luhua Pool, in the Qiongji Estuary of Liyue. From the surface it looks like an ordinary clear pond. Entry is sealed behind an old mechanism and a riddle-like inscription, and the palace holds two separate trials: "Voyage to the Sanguine Sky" and "Travels of the Moonlit Venturer".

It belongs to a trio of similarly named hidden palaces. The sister sites are the Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula and the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula. All three borrow their names from ancient divination systems, which is the only link between them that the game spells out. It is a one-time domain, so a traveller can clear each of its challenges for first-time rewards only once.

Geography: The entrance lies at Luhua Pool, a calm body of water in the Qiongji Estuary. A platform near the pool carries a circular mechanism. The game's description of the site stresses the contrast between the still surface and the hoard said to lie below, enough to drive a person mad, and adds that few who can decipher its secrets remain.

Atmosphere: Use it as a quiet, mildly eerie ruin: still water, weathered stone and an air of old secrets. The inscription at the mechanism says, in paraphrase, that anyone who follows in the footsteps of the immortals must kowtow before the treasure's gate. A wrong guess makes the puzzle reset, so a scene here rewards patience and observation more than force.

Travel: Activating the Pyro monuments that stand beneath the tall unbroken pillars, and only those, undoes the seal. Lighting a wrong monument resets the puzzle. Once the seal is broken the two domain entrances open.

History: Nothing in game text says who built the palace or why. The name echoes "Guicang", one of the ancient "Three Changes" divination texts of Chinese tradition, used here as a naming theme for three hidden palaces; this is an etymological note, not stated in-world history.

Quests: No story quest takes place here. Unlocking it grants an achievement named after the palace. The two inner domains are optional gameplay challenges.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, unchanged since its addition in 1.0. It does not figure in the Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content.

95.comment: Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula: Guizang Formula challenges
95.content: The two trials inside the Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula are "Voyage to the Sanguine Sky" and "Travels of the Moonlit Venturer". They are combat challenges that pay out treasure on first clear; treat them as self-contained trials with no recorded in-world story.

96.content:
Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula (also: Lianshan Formula): The Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula is a Domain of Forgery near Mingyun Village in Liyue, a thundering ancient sacrificial altar full of Electro slimes that rewards weapon ascension materials. Its description says the Lianshan Formula once raised endless storms inside the mountain, and that the rumbling outside the gate calls curious souls.

Its name is one of three "Hidden Palace of [Name] Formula" places, taken from the old Chinese divination arts Guicang, Lianshan and Zhou Yi (the Three Changes). Tradition, relayed by Lan Yan in the limited event Springtime Charms, says the Two Sages of Lianshan, two of the legendary Eight Adepts, used a hidden palace in the mountains south of Stone Gate as a place of retreat. The wiki ties that to this domain; the quest itself says only that it is the traditional belief.

Geography: The entrance sits near Mingyun Village in Qiongji Estuary, within Liyue. Thunder can be heard outside the gate. Inside, huge Electro energy courses through the altar, and dispersed Electro constantly drains Energy from anyone there.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: every party member gains 75% Cryo DMG (levels I to IV), with Cryo the recommended element; the enemies are Electro-based. Level names (Thundercloud, Thundering Ruins, Trial Grounds of Thunder) fit the storm theme.

Atmosphere: Heavy, dry air, storm light flashing in ancient stone halls, and thunder like a pulse in the walls.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1.

97.comment: Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula: Two Sages of Lianshan
97.content: In the limited event Springtime Charms (Version 5.3), the Two Sages of Lianshan are named as two of the Eight Adepts (with the Three Hermits of Guicang and the Three Beasts of Tao Dou). The mainstream story says the Guicang Hermits and Lianshan Sages were human. A hidden palace in the mountains south of Stone Gate is traditionally believed to have been their cultivation retreat.

98.content:
Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula (also: Zhou Formula Hidden Palace): The Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula is a Domain of Blessing on Wuwang Hill, in the Bishui Plain of Liyue. Its entrance text says a secret ritual that hides one gate out of eight, cutting off the route by which evil could escape, was performed here long ago and sealed demons inside this labyrinth. Rumor says the method of fitting pillars with Zhou Formula still seals an evil chi. Today it is a Hydro-themed trial where Artifacts are earned by defending a ley line monolith from Pyro-empowered monsters.

Its name is one of three "Hidden Palace of [Name] Formula" domains, drawn from the old Chinese divination arts Guicang, Lianshan and Zhou Yi (the Three Changes). It is the one whose English name does not match its Chinese name, which means roughly "Hidden Palace that Assumes Responsibility for Wuwang", a reference to the formulas used to seal the serpent at Wuwang Hill.

Geography: The domain stands at the top of Wuwang Hill, a subarea of the Bishui Plain in Liyue, on the hill that rises near Qingce Village. A large rock initially blocks the entrance, as at Cecilia Garden. To open it a traveller lights four ruins torches around the hill (one beside the Geo Monument, one inside a wind barrier, one at a hilichurl camp up the slope, and one north-east of that camp, where a Pyro Abyss Mage appears) and then activates the Geo Monument. Once it is open, the Electro cicins that wandered the area no longer appear.

History: The domain's description is the only direct account: a secret ritual that conceals one gate of eight was carried out here long ago and sealed demons in the labyrinth, and rumor says an evil chi is held by the method of fitting pillars with Zhou Formula. Nobody is named as the performer.

People: No one lives in the domain. The Wuwang Hill area has been avoided since the disaster, and local folk tales (told by children of Qingce Village) say a sea monster once lured the young people of Wuwang away with a whale-like song and drowned them, until only elders were left.

Dangers: Gameplay rules, labelled as such: the ley line disorder gives every party member a 75% Hydro DMG bonus at all four levels, and levels III and IV also grant a Hydro DMG bonus. The enemies are Pyro slimes, hilichurl fighters and berserkers, Blazing Axe Mitachurls, Dendro Samachurls and a Pyro Abyss Mage. At levels II to IV an elemental node empowers enemies with Pyro or Electro until the buff is removed by reactions such as Vaporize.

Atmosphere: Low grey sky, drifting blue ghost lights, thin fog on the hillside, and the heat of Pyro monsters against the damp of Hydro. It feels like a place where something is both held down and watched.

Quests: The domain is unlocked by the open-world puzzle on Wuwang Hill (light four torches, then the Geo Monument), and is also the subject of an achievement of the same name. It features in the lore of the limited-time event Springtime Charms only through the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method, not as a location.

Status as of 7.1: Permanent and unchanged as of Version 7.1. The Frost trials were renamed "Roaring Fire" in Version 4.8.

99.comment: Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula: Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method
99.content: A secret Liyue art that suppresses evil spirits and even gods by activating an array across eight key nodes of the ley lines, each overseen by one person. The array master conceals one gate, erasing themselves from the ley lines, so that the remaining seven stand and evil cannot flee. Its best-known use is the Eight Adepts' sanctification of the god Tao Dou. The domain's own text describes a similar ritual at Wuwang Hill, but names no performer.

100.comment: Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula: Chi of Qingce
100.content: A serpent god (also called Qingce in the ancient tongue) who nested where Qingce Village stands and was defeated by Morax; its spirit, bones, flesh, soul and form were each bound in a different direction to keep its power down. The domain text speaks only of "an evil chi" sealed by Zhou Formula, so do not assume it is this same being; the two stories rhyme but canon does not link them.

101.content:
Huaguang Stone Forest (also: Mist-Veiled Stone Forest): The Huaguang Stone Forest is a landscape of tall karst stone spires rising out of the clouds in Minlin, Liyue, hemmed in by three mountains: Mt. Aocang to the north, Qingyun Peak to the east and Mt. Hulao to the southwest. The in-game viewpoint says the place is forbidden to mortal steps and the kind of sight that draws those who yearn for the sky and who dwell in adepti realms.

It has no teleport waypoints of its own; travelers use those of the surrounding mountains. Two disciples of the declining Guhua Clan are found here searching for the adepti.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin whose pillars of rock stand like great pavilions above the clouds. Mt. Aocang lies north, Qingyun Peak east and Mt. Hulao southwest; the nearby waypoints on those mountains are the easiest way in. Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Jueyun Chili, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

People: Sun Yu and Little Que'er, disciples of the Guhua Clan, are found here for a time. Sun Yu has come to practise and, more importantly, to find the adepti and seek their counsel on how to revive the clan; Que'er accompanies him. Que'er is fiercely suspicious of strangers who approach, at first taking the Traveler for a mountain monster in disguise.

Dangers: Slimes of several elements, a Cryo Whopperflower and Geovishap Hatchlings.

Quests: No major story content is set here. The wiki lists the commission The Sparrow Studies the Blade for the area, and Sun Yu's presence here ends after a later quest named The Day the Sword Departs.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the forest is unchanged. The disciples' departure is the only story development tied to it, and no later content was found that alters it.

Places: The three surrounding mountains hold the waypoints: Mt. Aocang, Qingyun Peak and Mt. Hulao.

102.comment: Huaguang Stone Forest: The Guhua Disciples of Huaguang
102.content: Sun Yu and Little Que'er grew up together studying the Guhua Clan's martial arts. Sun Yu, devoted to the clan and eager to revive it, searches for an adeptus to advise him; Que'er follows him everywhere. Both are minor open-world NPCs. The Guhua Clan's base is Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng.

103.content:
Inverted City (also: The Inverted City, Upside-down city, Inverted Ancient City, Inverted Fountain, Diāndǎo Gǔchéng): The Inverted City is a ruin deep beneath the Chasm in Liyue: an ancient city whose buildings and a water pool hang upside down from the cavern ceiling. It is what remains of Lang-Gan, a city of Teyvat's unified civilisation governed by Zibai, after the Abyss tainted it and a Celestial Nail fell. The pool seems to soften the curse of immortality laid on the Khaenri'ahns.

It was sealed behind a purple barrier until the Traveler and Dainsleif reached it in Archon Quest Chapter II, where hilichurls came to live out their last days, the Black Serpent Knights stood guard, and the Abyss Order tried to turn the pool to its own purpose.

Geography: The city lies in the Nameless Ruins of the Chasm's Underground Mines, hanging above the cave floor with its terraces facing downward. Its crown is the upside-down water pool, with an altar-like structure and statues around it. Climbing the structure leads to the summit chamber.

History: Before Khaenri'ah, this was a city governed by Zibai under Celestia's gaze. After the war of funerary flame the city was corrupted by the Abyss and a Celestial Nail sent to purify it landed on it, burying Lang-Gan and creating the Chasm. The ruin stayed buried and dark for thousands of years.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the amplifier is destroyed, Halfdan is dead, and the pool remains a quiet relic. The Chasm itself is being reopened by the Qixing.

104.content:
Jade Chamber (also: Ningguang's floating palace): The Jade Chamber is a palace that floats in the sky above Liyue Harbor. It is the home and office of Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Liyue Qixing. She paid an astronomical sum for Plaustrite, a stone that can levitate, to build it, and from it she keeps watch over Liyue's commerce and affairs. Being invited up to the Jade Chamber is the greatest honour among Liyue's merchants. In the Archon Quest Ningguang sacrificed it to crush the ancient god Osial. She later rebuilt it, and the new Chamber floats over the harbor again.

Its map description calls it a symbol of Ningguang's might and of Liyue Harbor's unyielding will. The Chinese name means "Chamber of Many Jades".

Places: Decks outside the palace gates look out over almost all of Liyue Harbor on a clear day. The main hall holds Ningguang's desk and her famous intelligence wall. This wall is covered in shipping schedules, profit-and-loss accounts, warehouse inventories, road-safety reports and diplomatic intelligence, all kept up to date. Visitors are carried up on a specially carved Plaustrite platform run by the guide Bu'yun.

People: Ningguang does business here and allows only her three trusted confidants into the working rooms. These are the secretaries Baiwen, Baixiao and Baishi, who sort intelligence and pin summaries to the wall. Zhenhai serves as a guard. Guests come by invitation, and in the Archon Quest Ganyu delivered the Traveler's invitation for Ningguang.

Governance: The Chamber is Ningguang's personal property, not a Qixing office, but she runs much of her Tianquan work from it. The Qixing are said to monitor all of Liyue's goings-on from it. Liyue folk believe "Ningguang knows everything". Her real network is the harbor's children, whom she rewards with treats, and she checks their reports against other sources.

History: The Traveler first came to the Jade Chamber at Ningguang's invitation in A New Star Approaches. Keqing told them the way up and the password: "Excuse me, do you sell the moon here?" Ningguang received their gift, talked about gods, archons and the Fatui, and a clue on her wall led to evidence that the Fatui were copying Sigils of Permission. When Childe released Osial, the Qixing and the adepti gathered on the Chamber. They fought from Guizhong Ballistae that Ningguang had replicated, manned by Cloud Retainer, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver. Osial destroyed the ballistae. Ningguang then sacrificed the Chamber, which the Traveler helped send down onto the god, crushing him into the sea. She bid it farewell as an old friend and promised to meet again.

Functionality: The Chamber floats on a great core of Sunset Vermillionite, the name for especially large pieces of Vermillionite, a variety of Plaustrite. Plaustrite has to be activated before it floats; until then it weighs about as much as ordinary stone. The Chamber is steered from a control compartment, where Wonder Cores combined with Adepti Sigils act as its control centre. In the battle with Beisht, Ningguang fired projectiles at her from the Chamber.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the rebuilt Jade Chamber floats above Liyue Harbor again as Ningguang's residence and office, and visitors can be ferried up to it.

It is the second Jade Chamber. Some items from the first one's collection were never recovered.

105.comment: Jade Chamber: The Fall of the First Jade Chamber
105.content: In Turning Point (Chapter I, Act III) the Qixing and the adepti set aside their quarrel on the Jade Chamber to fight Osial, who had been released by Childe's Sigils of Permission. The Fatui sent soldiers through portals to wreck the ballistae; Keqing led the Millelith, and Xiao, Ganyu and Madame Ping blessed the Traveler. The adepti's combined shot failed and Osial smashed the ballistae and their platform. Ganyu insisted that the Chamber was their last line of defence and they could not give another inch; Ningguang answered that she would sacrifice it, and the Traveler drove a sword into it to send it crashing onto Osial.

106.comment: Jade Chamber: Beisht and the Second Jade Chamber
106.content: In The Crane Returns on the Wind, Ningguang rebuilt the Chamber with materials gathered through a public contest, lured Beisht, Osial's wife, and fought her with the people of Liyue rather than the adepti. Cloud Retainer praised the Qixing's preparation as considerable progress since the Osial crisis, while noting Shenhe's important part in the victory.

107.content:
Jade Mystery (also: The Jade Mystery, Jiecui Hang): The Jade Mystery is a jade shop in Liyue Harbor run by the cheerful boss Shitou. Its Chinese name is read Jiecui-hang, roughly "the store that reveals jadeite".

Shitou sells ores, cut stones and uncut rocks that customers can gamble on, in the hope of finding valuable jade inside.

Practice: Shitou says the shop takes pride in generations of experience crafting jade finery and has quite a reputation in Liyue. The shop sells pieces cut from raw stone, though not exactly rare jade, and its stock refreshes every few days. He greets customers by telling them they look radiant and must be lucky today.

People: Shitou is the boss, bright and persuasive, and enjoys a card game with customers.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

108.content:
Jademouth: Jademouth is a stretch of the Bishui River in Chenyu Vale, Liyue, flanked by enormous pieces of jade. Legend says an adeptus cast the jade down to protect the people of the vale from flooding.

Geography: Huge blocks of jade stand on both sides of the Bishui River in the upper part of Chenyu Vale. It is a subarea of the Upper Vale. The Version 4.4 preview text, in verse, refers to spring cries rippling through the vale, shrines leaving the northeast shores, and a whirlpool that never churns, with beautiful jade concealed within.

History: Legend says an adeptus cast the jade down to protect the people from flooding. Chenyu Vale lore, as cited by the wiki, ties this to the Archon War: the mistress of Chenyu Vale was at war with Morax and, near the end, loosed a flood along the Bishui River that would have drowned the vale. Her three adepti, the Herblord, Lingyuan and Fujin, rebelled; Fujin threw the Votive Rainjade into the water and so made Jademouth.

Atmosphere: Cool green stone beside moving water, in a vale of tea terraces and mist. The place feels like a shrine to an old rescue.

Quests: No Jademouth-specific quest was identified in the pages read. The related story is in the Chenyu Vale region quests of Version 4.4.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1 in the sources read. The source material on this landmark is thin; this entry is short on purpose.

109.content: Jademouth is the jade-flanked stretch of the Bishui River in Chenyu Vale. Legend says an adeptus threw the jade down to protect people from flooding; lore texts attribute it to Fujin and the Votive Rainjade.

110.content:
Jiulue Teahouse: The Jiulue Teahouse is a teahouse in Yilong Wharf, owned by Baishu. It has a stage for performances and an outdoor dining area, and the indoor dining area, private seats and rooms are temporarily under renovation.

Its Chinese name is Jiulue Chaguan. It is decorated for the Lantern Rite festival in the Springtime Charms event.

People: Baishu is the boss, an expansive businessman who trades on good wishes and flattery. He is also behind many of the nearby inns. Quezhi is the waitress who offers a choice of tea with a performance or a quick work meal; Jiewu is the storyteller. Regular customers include the tea merchants Jiuguan and Fryslan and, at night, Lixing of the Communications Office.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

111.content: Baishu went from tea farmer to owner of a teahouse, nearby inns and restaurants, and credits Master Jiuguan and the mechanisation of tea-making for his luck.

112.content:
Jueyun Karst (also: Jueyun Jian, Jueyun): Jueyun Karst is a realm of towering, cloud-ringed sandstone peaks in Minlin, northwestern Liyue, where the adepti, the immortal illuminated beasts who fought for Rex Lapis, have lived in seclusion since the Archon War. Mortals consider it sacred and seldom enter, though the brave or desperate still climb in search of adeptal blessings. Its great peaks each belong to an adeptus: Qingyun Peak to Moon Carver, Mt. Hulao to Mountain Shaper and Mt. Aocang to Cloud Retainer.

The Chinese name means roughly "Cloud-Terminating Place", for peaks that rise above the clouds. On maps "Jueyun Karst" also names one particular stretch of Minlin around the sunken Taishan Mansion, but people in Liyue use it for the whole adeptal highland.

Geography: Steep karst pillars and mountains wrapped in mist, with waterfalls and lakes. The map subarea lies between Taishan Mansion and Guili Plains. Around it rise Qingyun Peak, Mt. Aocang and Mt. Hulao, which ring the Huaguang Stone Forest. Wangshu Inn offers the classic distant view.

Places: Qingyun Peak (Moon Carver), Mt. Hulao (Mountain Shaper, guarded by amber-making "karst crawler" plants) and Mt. Aocang (Cloud Retainer, whose abode is reached from a stone table in a lake) each hide a sealed abode. Taishan Mansion is an ancient trial site, now flooded and sealed.

Culture: Liyue folk regard Jueyun Karst as sacred land that mortals should not enter. Entering without offending the adepti is said to be possible only for someone holding a Sigil of Permission, a talisman Rex Lapis once cast. Visitors leave food offerings, especially at Mt. Aocang's stone table.

History: After the Archon War some two thousand years ago, most adepti withdrew to Jueyun Karst and watched over Liyue from afar. Cloud Retainer remembers the peaks ringing with music when the adepti gathered; now they are quiet, since most of her old friends died in the wars.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Jueyun Karst remains the secluded home of the adepti and is still treated by mortals as sacred ground. Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper still keep their peaks.

Cloud Retainer moved to Liyue Harbor in human form as Xianyun before the 4.4 Lantern Rite but still keeps her abode on Mt. Aocang. The 7.0-7.1 Archon Quest takes place in Snezhnaya and shows no new events here.

113.comment: Jueyun Karst: The Traveler Seeks the Adepti
113.content: After Rex Lapis was apparently killed at the Rite of Descension, the Traveler was accused. Childe of the Fatui gave them a Sigil of Permission and sent them to Jueyun Karst to win the adepti's word. At Qingyun Peak, Moon Carver met them and asked them to drive off the pursuing Millelith. Learning of Rex Lapis' death enraged him, and he sent them to the other adepti. On Mt. Hulao, the Traveler freed a man's brother from amber, and Mountain Shaper scolded them for helping a "thief". On Mt. Aocang, they offered dishes at the stone table and made their way through Cloud Retainer's abode. She spoke of quashing Liyue, but because they came bearing a Sigil of Permission and appealing to contracts, she agreed to investigate first. Xiao was found at Wangshu Inn.

key: Illuminated Beast of the Sea of Clouds
114.comment: Jueyun Karst: Ganyu's Retreat to Jueyun
114.content: Ganyu, sent to deliver a letter from the Qixing to the adepti, lingered in Jueyun Karst. Seeing Ningguang's secretaries doing her work, she wrongly believed she had been replaced, and she doubted whether a half-qilin belonged among humans. At her request Cloud Retainer set her a trial near Mt. Aocang, and Xiao trained her at Nantianmen. A pilgrim, Xin Cheng, sought a materialistic blessing, which she refused. Back in the harbor, helping the official Huixin, whose family had looked up to her for generations, made her realise people valued her, and she resolved to keep working with the Qixing.

115.comment: Jueyun Karst: Jadevoid and the Trials of Heaven and Earth
115.content: Those seeking the adeptal path once faced two trials: "earth" at Taishan Mansion and "heaven" at the Dwelling in the Clouds, a plaustrite island above Qingyun Peak. Cloud Retainer built the Dwelling for meditation and lent it for the trial at Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper's urging, with the blessing of Rex Lapis, Guizhong and Streetward Rambler. The trial of crossing the void gave the name "Jadevoid", later applied to every adeptus' abode. Taishan Mansion is now sealed under water and has become a common treasure trove, its old altar now coursing with scorching Pyro energy.

116.content:
Karma-Heavy Cavern (also: Cavern of Karma): The Karma-Heavy Cavern is a cave in Guili Plains, Liyue, that draws creatures twisted by sinister energy. It is the setting of "The Purging of Evil", a Xiao story quest, in which the adeptus Xiao and the Traveler clear it of tainted hilichurls.

It is a quest domain, not a standing location: it is entered through the quest and used for one fight, not for exploration or trade.

Geography: The cavern sits in the Guili Plains region of the Qiongji Estuary. The quest begins with the Traveler tracking tainted hilichurls across the plains with Elemental Sight, and the trail leads to the cave. Platforms inside are cleared one after another.

Atmosphere: Oppressive and unnatural: Paimon says it gives her goosebumps. Xiao tells his companions to stay calm and not to be affected by the lingering wrath of bygone gods.

Dangers: Hilichurls and creatures corrupted by an evil aura fill the cave. Xiao uses a rite called the Bane of All Evil to relieve the place of its karma. In gameplay terms (a game mechanic, not lore), the party is Xiao alone, and his Elemental Burst stays active, constantly draining his health while hits restore it.

Quests: In "The Purging of Evil" (part 3 of Butterfly's Dream) Xiao is found having already slain tainted hilichurls. He admits his karma caused the changes and declines company, then lets the Traveler and Paimon come along. After the fight he learns about "Starsnatcher", a masked man posing as a wish-granting adeptus who exorcises demons with a Sigil of Permission without destroying them. Xiao concludes that this is why demons gather here and resolves to confiscate the sigil.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing has changed. The cavern does not appear in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content.

117.comment: Karma-Heavy Cavern: Karma-Heavy Cavern and Xiao
117.content: In the Karma-Heavy Cavern Xiao purifies living things that carry demonic taint sourced from his own karma. He accepts suffering as the price of ages of slaughter, but says others should not suffer for a burden that ought to be his alone; he resolves to reflect on this.

118.content:
Lang-Gan (also: Langgan, Lánggān, ancient nation of Lang-Gan, Lang-Gan civilisation): Lang-Gan was a great nation of Teyvat's unified civilisation, on what is now the western coast of Liyue. Its people lived by the mines and were guided by Zibai, an angel who served Celestia as a Moon Envoy and whom they worshipped as a god of soil and grain. In the war of funerary flame the Abyss tainted it, and Celestia sent a Celestial Nail to purify it. Zibai died holding the Nail back so that her people could flee, and the impact made the Chasm.

The Inverted City and Nameless Ruins under the Chasm are what is left. Some survivors went east and founded Chenyu Vale, taking their old rites; Zibai was later remembered in Liyue as the White Horse Adeptus.

Geography: A coastal nation whose settlements ran from peak to peak across the crystal-veined mountains where the Chasm now yawns. Wiki-cited texts say it was a great and lovely land, made to bless the children of humanity. A weapon legend places it on the western coast before Mt. Tianheng rose.

People: The Lang-Gan people mined jade and ore, and their lives and families revolved around the mines. Zibai taught them silk painting, farming, spinning and weaving. At the dawn of the nation she gave the longbow Yayu to the high priest, which gave him the right to lead as emperor. The people had no books; they kept history in ballads that poetry collectors later wrote down for the court.

Culture: Lang-Gan honoured the Three Moons, and above all Zibai, at a finely carved jade altar, with offerings and sacrifices. Its people held the Three Moons in awe along with other civilisations of the Moon era such as Hyperborea, Arcadia, Sal Vindagnyr and Meropis. In memory visions, Lang-Gan's people released lanterns at the altar when a Trilunar Syzygy filled the sky.

Governance: A priest-emperor ruled under Zibai's guidance; Zibai herself was the divine envoy of Celestia and the people's patron deity.

History: After the Eternal and Iridescent Moons shattered in the war of funerary flame, Abyssal corruption tainted Lang-Gan. The Heavenly Principles answered by sending Celestial Nails to heal the land. Istaroth advised Zibai to let it fall, but she refused to abandon her people, held the Nail back for a time at the cost of her life, and let the inhabitants flee. Istaroth preserved her soul, splitting it into the Three Deadly Selves. The refugees travelled east.

Dangers: The ruins are under the Chasm's Underground Mines, with Abyss Order agents, Ruin Guards and corrupted mines. Nothing remains of the nation as a place to visit.

Travel: Not directly reachable; one sees its remains through the Inverted City and the Nameless Ruins in the Chasm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lang-Gan is a buried ruin and a memory; its descendants live in Chenyu Vale and beyond, and Zibai has been restored.

119.content: This account comes from the "A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon" story (Lantern Rite 2026, 6.3, since kept as a story quest), shown as a memory by Zizhi, the wrathful fragment of Zibai's soul. A Celestial Nail appeared in the sky over Lang-Gan. Istaroth told Zibai that everything tainted by the Abyss must be purified, Lang-Gan included, that this was heaven's will and that she was only an emissary; Zibai answered that her people honoured and prayed to her and that she would die among them rather than live with the guilt. Her Jadelight Canopy halted the Nail's descent for a time and the people fled. She fell and Istaroth caught her, splitting her soul into the Three Deadly Selves; the survivors looked up at the one remaining moon. Zizhi says the tainted remnants of the war falling from the sky devastated Lang-Gan and that the descendants of Lang-Gan made their home throughout Liyue.

120.content:
Lianfang Dim Sum: Lianfang Dim Sum is a shop in Yilong Wharf run by Lianfang. It sells local food, cooking ingredients and recipes, and is open at all times of the day.

Its stock includes tea eggs, a tea brew, smoked squab and, per the wiki, recipes for them; Lianfang pitches them as simple, convenient foods you can even eat on board a ship.

Philosophy: Lianfang explains that Chenyu Vale's traditional dining is leisurely: sitting by the water with a pot of tea and a few dishes, drinking, enjoying the view and composing poems. But Yilong Wharf is a commercial port whose visitors want working meals they can finish quickly, so she adapts traditional dishes to suit them.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1.

121.comment: Lianfang Dim Sum: Lianfang's working meals
121.content: Lianfang is proud of Chenyu Vale's leisurely dining traditions yet pragmatic about commercial reality.

122.content:
Lingju Pass: Lingju Pass is a mountain pass in Lisha, Liyue, made up mostly of old ruins and puzzle mechanisms. Legend says the ruins were once a stronghold of the Geo Archon Morax where mortals and adepti fought side by side, and a sign in the pass carries an anonymous poem about a divine order. The name is usually read as "divine law".

The pass hides one of the three Nameless Treasures that tell of the sealing of the Geo dragon Azhdaha, and a one-time domain lies close by.

Geography: A subarea of Lisha with ruins, a lake with a floating platform, and Geo-controlled puzzle monuments. The one-time Domain of the Wayward Path lies between Lingju Pass and Mt. Tianheng. Local specialties are Cor Lapis and Violetgrass.

Places: The ruined stronghold; a signboard bearing a poem (see history); the lake and its floating platform; the Domain of the Wayward Path nearby.

History: The wiki records a legend that Morax built the ruins as a stronghold where mortals and adepti fought together, and vague tales of Morax's divine law, lingju, which may connect to the poem on the sign. The poem reads, in summary, that a divine order governs the world, that everyone must die whether noble or wicked, rich or poor, and that the creator shows favour to none, so the faithful praise the divine rule in song.

Quests: And This Treasure Goes To... (world quest: investigate a strange camp, look for a missing scholar, defeat Treasure Hoarders for a key, open a cage and dig up the buried Nameless Treasure). Zhongli's story quest Historia Antiqua Chapter, Act II, No Mere Stone, passes through while following missing miners. Tartaglia's story quest Monoceros Caeli Chapter, Act I, Mighty Cyclops' Adventure!, begins here when Ruin Guards roam the wild and the Traveler meets a boy from Snezhnaya named Teucer.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Fatui skirmishers, mitachurls, Abyss mages and Ruin Guards.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lingju Pass is unchanged and open. No later story content was found that alters it.

123.comment: Lingju Pass: Nameless Treasures and the Sealing of Azhdaha
123.content: Three Nameless Treasures, one each at Lingju Pass, Qingxu Pool and Dunyu Ruins, form a set whose patterns tell how Azhdaha, a dragon born from Liyue's Geo spirits, was lured into a cavern by Rex Lapis and sealed there by three adepti. Linlang reads two of the three adepti as Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver; the third carving was erased, and the identity is not stated.

124.content:
Lingshu Courtyard (also: Herblord's abode): Lingshu Courtyard is a cave garden in Chenyu Vale's Southern Mountain, the abode of a long-departed adeptus known as the Herblord. A talkative stone Carefree Simulacrum guards it and asks the Traveler to chase scattered butterflies back into a medicine jar so a withered adeptal tree can bloom again. Entering for the first time starts the world quest Silently the Butterfly Crosses the Valley.

Only empty medicine containers remain of the Herblord, and a hidden vault holds her notes. The wiki thinks the name echoes the Lingshu Jing, an ancient Chinese medical text, which suits the setting.

Geography: The courtyard lies in a cave reached from Yaodie Valley. Features: Seelie, a Golden Carp's Leap, a Windmill Mechanism and Rock Piles; specialties are Clearwater Jade and Glaze Lily; common enemies are Grounded Geoshrooms and Whirling Electro Fungi. Large hanging pots, stalagmites and jars fill the courtyard, and a withered adeptal tree stands there.

People: The Carefree Simulacrum speaks in an old, formal and sleepy manner, boasts that it frightens off intruders, and wants the butterflies returned. Smaller Sacred Simulacra give riddling hints. It misses the Herblord, who left when she lost the power to keep her human form.

History: Long ago the Herblord used the butterflies to adorn the door of her abode; that mechanism was later broken. The tree withered, and the butterflies scattered once she left. The viewpoint text says her wish to help those in need never wavered, even at the very end of the Archon War.

Quests: Silently the Butterfly Crosses the Valley: catch five butterflies (orange, golden, blue, green and purple) in the courtyard and put them in the medicine jar, then revive the tree, enter the vault and read the Ancient Text.

Status as of 7.1: The Herblord remains absent as of 7.1. The tree and vault are open to visitors after the quest.

125.content: The Ancient Texts in the hidden vault mention Fujin's enthusiasm for the Votive Rainjade, a request for slimming tea and a vague bad feeling; they are the private voice of an adeptus rather than a record of events. The vault is reached by breaking a branch from the revived tree and placing it in the broken jar.

126.content:
Lisha (also: Glaze Sand Outskirts, Líshā-jiāo): Lisha ("Glaze Sand Outskirts") is the dry ruin-country of southwestern Liyue. Its crumbling stone sites date from the Archon War and earlier: the sunken-city ruins of Qingxu Pool, the fortress of Lingju Pass, the Dunyu Ruins hollowed by the cataclysm, and a small restored temple to a long-dead yaksha. The entrance to the Chasm and its mines lies on its edge, and its old surface mines have largely moved there.

Most of its history is told in tablets, notices and legends; few people live here now.

Geography: Open, sandy-hued uplands of rock and glazed stone broken by ruins and pools. The river that flows through much of Liyue does not reach Lisha. A notice northwest of Qingxu Pool, by a group of ore investigation points, announces that the miners have moved to the Chasm.

Places: Qingxu Pool: ruins of a city said to have been submerged until the Archon War's end, with a tower rising from a green field. Lingju Pass: a ruined stronghold of puzzles and Geo monuments. Dunyu Ruins: ancient vestiges around a dead lake. Pervases' Temple: a small shrine to the yaksha Pervases, restored in the Hereafter quests.

History: Lingju Pass is said to have been a stronghold of Morax where mortals and adepti fought side by side. Qingxu Pool's ruin predates the Archon War and sat submerged until the war ended. The dragon Azhdaha was said to have rampaged across Lisha before Rex Lapis and three adepti sealed him in the Chasm. In the cataclysm, the Dunyu Ruins and the Chasm were two Liyue places hit hardest; Dunyu's people abandoned the city for Liyue Harbor and have never explained why.

Travel: Travelers mostly pass through on the way to the Chasm, whose entrance is marked by the miners' notice near Qingxu Pool.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Lisha is quiet ruin country beside the Chasm; no Lisha-specific change is recorded in 6.x-7.1 content.

Pervases' Temple stands restored. The Chasm nearby is the focus of the 7.1 Celestial Nail anomaly, with extra Millelith patrols.

127.content: Qingxu Pool is a ruined tower amid a green field and, beneath it, sealed underground ruins that legend says belonged to an evil god's city, submerged until the Archon War ended. The Qixing once approved an excavation for the rumored buried treasure, but the ruins were sealed and the tech to blast through solid rock did not yet exist. Many groups kept hoping, including the Fatui. A Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan in Yelan's story quest covered a plot to use the Blackcliff Forge's explosives to open them. The local Tieshan comes from a settlement in the area.

128.content: Dunyu Ruins ("Fleeing Jade Mausoleum") is a set of ancient vestiges around a dead lake, suspended in time. During the cataclysm an iron meteorite hit the Chasm and monsters poured out; Dunyu was one of two Liyue sites most affected, and its people decided to abandon the city and move to Liyue Harbor. Neither the refugees nor the adepti have talked about what happened. One of the three Nameless Treasures is hidden here.

129.content: Lingju Pass is a ruined stronghold that legend says Morax founded, where mortals and adepti fought together. Its Geo monument puzzles lead to a floating platform and chests, and a poem on a sign about the divine order of the world is thought to relate to Morax's lingju, his divine law.

130.content: Pervases' Temple honors the junior yaksha Pervases, killed in the Archon War and said to linger in a crane statue. It began as a run-down house until the repentant fraud Wang Ping'an rebuilt it in the world quest series Hereafter, sinking his earnings into the project. After the Chasm, Xiao came back to the temple to think about the fate of the yakshas, and it was shown that Pervases was close to the Prime Yaksha Bosacius.

131.content:
Liuli Pavilion (also: Glaze Pavilion): Liuli Pavilion is the leading restaurant for Li-style cuisine in Liyue, a style centred on mountain delicacies. It stands on Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor, deliberately across from Xinyue Kiosk, the flagship of the rival Yue style. In the Archon Quest Childe arranges a business dinner here to introduce the Traveler to Zhongli.

The Traveler is directed there by Ekaterina at the Northland Bank. The staff includes the waiter Hongru and Licai, a waitress who stands outside; a visitor from Fontaine called Francis also dines there.

Places: The pavilion has an exterior, an interior that looks different by day and by night, and private rooms; Hongru tells Childe that Zhongli awaits in the room Childe booked. Licai stands outside and sells the pavilion's specialties. The pavilion is the Li style's counterpart of the Yue-style Xinyue Kiosk, close by on Feiyun Slope.

People: Hongru is the waiter who greets Childe, who is a returning guest. Licai is a waitress outside who sells the house specialties. Francis is a Fontaine visitor inside by day.

Culture: Liyue has two main styles of cooking, Li style and Yue style, which have competed for centuries without a clear winner. Li cuisine uses mountain delicacies; Liuli Pavilion is its flagship, while Xinyue Kiosk is the flagship of Yue style. Paimon explains this to the Traveler on the way.

History: Ekaterina at the bank says Childe is at Liuli Pavilion. Paimon explains the Li and Yue rivalry. At the pavilion Hongru welcomes Childe, saying Zhongli awaits them in the booked room. Childe says he followed Liyue custom in arranging a business dinner. In the private room he introduces Zhongli as a consultant to Wangsheng, and Zhongli says he can bring the Traveler to see Rex Lapis' vessel.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Liuli Pavilion remains open on Feiyun Slope.

132.comment: Liuli Pavilion: Li and Yue Cuisine
132.content: Paimon explains that Liyue has two cooking styles, Li and Yue, which have competed for centuries without a winner. Li style focuses on mountain delicacies and its flagship is Liuli Pavilion; Yue style is represented by Xinyue Kiosk. Liuli Pavilion is on Feiyun Slope specifically to compete face to face with Xinyue Kiosk.

133.content:
Liyue: Liyue is the nation of contracts in eastern Teyvat, the land of the Geo Archon Morax, whom locals call Rex Lapis. He founded Liyue Harbor about 3,700 years ago and ruled it as the God of Contracts and Commerce, but he has since faked his own death and lives quietly among mortals as Zhongli, a consultant at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. The nation is now run by the Liyue Qixing, seven merchant leaders. The immortal adepti still guard it from the mountains. Liyue Harbor is the wealthiest trading port in Teyvat, and Mora, the coin used across the continent, is named after Morax.

Liyue folk take contracts seriously, haggle without shame and revere the adepti. Few people know that Zhongli is their god. The Qixing told the public that Rex Lapis died in a trial and took over every one of his duties.

Geography: Liyue is mountainous country of stone forests, karst peaks, terraced fields, marshes and rivers. Its main areas are:
- Bishui Plain: Stone Gate, Wangshu Inn and Qingce Village.
- Qiongji Estuary: the Guili Plains.
- Minlin: Jueyun Karst, home of the adepti.
- Lisha: ancient ruins.
- The Sea of Clouds: Liyue Harbor, Mt. Tianheng and the Guyun Stone Forest.

Further west lie two more subregions: The Chasm, a vast mine (opened in 2.6), and Chenyu Vale, tea country on the Fontaine border (opened in 4.4).

Government: The Liyue Qixing ("Seven Stars") are seven leading businesspeople who have governed since about 2,000 years ago. They meet at Yuehai Pavilion on Yujing Terrace. Each takes a title from a star of the Big Dipper, and all are formally equal. Three members are publicly known:
- Tianquan Ningguang: law and foreign relations.
- Yuheng Keqing: land, construction and real estate.
- Tianshu Uncle Tian: policymaking.

The half-qilin adepta Ganyu has been General Secretary from the start and does the calculations behind the council's policies. The Millelith, the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Eight Trades all answer to the Qixing.

Religion: Rex Lapis is revered as the God of Contracts and Commerce and the Warrior God. The adepti are revered almost as much. They are illuminated beasts and spirits who fought for Morax under contract. Some still live in Jueyun Karst, and others asked to be turned to stone when the war ended. Wangsheng Funeral Parlor performs funerals for mortals and the rare rites that send off adepti.

History: Morax was born more than 6,000 years ago. With Guizhong, the God of Dust, he founded the Guili Assembly. About 3,700 years ago, during the Archon War, a battle destroyed it and killed Guizhong. Morax led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng and founded Liyue Harbor. There he raised the Millelith, minted Mora and bound the adepti by contract. He then conquered the rival gods, pinning Osial beneath the Guyun Stone Forest, and became the Geo Archon about 2,000 years ago. During the cataclysm 500 years ago, monsters burst out of the Chasm and were sealed away at great cost. In Chapter I, Rex Lapis staged his own death and gave the Geo Gnosis to the Fatui.

Customs: Contracts are sacred, and breaking one's word is shameful. Tea, opera, calligraphy, fine cooking and antique-collecting flourish. The great festivals are the Lantern Rite, which begins on the first full moon of the year, and the autumn Moonchase Festival. Glaze Lilies are Liyue's traditional flower.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Liyue is prosperous, at peace and governed by the Qixing alone. Rex Lapis is publicly believed dead; in truth he lives in Liyue Harbor as Zhongli and works for Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. The Geo Gnosis is in the Fatui's hands.

The Golden House has stopped minting Mora. The adepti accept mortal rule, and Cloud Retainer now lives in the city in human form as Xianyun. The Jade Chamber, sacrificed against Osial, has been rebuilt. Xiao still guards Liyue from Wangshu Inn, and Ganyu still serves the Qixing.

135.comment: Liyue: Lantern Rite and Moonchase Festival
135.content: The Lantern Rite is Liyue's biggest festival. It begins on the first full moon of the year and lasts five days. People release Xiao Lanterns, which began as lights to guide soldiers home in wartime and later became a way to remember the war dead. Each year a giant Mingxiao Lantern honours a hero of Liyue's past, usually an adeptus who died defending the land. The autumn Moonchase Festival is a time for family reunions and feasts. The Qixing choose its theme and host the Masterful Chefs cooking contest.

136.content: Liyue Harbor stands on the coast beneath Mt. Tianheng and is Teyvat's richest port. Yujing Terrace, the wealthiest district, sits on the clifftop and holds Yuehai Pavilion (the seat of the Qixing), the Golden House mint, and the lift to the Jade Chamber, which floats above the city. Feiyun Slope is the shopping and guild quarter, home to Liuli Pavilion, Xinyue Kiosk and the Feiyun Commerce Guild. Chihu Rock is the poorer end of the city, with street food, Wanmin Restaurant and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Bubu Pharmacy stands on its own small island, and the Northland Bank, Heyu Tea House and the Ministry of Civil Affairs are all in the city.

137.comment: Liyue: Bishui Plain and Wangshu Inn
137.content: Bishui Plain is the northern gateway to Liyue. Stone Gate is the crossroads where the roads from Dawn Winery, Qingce and Liyue Harbor meet. Dihua Marsh was a fertile islet until the battle that destroyed the Guili Assembly turned it into a swamp. Wangshu Inn stands on a giant stone pillar south of the marsh, a landmark for caravans. Its staff are secret Qixing agents who support Xiao, who lives on its balcony. Qingce Village, with its terraced fields at the foot of Mt. Qingce, has become a place where the elderly retire. Wuwang Hill is permanently dark and grey.

138.comment: Liyue: Minlin, Jueyun Karst and the Adepti
138.content: Minlin is high karst country, and its centre, Jueyun Karst, is where the adepti dwell. Few dare to climb there, though the desperate and the devout still go seeking blessings. Cloud Retainer, a crane adeptus and master of mechanisms, lived on Mt. Aocang. Moon Carver lives on Qingyun Peak. Mountain Shaper guards Mt. Hulao, whose amber traps catch intruders. Nantianmen is where the earth dragon Azhdaha lies sealed beneath the tree called the Dragon-Queller, which he has begun to merge with.

139.content: Lisha holds ruins older than Rex Lapis' rule. During the Archon War the whole region was under water. Lingju Pass and Qingxu Pool were submerged with it and only reappeared when the tides receded after the war. Qingxu Pool's ruins are said to have been built by an evil god whose name has been erased. Dunyu Ruins was abandoned during the cataclysm, reportedly because of Abyssal influence. In Qiongji Estuary, the Guili Plains hold the broken remains of the Guili Assembly. Mingyun Village was abandoned when its ore ran out. Yaoguang Shoal is named for the glowing sea creatures that once filled its waters.

140.comment: Liyue: Sea of Clouds and Guyun Stone Forest
140.content: The Sea of Clouds holds Liyue Harbor, Mt. Tianheng and the Guyun Stone Forest. The Guyun Stone Forest is an archipelago of seven islands bristling with the stone spears Morax hurled down to pin Osial and other sea monsters to the ocean floor, sealed with Sigils of Permission. Seen from above, the formation resembles his Geo symbol. Mt. Tianheng shelters the harbour. During one battle a god split its foundation, and the adeptus Skybracer had his antlers, a gift from Morax, cut off to prop the mountain up before he died of his wounds. Blackcliff Forge on the mountain makes the Blackcliff and Prototype weapons.

141.content: The Chasm is a vast mining region in western Liyue. Its depths, the Underground Mines, lie beneath the Seven-Star Array, a seal the Qixing laid over them. They closed the mine after mysterious accidents, earthquakes and a harmful "Wishstone" dug up by miners, and are now letting experienced miners back in. In the cataclysm an object struck the Chasm and monsters poured out. The Yaksha Bosacius, the thaumaturge Boyang and the Millelith vanguard sealed themselves in the depths with the beasts using the Fantastic Compass. Deep below hangs the Spiritstone, a Celestial Nail.

142.content: Chenyu Vale is the fog-wrapped tea country of western Liyue on the Fontaine border. Qiaoying Village's tea is famous across Teyvat, and Yilong Wharf is a busy port where Fontainians come to experience Liyue culture. In ancient times a nameless mistress of the vale ruled its wild spirits and the Bishui River, attended by three adepti: the snake Herblord, the golden carp Fujin and the suanni Lingyuan. Near the end of the Archon War she fought Morax and tried to flood the river. The three adepti turned on her and sealed her beneath the vale, and Fujin cast the Votive Rainjade into the water.

143.comment: Liyue: Rex Lapis' Departure and the Osial Crisis
143.content: At the Rite of Descension the Traveler attended, Rex Lapis' body fell from the sky, apparently murdered. The Qixing locked down the city and took the Exuvia to the Golden House. Zhongli, hired through Childe to arrange the Rite of Parting, led the Traveler through the old customs. Childe then searched the Exuvia for the Gnosis, found nothing, and used Sigils of Permission to free Osial and force the "hidden" god to show himself. The Qixing, the adepti, the Millelith and the Traveler held Osial back, and Ningguang dropped her Jade Chamber onto him. Zhongli then revealed that he was Morax. He had staged the whole affair to test whether Liyue could stand on its own, and he gave the Geo Gnosis to Signora under his contract with the Tsaritsa.

144.content:
Liyue Harbor: Liyue Harbor is the capital of Liyue: a vast, prosperous port on the coast beneath Mt. Tianheng, founded by the Geo Archon Morax (Rex Lapis) and now governed by the merchant council of the Liyue Qixing. It is Teyvat's largest market harbour, where a thousand ships drop anchor and goods from every nation change hands under a dense web of contracts. Its three districts are the clifftop Yujing Terrace (wealth and government), the merchant quarter of Feiyun Slope, and the working-class Chihu Rock by the docks. Ningguang's floating palace, the Jade Chamber, hovers above the city.

Every year the Lantern Rite fills the night sky over the harbour with thousands of lanterns. Since the Rite of Descension at which Rex Lapis was apparently killed, the city has run without a living god's guidance; in truth he lives here quietly as Zhongli.

Geography: The harbour lies in the Sea of Clouds area, between the sea and the cliffs of Mt. Tianheng. Yujing Terrace climbs the western cliffside; Feiyun Slope sits in the middle and is the entrance from the northern road; Chihu Rock is an island to the southeast, bridged to Feiyun Slope and Mt. Tianheng.

Places: Yujing Terrace holds Yuehai Pavilion, seat of the Qixing. Feiyun Slope has the shops, guilds, restaurants, Heyu Tea House, the Northland Bank and Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Chihu Rock has Wanmin Restaurant, street food, the Adventurers' Guild and the docks. Bubu Pharmacy is the city's famous pharmacy.

People: Residents include the Qixing (Ningguang, Keqing, Uncle Tian) and their secretary Ganyu; Zhongli and Hu Tao of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor; Xiangling of Wanmin Restaurant; Xingqiu; Baizhu and Qiqi; and Yun Jin. Beidou's Crux berths here.

Culture: Commerce and contracts define the city. The Lantern Rite, Liyue's five-day new year festival from the first full moon, is the greatest celebration: people release Xiao Lanterns and raise the giant Mingxiao Lantern in remembrance of the fallen. Opera, teahouses, storytelling and food thrive.

History: About 3,700 years ago, after the Guili Assembly on the Guili Plains was destroyed in the Archon War and Guizhong died, Morax, Marchosius and the adepti led the survivors south of Mt. Tianheng and founded Liyue Harbor. Morax raised the Millelith, made a contract with the adepti to defend the city and minted Mora. When the Traveler arrived, Rex Lapis' body fell from the sky during the Rite of Descension; the "death" was staged by Morax, who then gave his Gnosis to the Fatui after Childe released the sea god Osial against the city and Ningguang dropped the Jade Chamber onto it.

Atmosphere: Crowded wharves, hawkers and haggling, teahouses and opera, street food in Chihu Rock, merchants and foreigners on Feiyun Slope, and the stately calm of Yujing Terrace beneath the floating Jade Chamber.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Liyue Harbor is prosperous and at peace under the Qixing. Rex Lapis is publicly believed dead, but lives in the city as Zhongli. The Jade Chamber has been rebuilt and again floats above the harbour.

The Golden House has stopped minting Mora. Cloud Retainer lives in the city as Xianyun. The White Horse Adeptus Zibai, restored during the 6.3 Lantern Rite event, is now associated with Liyue Harbor. The Archon Quest has moved to Snezhnaya (Chapter VII); no new crisis in the harbour is shown there.

145.content: Yujing Terrace is the westernmost and wealthiest district of Liyue Harbor, built along the cliffs of Mt. Tianheng above the harbour. It holds Yuehai Pavilion, seat of the Liyue Qixing and their secretaries, and Yiyan Temple, where a guide admits visitors to the Jade Chamber. The Rite of Descension was held here each year, and it was here that Rex Lapis' body fell before the crowd.

146.content: Feiyun Slope is Liyue Harbor's prosperous merchant district and the city's entrance from the northern road. Along its tiers stand the Ministry of Civil Affairs, Liuli Pavilion and Xinyue Kiosk, Wanwen Bookhouse, Mingxing Jewelry, Heyu Tea House (where the Yun-Han Opera Troupe performs), the Northland Bank on the top level, a Snezhnayan merchant area, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, and the northern wharf.

147.content: Chihu Rock is Liyue Harbor's lower-class district, on an island southeast of the rest of the city, bridged to Feiyun Slope and Mt. Tianheng. It is the city's working heart: Wanmin Restaurant and food stalls, the Adventurers' Guild branch, blacksmiths, a jade shop, the storytelling teahouse Third-Round Knockout, Yanshang Teahouse, the dockyard, warehouses and the fish market.
