148.content: The Jade Chamber is the floating palace of the Tianquan Ningguang, hovering over Liyue Harbor, from which she monitors happenings across Liyue; her famous intelligence wall is kept there. It floats on a great chunk of Sunset Vermillionite, a kind of plaustrite, and is steered by Adepti Sigils and Wonder Cores. Ningguang sacrificed it to crush Osial, and its weight and stored energy defeated him. She later rebuilt it (2.4), partly to lure out Beisht, and the second chamber survived the battle.

149.content: The Golden House, on Mt. Tianheng above the harbour, is where all of Teyvat's Mora was minted using the Geo Archon's power. After Rex Lapis' "death" the Qixing moved his body, the Exuvia, there, and the Fatui tried to strike it during the Archon Quest. Since he gave up his Gnosis it has stopped producing new Mora; Zhongli says existing Mora will not vanish and leaves the problem to the Qixing.

150.comment: Liyue Harbor: The Rite of Descension and the Osial Crisis
150.content: When the Traveler arrived, Liyue Harbor was preparing the yearly Rite of Descension at Yujing Terrace. Instead of the god appearing, Rex Lapis' body fell dead before the crowd; the Millelith sealed off the Terrace and hunted suspects, and the Traveler fled with Childe's help. Childe, believing he was flushing out the god, used stolen Sigils of Permission to free Osial from the Guyun Stone Forest. As the monster bore down on the harbour, the Qixing, Millelith and adepti fought together and Ningguang dropped the Jade Chamber onto it. Zhongli then presided over the Rite of Parting and handed the Geo Gnosis to Signora under his contract with the Tsaritsa.

151.content:
Luhua Pool (also: Weeping Garden): Luhua Pool is a scenic landscape of brightly coloured pools watched over by two giant statues, in Qiongji Estuary, Liyue. A hidden ruin beneath it guards the entrance to the one-time domain called the Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula. The game describes it as the product of a deep, pure affection that once filled an ancient garden.

A travelling painter, Vermeer, is found here looking for inspiration. The two statues' eyes are the key to opening the ruin.

Geography: A subarea of Qiongji Estuary with terraced ponds, two giant statues, and Geo and Pyro elemental monuments. Local specialty: Cor Lapis. Roaming foes are hilichurl grenadiers, a Cryo hilichurl shooter and a large Dendro slime, plus a Fatui Pyro Agent as the elite.

Places: The terraced ponds; the two statues overlooking them; the ruin entrance with a central monument; the Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula domain, which holds two domains, Voyage to the Sanguine Sky and Travels of the Moonlit Venturer.

People: Vermeer, a travelling painter, is found near the pool. He has been looking for a good angle for a picture of the giant statues with blazing eyes that he has heard about.

Quests: Luhua Landscape (world quest). After recovering Vermeer's tools from the places in his two sketches, the Traveler collects the "strange stones" (eye-like stones, one found by Vermeer in a pond), inserts one into each statue's head, activates the central monument with Geo and fights Cryo, Pyro and Hydro Abyss mages that appear, then opens the ruin's chests.

Dangers: Mostly mild: hilichurls, a large Dendro slime and a Fatui Pyro Agent. The ruin puzzle can summon Abyss mages briefly.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pool is unchanged. No later story content was found that alters it.

152.comment: Luhua Pool: Hidden Palace of Guizang Formula
152.content: A one-time domain entrance in Luhua Pool whose description promises treasure enough to drive a person mad, though few remain who can decipher its secrets. It contains two domains, Voyage to the Sanguine Sky and Travels of the Moonlit Venturer. It is one of three "Hidden Palace" domains named for ancient Chinese divination arts.

153.content:
Lumberpick Valley: Lumberpick Valley is a surface subarea of the Chasm in Liyue. Geograna, Seelie and spoutrocks lie among its rocks, Noctilucous Jade can be gathered, and it is crowded with hilichurls, Treasure Hoarders and a Ruin Hunter.

The Chinese name means Lumber-Picking Valley, which hints at woodcutting, though no text confirms it.

Geography: Features: Geograna, Seelie, Spoutrocks, Unique Rocks and Unique Rock Pillars. The local specialty is Noctilucous Jade.

Dangers: Elite enemies are Blazing Axe Mitachurls and Ruin Hunters. Common ones are ordinary and Electro Hilichurl Grenadiers and fighters, Anemo and Dendro Slimes, and many kinds of Treasure Hoarders (Marksmen, Pugilists, Scouts, Seamen and the three Potioneers).

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

154.content:
Mingxing Jewelry (also: Mingxing-zhai, Bright Star Studio, 明星斋): Mingxing Jewelry is a jewelry shop on Feiyun Slope in Liyue Harbor. The map calls it renowned, and says that in its prime its shelves were filled with gems shining like stars in the night sky. For reasons the game does not give, it now runs a side business swapping rare stones for the Geo Sigils that adventurers carry. The owner is Xingxi.

Its Chinese name, Mingxing-zhai, can be read as 'Bright Star Studio'; the wiki notes that 'mingxing' also means 'celebrity'.

Places: A single shopfront, set across the street from Xinyue Kiosk. Its stock is sold only for Geo Sigils, not Mora: gem slivers, a few ascension materials and weapon billets, and occasionally Mora itself, in exchange for sigils.

People: Xingxi is the owner and the only named person. The wiki describes her as a girl with long straight black hair and brown eyes, in a blue and white dress. No history, family or personality is given.

Atmosphere: A shop that remembers being grander than it is now: a polished storefront on a busy street, doing a quiet trade with adventurers instead of the high-end customers its name suggests.

Travel: Feiyun Slope, in the upper part of Liyue Harbor. Xinyue Kiosk is the nearest well-known neighbour.

Status as of 7.1: Open and trading as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

155.content: Xingxi owns Mingxing Jewelry. She takes only Geo Sigils as payment and sells gem slivers, certain ascension materials and weapon billets in return. Canon gives no further information on her.

156.content:
Mingyun Village (also: Mingyun): Mingyun Village is an abandoned mining village in Qiongji Estuary, Liyue. Its scattered ore deposits ran dry, and the miners moved west toward Liyue Harbor and the Chasm. Hilichurls now use the leftover facilities. A ghostly father haunts it in the quest The Tree who Stands Alone.

Three small mine tunnels around the village hold iron chunks, Noctilucous Jade and Cor Lapis. The Hidden Palace of Lianshan Formula domain lies near the village.

Geography: The village sits in Qiongji Estuary with its mining tunnels in the surrounding hills. Local specialties of the estuary include Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade, Qingxin and Violetgrass.

Places: Mining tunnels, a billboard, houses, including one with lost notes. Notices still pinned up announce the mine's closure.

People: No living residents remain. Yuan Hong is a ghost, father of three deceased sons, each of whom mistook his will for a treasure map: Yuan Cheng, Yuan Qing and Yuan Liang.

History: The mine was run by a mining crew until its ores failed; notices say the crew was to be re-dispatched to the Chasm. The date is not given.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mingyun Village is abandoned.

The mines are closed, hilichurls roam it, and Yuan Hong's ghost has departed after the quest.

157.content: Yuan Hong's will, left in verse, was misread by his three sons as a treasure map. They searched the mines instead of understanding it. The Traveler finds the will's four parts in the surrounding caves and follows it to a large tree. Treasure Hoarders arrive hoping for riches. The chest at the tree holds items Hong placed every year, showing that the family was the treasure.

158.content:
Minlin (also: Forest of Jade-Like Stone, Mínlín): Minlin ("Forest of Jade-Like Stone") is the cloud-wrapped mountain country of western Liyue, and the part of the nation that belongs to the adepti. Its peaks, karst spires and ruins hold Jueyun Karst, where the adepti are said to dwell; Mt. Aocang, Qingyun Peak and Mt. Hulao, abodes of individual adepti; Nantianmen, where a great tree seals an ancient dragon; and the old ruins of Tianqiu Valley and Cuijue Slope. Mortals rarely go up; those who do are usually herb gatherers or people seeking the adepti's blessing.

Legend, not law, keeps people out. Several slopes have barriers or amber traps, and the adepti's presence is more felt than seen.

Geography: Layered stone peaks ringed by cloud in the west and northwest of Liyue, best viewed from far away at Wangshu Inn. Huaguang Stone Forest lies in the middle, bounded by Mt. Aocang to the north, Qingyun Peak to the east and Mt. Hulao to the southwest. Nantianmen and its sealing tree stand near Mt. Hulao; Tianqiu Valley and Cuijue Slope lie among the ruins and valleys beyond.

Places: Jueyun Karst is the traditional realm of the adepti; Taishan Mansion, a residence 'established by royal decree' whose path was lost to mortals, lies there, now flooded. Mt. Aocang was the domain of Cloud Retainer. Qingyun Peak is the home of Moon Carver. Mt. Hulao is the abode of Mountain Shaper, studded with amber rock. Nantianmen holds the Dragon-Queller. Tianqiu Valley is a ruined ancient settlement. Cuijue Slope guards the Nine Pillars of Peace.

History: The adepti gathered here after serving Morax in the Archon War. In the distant past the dragon Azhdaha raged north from the Chasm to Nantianmen before being sealed in the tree by Morax and three adepti, and Tianqiu Valley's settlement was lost around the same ancient rampage. Cloud Retainer lived alone on Mt. Aocang after the war until the events of A Thousand Moonlit Miles (4.4), when she took up residence in Liyue Harbor.

Travel: Teleport waypoints on the peaks let you reach each abode and Nantianmen. Climbing up is routine for Herb Gatherers; mysterious barriers seal the abodes on Qingyun Peak and Mt. Hulao.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the adepti still keep their mountain abodes, but Cloud Retainer now lives in Liyue Harbor and Xiao watches the Chasm at Rex Lapis's order.

After the 7.1 anomaly in which the Celestial Nails across Teyvat began shining, Xiao says additional Millelith patrol the Chasm and Cloud Retainer and the other adepti have begun investigating.

159.content: The Dragon-Queller is a vast tree with blue-veined bark near Mt. Hulao and Nantianmen. It seals Azhdaha, an ancient Geo dragon who once befriended Morax before erosion ate away his memory and he began harming humans; Morax and the adepti fought him from the Chasm north to Nantianmen. A stone tablet erected by Mountain Shaper begs passersby not to disturb it. Before Zhongli's story quest, an NPC named Jiu worshipped him and prophesied his return; in the quest she is revealed as a vessel of Azhdaha's rage, and he is defeated and resealed.

160.comment: Minlin: Mt. Aocang and Cloud Retainer
160.content: Mt. Aocang was the domain of the adeptus Cloud Retainer (Xianyun) during the long isolation that followed the Archon War, until A Thousand Moonlit Miles. Its stone table is engraved for three seats: Retainer, Guizhong and Rex. Ruins-treasure monuments near the Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain record a former disciple of the mountain's doubts about whether monsters are truly evil and whether mortals and adepti are truly good; the disciple's identity is not given. Cloud Retainer also made the Dwelling in the Clouds above Qingyun Peak.

161.comment: Minlin: Cuijue Slope and the Nine Pillars of Peace
161.content: The Nine Pillars of Peace stand around a temple on Cuijue Slope. Legend says they were raised to hold nine human desires at bay (greed, nostalgia, vision, jealousy, anger, lust, self-aggrandizement, competition and turmoil) and that breaking them would bring war again; the inscription nonetheless tells any who do open it to take the treasures within and defend Liyue. Nine Stones of Remembrance, earned by offering Geoculi to the Statues of the Seven, break the seals. The shrine's door insignia is unique and little is known of the pillars even in Liyue folklore.

162.content: Tianqiu Valley was once a prosperous settlement in the ancient past; three ruined towers stand on its west side. It seems to have fallen during the rampage of an ancient dragon king, whom Rex Lapis and his adepti imprisoned in an adeptal realm, and the dragon's servants fled into the earth to sleep until his return. How the valley came to ruin is not told in detail.

163.content:
Mt. Aocang (also: Mount Aocang): Mt. Aocang is the mountain of the adeptus Cloud Retainer, one of the great peaks of Jueyun Karst in Minlin. After the Archon War she lived here in seclusion behind a sealed abode, and pilgrims who sought her blessing mostly went away empty-handed. Today she lives in Liyue Harbor as the mechanic Xianyun, but the mountain is still hers.

Its heart is a lake with a stone table laid for three, where offerings are left for the adepti. The Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain lies on its north side. A tablet describes Cloud Retainer as the Free Adeptus, who performs no action and sets no rule.

Geography: A tall mountain in Minlin, in the adeptal highlands of Jueyun Karst. A stairway climbs to a lake at the top, in the middle of which stands a stone table with three chairs. The Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain lies to the north.

Places: - The lake and stone table: three chairs marked "Retainer", "Guizhong" and "Rex". Retainer's has a wine jar, Guizhong's a bowl and chopsticks, and Rex's nothing.
- Cloud Retainer's abode: a dwelling of mechanisms, entered after an offering is made at the table.
- The Clear Pool and Mountain Cavern domain.
- Ruin-treasure monuments of a disciple's story.

People: Cloud Retainer, an adeptus in the form of a crane, who now lives in Liyue Harbor as Xianyun. Her disciples Ganyu and Shenhe grew up under her care; Shenhe was taken in as a child. A wild crane called Yuandai once followed her faithfully here.

Culture: Pilgrims have come to Mt. Aocang since ancient times in search of adeptal blessings, and most returned empty-handed. Offerings of cooked dishes are left at the stone table.

History: After the Archon War, Cloud Retainer settled on Mt. Aocang and lived in isolation. The table's three chairs suggest she, Guizhong and Rex Lapis once dined here as friends (an inference from the engraved names). She and Guizhong quarrelled over ideals, yet after Guizhong's death she finished Guizhong's Ballista in her memory. In the Archon Quest of 1.0 the Traveler offered her dishes at the stone table and crossed her abode to speak to her.

Atmosphere: Quiet and remote, high above the sea of clouds, with a lake, a laid table and stairs that feel like a place meant for visits that rarely happen.

Dangers: Geovishaps, their hatchlings and Eyes of the Storm. Mortals regard the adepti's peaks as forbidden, and uninvited visitors may not be welcome.

Travel: Reached by the mountain path and stairs from Jueyun Karst; the abode itself opens only after an offering is made at the stone table.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Aocang is still Cloud Retainer's mountain. She keeps her abode but lives in Liyue Harbor as Xianyun.

No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the mountain. Xianyun is a playable character.

164.comment: Mt. Aocang: Cloud Retainer's Abode and the Stone Table
164.content: Cloud Retainer, the Free Adeptus, keeps a mechanical abode on Mt. Aocang, sealed by a talisman barrier. A stone table by the lake is set with three chairs for herself, Guizhong and Rex Lapis. When the Traveler arrived with a Sigil of Permission she sensed it and, moved by their sincere dishes, let them find their way through her abode to an audience. She is an expert in mechanical contraptions. Old records describe her human form as elegant in purple robes and her crane form as flying gracefully among the clouds; as Xianyun she has black updone hair and wears red-rimmed spectacles.

165.content:
Mt. Hulao (also: Amber-Prison Mountain): Mt. Hulao is a mountain in Minlin, Liyue, near the Dragon-Queller and Nantianmen, and the abode of the adeptus Mountain Shaper, a red-and-orange crane. Its slopes are guarded by karst crawlers, flowers he planted whose hidden roots wrap anything that steps on them in amber; breaking the amber frees whatever was trapped, whether treasure or an enemy. A large sealed cave near the pond is his dwelling, and when the Traveler first comes the adeptus is away.

It is where the Traveler meets Mountain Shaper in the first Archon Quest chapter. The name Hulao is rendered "Amber-Prison Mountain" by the wiki.

Geography: A subarea of Minlin. The path up the mountain winds past ambers; at the top stands a large talisman-sealed barrier in front of a pond and a sealed cave. The Huaguang Stone Forest lies to its northeast. Local specialties: Cor Lapis and Qingxin.

Places: The sealed cave and pond at the top (the Mountain Shaper's abode); the mountain road lined with Amber Rock; a pagoda northeast of the waypoint.

People: Mountain Shaper, an adeptus who first appears as a crane and has a human form of a bespectacled young man with a red streak in his dark hair (a human alias, Jiehu, appears in later event content). Two brothers, Li Ding and Li Dang, appear in the Archon Quest: poor men who came to hunt for treasure in the amber and were caught.

History: Mountain Shaper was one of the adepti summoned by Morax to fight in the Archon War. He explains that he planted the karst crawlers after settling here so that the mountain's tranquillity would not be disturbed; over the years they have prevented many disturbances but also trapped many curious things. He says that as the people of Liyue prospered, the adepti withdrew gradually into the mountains as a gesture of good will. According to the wiki's summary of Qiqi's character story, he once imprisoned the girl Qiqi in amber when she went on a rampage after the adepti revived her.

Dangers: Amber Rock that traps travelers and may release enemies or treasure; Abyss mages; ordinary hilichurl camps.

Quests: Moulder of Mountains (Archon Quest, Chapter I, Act I: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths). Moon Carver sends the Traveler here to Mountain Shaper with a Sigil of Permission.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Hulao is unchanged. Mountain Shaper left to convene with the other adepti in Chapter I, and he reappears in later seasonal event content.

166.comment: Mt. Hulao: Mountain Shaper at Mt. Hulao
166.content: Mountain Shaper is the adeptus of Mt. Hulao, formally known as the Perfected Lord who Guides the Waters and Shapes the Mountains (the wiki's translation of his Chinese title). His character page belongs in the NPC entry; here, note only that he protects the mountain by planting karst crawlers and speaks in the formal impersonal "one" of the older adepti.

167.content:
Mt. Laixin (also: Laixin, the sacred mountain, Láixīn-shān): Mt. Laixin ("the sacred mountain") is the peak where Chenyu Vale's spirit veins converge, so whoever controls it can control every acre of the vale. It was sealed until the 4.4 quest An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade opened it. On it stand Chiwang Terrace, an altar copied from the ancient city of Lang-Gan, and Carp's Rest, the abode of the carp adeptus Fujin, with the Votive Rainjade where offerings are made.

It is the only area on the world map without a Statue of the Seven.

Geography: A mountain in the vale's heart. Before it is unlocked, entering the area turns the view red and triggers an out-of-bounds reaction; the map shows it as colorless rather than red. Chiwang Terrace is on the summit; Carp's Rest is an adeptal abode on the mountain.

Places: Chiwang Terrace: a jade-styled altar, unlocked by An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade. Carp's Rest: Fujin's abode, unlocked in The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose. Votive Rainjade: the offering site in Carp's Rest.

History: Fujin hurled the Votive Rainjade from Mt. Lingmeng to quell the mistress's flood in the Archon War and then sank, losing power, into Carp's Rest, where for thousands of years she could only reminisce about the outside world through the scent of tea offerings. In 4.4 the Traveler found that Lingyuan, who longed for her old friend, was disturbing the spirit veins to restore the vale to nature; she yielded after defeat and Fujin performed the Rainjade Rite.

Travel: Locked until An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade; afterwards open. Carp's Rest requires finishing The Cloud-Padded Path to the Chiwang Repose, a quest available one in-game day after the earlier one.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Laixin is open to travelers; Fujin rests at Carp's Rest and Lingyuan presides over the vale.

Fujin can also be found outside Qiaoying with Lingyuan or Little Mao after completing Rainjade's Benediction.

168.comment: Mt. Laixin: Carp's Rest and Fujin
168.content: Carp's Rest is Fujin's abode on Mt. Laixin, the hidden refuge she retreated to after the war, "sinking into the sea" and losing much of her strength. Fujin, a giant golden carp who took human form, was worshiped as an adeptus and was close to humans. The Traveler first met her there in Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, when she lent them adeptal energy. After performing the Rainjade Rite she is back at Carp's Rest, in her carp form, to recover.

169.content: The Votive Rainjade is a jade where Chenyu Vale's ancestors once offered jade by casting it into water, transferring adeptal energy to the spirit veins to guard their homeland and bring favorable weather and harvests. The old rite has long been forgotten, but if the lost adeptal energy is gathered into the jade again, the soil and water might be blessed anew. Offering Spirit Carp to the jade raises Rainjade's Benediction and unlocks rewards.

170.content:
Mt. Lingmeng (also: Past Glories of Wangshan): Mt. Lingmeng is a mountain in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale, Liyue, west of Qiaoying Village and southeast of Yilong Wharf. Its main landmark is Wangshan Hall, the weathered stronghold of the Guhua Clan, a martial school whose glory has faded. Local folklore also places an ancient cave and old spirits of the vale beneath its waterfalls.

The mountain, introduced in Version 4.4, is also the place from which, in the vale's history, the adeptus Fujin threw the Votive Rainjade into the water to save the people.

Geography: A subarea of Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale. Wangshan Hall (a main hall and a secret chamber) is the area's only listed point of interest. An Ancient Cave beneath the northwest waterfall holds a mural, once cleaned, showing the people of Chenyu Vale performing the Votive Rainjade ritual.

Places: Wangshan Hall: the stronghold of the Guhua Clan, in disrepair because of the clan's decline. Huang the Third, a clan member, tries to raise money for its restoration by luring people at Yilong Wharf to tour it with exaggerated claims of its majesty.

People: Guhua Clan members live at and around the hall: Huang the Third, Wen the Fourth and others, a handful of practitioners trying to restore the clan's reputation.

History: At the end of the Archon War, in the story of An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade, the mistress of Chenyu Vale unleashed a flood down the Bishui River. Herblord fought her while Lingyuan led the people to shelter, and Fujin climbed Mt. Lingmeng and hurled the Votive Rainjade into the waters; the flood was stopped, though Fujin lost much of her strength. The cave murals on the mountain depict the rite.

Quests: World quests Scrolls and Sword Manuals of Guhua (Arcane Archive puzzle) and Shrouded Vale, Hidden Hero (a trial and an ancient sword), plus A Wangshan Walk to Remember. A hidden exploration objective, Wangshan Swordsman's Inscriptions, is also tied to the hall.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Lingmeng is unchanged, and the Guhua Clan still maintains Wangshan Hall as a modest school. No later story content was found that alters it.

171.comment: Mt. Lingmeng: Wangshan Hall and the Guhua Clan
171.content: Wangshan Hall is the base and main training ground of the Guhua Clan. It has a main hall and a secret chamber, and is kept up by the few members who remain. The clan's motto, as quoted by its former member Chen the Sharp, is that the noblest martial virtue is to pursue what benefits other people. Xingqiu counts as a member with the title Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame.

172.content:
Mt. Mingyuan (also: Mount Mingyuan): Mt. Mingyuan is a mountain in Chenyu Vale's Upper Vale in Liyue. It stands west of Yilong Wharf and east of Fontaine, directly under Celestia, whose floating island is visible straight overhead. The world quest The Dealing Sands begins here.

A Millelith camp lies on its southern slope, and a beach to its west was the setting for a sting against smugglers.

Geography: The wiki places it west of Yilong Wharf, east of Fontaine and under Celestia; a Treasure Hoarder camp sits west of the southern waypoint. The page lists Iron Dou'er as its NPC.

People: Iron Dou'er, Iron Chuan'er and other "Iron" Treasure Hoarders loiter about the beach west of the mountain; Dou'er and Chuan'er turn out to be Millelith in disguise. At a Millelith camp on the southern slope the quest page lists Hongyu, Qingye (both in hoarder outfits) and Yijun.

History: In The Dealing Sands the Millelith spent about a month infiltrating the Iron and Salt Gang, which was smuggling goods to buyers from Fontaine. When the Traveler stumbled onto a deal at the beach, the Millelith revealed themselves, fought Johnnie and Iron Ming, and arrested the smugglers. They paid the Traveler in Mora and said such helpers should be rewarded so that others would help too.

Quests: The Dealing Sands starts at Mt. Mingyuan with Iron Dou'er. The player goes to the beach beneath the cliff, joins talks between the two parties, defeats Johnnie and then Iron Ming, and speaks to the Millelith. It rewards the achievement Breaking Iron and Stone.

Dangers: Treasure Hoarders are present, though the "hoarders" at the camp and beach are mostly Millelith in costume; real hoarders and Fontainian smugglers appear in the quest.

Status as of 7.1: The smuggling ring is broken and its leaders arrested; nothing later changes it as of 7.1.

173.content: In The Dealing Sands, Millelith agents posing as the Iron and Salt Gang's Treasure Hoarders caught the real gang boss and a Fontainian buyer from the Pinky Club on a Mt. Mingyuan beach, with the Traveler's help.

174.content:
Mt. Tianheng (also: Mount Tianheng, Tianheng): Mt. Tianheng is the mountain range that shelters Liyue Harbor from the west and north, a natural shield for the city. Old tablets say Rex Lapis raised it when he first came down to Liyue, and that the first people there mined jade from its depths. Today it holds the Golden House, where Mora is minted, Blackcliff Forge, the Guizhong Ballista and the cliff-side district of Yujing Terrace.

In-game description calls it the pride of the range that shelters the harbor, a natural shield against anyone who comes from the west. Records speak of many wars where enemies were stopped by it, and the old walls, forts and defences are still visible.

Geography: The map labels the peaks west of Liyue Harbor as Mt. Tianheng. The wiki points out that the range north of the harbor, which the road to Guili Plains crosses, is also part of it. Yujing Terrace is built along its cliffside, and Chihu Rock connects to it on the west by bridge.

Places: - The Golden House: the mint where all of Teyvat's Mora is made.
- Blackcliff Forge: the workshops that gave their name to the Blackcliff and Prototype weapon series.
- The Guizhong Ballista: an ancient automatic crossbow.
- The Jade Chamber: the Qixing's floating palace, here classed as part of Mt. Tianheng.
- Yujing Terrace, built into the cliffs.

History: According to Stone Tablet Compilations, Rex Lapis lowered the tides, raised Mt. Tianheng and calmed the waves when he first descended. People cut into the mountain, found jade and built a settlement they named Shanhui Fort ("Mountain Splendor Fort"); everyone prospered from the mines. The goddess Guizhong set up the Guizhong Ballista to guard it. Later Guizhong led her people north of the range to the Guili Plains. After she fell in the Archon War, Rex Lapis led his people south of Mt. Tianheng, where Liyue Harbor was founded.

People: Blackcliff Forge workers and miners; Gongming and Millelith guards at the Golden House; Treasure Hoarders, Fatui skirmishers and other enemies in the ruins.

Dangers: Fatui Skirmishers (Geochanter Bracers and Electrohammer Vanguards), hilichurl shooters, samachurls, slimes, Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls and Ruin Hunters wander the range. The Guizhong Ballista fires on perceived threats, including Treasure Hoarders approaching the ruins.

Travel: Liyue Harbor lies at the foot of the range. The main road from the north runs through Mt. Tianheng and arrives at Feiyun Slope. Another road leaves the city from Yujing Terrace past the Guizhong Ballista.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Mt. Tianheng still shelters Liyue Harbor, with the Golden House no longer minting. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

The Golden House no longer mints Mora since the Geo Gnosis was handed to the Tsaritsa. The Jade Chamber has been rebuilt (2.4).

175.content: The Golden House is where all of Teyvat's Mora is minted. After the Rite of Descension the Qixing moved the dead god's body, the Exuvia, here. The Traveler faced Childe there before Osial's attack. After Rex Lapis handed his Gnosis to the Tsaritsa, it stopped minting new Mora.

176.content: Blackcliff Forge is known as the birthplace of the Blackcliff and Prototype series weapons and also makes White Tassels. Its workshops and furnaces were carved into the mountains and joined by tunnels. Mountain tribes are said to have sheltered in the tunnels in wartime and unexplored passages lead to an ancient underground realm. The Yun family's founder is credited with first tunnelling through these mountains.

177.content: A giant automatic crossbow built by Guizhong, the late Goddess of Dust, and the adepti to protect Liyue. It fires at any perceived threat nearby, even Treasure Hoarders. After Guizhong's death Cloud Retainer finished it in her memory. A notice at the supply post says its spare parts should only be collected by a worthy craftsman if "that ancient evil" returns. Replica ballistae were used against Osial at the Jade Chamber, and enhanced ones against Beisht at Guyun Stone Forest.

178.content:
Mt. Xuanlian (also: Mount Xuanlian): Mt. Xuanlian is a peak in Chenyu Vale's Southern Mountain in Liyue, south of Chizhang Wall and Yaodie Valley. It is admired for strange rock and sunset views, and a nearby cave holds the blessed water sought in a world quest.

A viewpoint here is called Clear Skies Over Xuanlian. The Hezhe Post photography contest names the mountain as one of its four subjects.

Geography: South of Chizhang Wall and south of Yaodie Valley; reached by a shortcut from Yaodie Valley through a cave. Pressure plates in a cave near the mountain hide a Sacred Simulacrum.

People: Akai, a contest competitor in Our Chenyu Vale Trek, is menaced by monsters on the mountain and shares his best photo spot with the Traveler.

History: The viewpoint text quotes a short line of verse: the weighty winds blow, the day is dark, but the cascading falls run clear. A competitor's scenery guide in Our Chenyu Vale Trek says you rarely see such strange mountains elsewhere and that the sunset there is "truly moving".

Quests: Our Chenyu Vale Trek (photograph the mountain between 17:00 and 18:00 for Picture: Mt. Xuanlian) and The Roaming Abode (draw blessed water at the cave). The viewpoint is Clear Skies Over Xuanlian.

Dangers: Hilichurls near the quest photo spot; monsters in the shortcut cave that wounded a villager in The Roaming Abode.

Status as of 7.1: Unchanged as of 7.1.

179.content:
Nameless Ruins (also: Wúmíng Yíjì, Nameless Ruins of the Chasm): The Nameless Ruins are an area of ancient, unnamed ruins in the Underground Mines under the Chasm in Liyue. Mounds of dark mud cover the floor, and the roof of the cavern bears an upside-down ruin with a water pool: the Inverted City, an old Lang-Gan site. The mines' travellers meet Abyss mages, Ruin Guards and hilichurls here.

The Nameless Ruins are where the Archon Quest of Chapter II brings the Traveler and Dainsleif deep below the Chasm.

Geography: A set of halls, stairs and sealed sections in the Underground Mines. The floor holds solid dark-mud mounds, luminous Seelie wander the dark, and Oozing Concretions and Noctilucous Jade grow here. A purple barrier closed off the Inverted City until "The Grave of the Guarded".

Dangers: Elite Abyss mages (Electro, Hydro, Pyro), Ruin Guards and Ruin Graders, Black Serpent Knights and Shadowy Husks, plus Hilichurls, Floating Hydro Fungus, Cryo Whopperflowers and Geo Slimes.

Quests: "Requiem of the Echoing Depths" (Chapter II Act IV, 2.6), especially "The Grave of the Guarded"; it also lies on the way for "Perilous Trail" in the Chasm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 a dark, mostly empty set of ruins under a partly reopened mine.

180.content:
Nantianmen (also: Southern Heavenly Gate): Nantianmen is the northwestern corner of Minlin, where an enormous tree with glowing blue veins, the Dragon-Queller, rises from the rocks. Beneath it lies the Geo dragon Azhdaha, an ancient friend of Rex Lapis that the adepti sealed after erosion drove him mad. A stone tablet by the tree asks passers-by not to disturb the evil dragon beneath.

The tablet reads that life endures in Heaven and Earth thanks to the merciful Adeptus, and that an evil dragon lies here. The Dragon-Queller is described as a tree that the dragon is slowly merging with. The name means "Southern Heavenly Gate", a term in Chinese myth for the gate between mortal and heavenly realms.

Geography: Nantianmen lies in the northwest of Minlin, near Mt. Hulao. The Dragon-Queller is a massive tree whose branches flow with cold moonlight; at its tip a large blue branch points straight toward Liyue Harbor and cannot be climbed. Bright yellow flowers grow around its base.

Places: - The Dragon-Queller, the tree that seals Azhdaha, with the Moonlit Tree viewpoint.
- The stone tablet at the tree's foot, erected by Mountain Shaper as a warning.
- Beneath the Dragon-Queller: the domain in the earth under the tree where Azhdaha is fought.

People: Jiu, a young-looking girl who was Azhdaha's vessel, was seen here before the events of Zhongli's story quest. The miners of the Chasm were lured here. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver sealed the dragon long ago.

History: Azhdaha, a Geo dragon ruling much of what is now Liyue, was woken from a long sleep and gained sight from Morax, whom he befriended and swore never to harm Liyue. Erosion made him forget, and mining in the Chasm hurt the ley lines and drove him into a rage. Morax, Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and another adeptus fought him from the Chasm north to Nantianmen. With a shred of sanity he accepted his fate, and was sealed in the Dragon-Queller. Mountain Shaper set up the tablet.

Atmosphere: A strange, moonlit stillness around a vast living tree whose branches glow cold blue, with a feeling that something huge is waiting beneath. The viewpoint text says its roots reach into the heart of the earth, perhaps joined to something that awaits an opportunity to emerge and bask in moonlight.

Dangers: Hilichurls, Cryo and Geo slimes, Treasure Hoarders, Eremites, Stonehide Lawachurls, Rock Shieldwall Mitachurls and Ruin Hunters wander the area. The deeper danger is the sealed dragon, whose seal weakened over time.

Travel: The tree stands between Mt. Hulao and Nantianmen proper. The Trounce Domain beneath it is entered through the tree.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Azhdaha remains sealed under the Dragon-Queller after being resealed in 1.5. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes the site.

Jiu faded away, and the benevolent remnant said goodbye to Morax.

181.content: Azhdaha is an ancient earth dragon, once Morax's friend and ally in the Archon War. Erosion made him forget Morax and mortals; when miners damaged the ley lines in the Chasm he attacked humans, and Morax and the adepti sealed him in the Dragon-Queller. Centuries later his vessel Jiu tried to free him. He was beaten by the Traveler, Zhongli and his own benevolent remnant, and resealed. The tablet by the tree was set up by Mountain Shaper to warn the world.

182.content:
Nine Pillars of Peace: The Nine Pillars of Peace are nine ancient stone pillars standing on Cuijue Slope in Minlin, Liyue, around a ruin and a temple at the centre of the area. In-game viewpoint text says nine shackles of stone were said to be laid deep in the valleys there to drive off evil and cleanse the world.

Approaching them darkens the sky: when a player nears the pillars, the area turns grey and the land outside Cuijue Slope looks unnaturally dim until they leave the vicinity.

Quests: The world quest Nine Pillars of Peace is started at the stone tablet in the middle of Cuijue Slope. The Traveler gathers nine Stones of Remembrance by making offerings to Statues of the Seven in Liyue, then climbs each pillar and sets a stone into its face-like tile. Doing so opens the central ruin, where the Traveler must defeat Ruin Guard and other guardians to reach its treasure room.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 nothing further has been revealed about the pillars; they remain a relic of old Liyue, raised to suppress conflict per the quest tablets, with no builder named.

183.content:
Northland Bank (Liyue) (also: Liyue Northland Bank, Northland Bank Liyue branch): The Northland Bank (Liyue) is the Liyue Harbor branch of the Northland Bank, the Snezhnayan bank with branches around Teyvat. It stands on Feiyun Slope and is the only non-local bank in Liyue. The Fatui use Northland Bank funds abroad and sometimes its branches as bases, and in the Liyue Archon Quest this branch is where the Traveler meets Childe's contact Ekaterina and where Childe arranges to meet them.

The branch is staffed by a manager, a receptionist, guards and the occasional customer. It is also the stop from which Childe sends the Traveler on to Liuli Pavilion, where he has arranged a dinner with Zhongli.

Places: The bank has a public hall inside, where the receptionist works at her desk and the manager is found by day, and a back room behind it. Guards stand outside. It sits on Feiyun Slope in upper Liyue Harbor, just above the Heyu Tea House.

People: Andrei is the manager and is inside only by day. Ekaterina is the receptionist and is present day and night; she greets the Traveler as a friend of Childe and passes on his messages. Vlad guards the door by day and Nadia (the Liyue guard) by night. A customer, Mister Qi, is inside by day.

Governance: The Northland Bank belongs to Snezhnaya. Later canon (7.0) says Pantalone is in charge of its operations as a whole, though other Harbingers may handle the opening of new branches. The Liyue branch operates openly in Liyue Harbor as a bank, even though Fatui business passes through it.

History: After the Rite of Descension Childe uses the bank as the place where the Traveler can find him once he is free of the Millelith. Back from visiting the adepti, the Traveler and Paimon find that the Qixing have hidden the Geo Archon's vessel. Childe has promised to find someone to break the stalemate, so they visit the bank again. Ekaterina says Childe has kept his side of the agreement and that he is at Liuli Pavilion; there he introduces Zhongli. The final visit is in The Fond Farewell, in search of Zhongli.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the branch remains open in Liyue Harbor as one of the Northland Bank's overseas branches.

No later canon changes it. In 7.0 the Snezhnograd headquarters and the bank's founding by Pantalone were shown; that history belongs to the main bank, not this branch.

184.content: Staff seen in the Liyue branch: Andrei, the manager (daytime, inside); Ekaterina, the receptionist (inside, day and night); Mister Qi, a customer (daytime); Vlad, a guard outside by day; Nadia, a guard outside at night. Ekaterina is the one who deals with the Traveler on Childe's behalf.

185.comment: Northland Bank (Liyue): Northland Bank as the Fatui's Foreign Base
185.content: Loading-screen text says the Northland Bank has branches in many places; when the Fatui operate outside Snezhnaya they use funds provided by the bank and even use it as a base. Pantalone founded the bank shortly after becoming a Harbinger and is in charge of its operations. Loans are generous but must be repaid in full and on time, and the Fatui have a debt-collection division for those who default.

186.content:
Pearl Galley (also: The Pearl Galley): The Pearl Galley is a luxurious ship anchored near Liyue Harbor in the Sea of Clouds, meant for the exclusive enjoyment of specially invited guests. Its receptionist is Luoxia and its proprietor is Rouran.

Guests are expected to come by invitation; the Traveler's first boarding without one is handled gently by Luoxia. Once The Ocean Pearl is done, the ferryman Pinghai can take the Traveler to and from the ship.

People: Aboard are the receptionist Luoxia, the poet Li the Ninth, Cui'er, Guan Hong, Luo Feng, Maksim and Qiu'ge, with Uncle Zhao as daytime security. Pinghai ferries visitors from Liyue Harbor.

Culture: A scroll on one table, the Connoisseur Catalog, offers the ship's "wares of beauty" in poetic language and lists the names of the "flowers" of the painted boat. The wiki reads these as the names of hostesses who can be hired to keep guests company. The catalogue's line about the beauty of water lying in the pearls it holds echoes a classical Chinese essay on literature.

Quests: Boarding for the first time triggers the world quest The Ocean Pearl. The ship is also the starting point of Zhongli's story quest Shadow of Yore, the first part of Sal Flore, where Zhongli is discussing Rex Lapis and the first Mora with guests at a table and the Traveler meets Wanyan at the stern. If The Ocean Pearl is not yet complete, it starts first and both quests can proceed together.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Pearl Galley remains moored near Liyue Harbor.

187.content:
Pervases' Temple (also: Temple of Pervases): Pervases' Temple is a small temple in Lisha dedicated to Pervases, a Yaksha who died in the Archon War, and holds a statue of him. It began as a run-down house, then was restored through the Hereafter quests. Wang Ping'an, once the false adeptus Starsnatcher, now keeps it and gives out incense for visitors to offer to the statue.

Pervases was a junior Yaksha who served Rex Lapis and perished during the Archon War. The temple is where his spirit lingered in a crane statue, and where Xiao is moved by the loss of his fellow Yakshas.

Places: Before restoration the temple looks like a dilapidated house in poor repair, with Treasure Hoarders nearby. After the quests it is repaired and tidy, with a censer and a statue of Pervases. The statue shows an illuminated beast form, a crane wearing a large-bead necklace like the one Xiao wears.

People: Wang Ping'an looks after the temple, hands out incense and says few people come, that the temple is off the beaten track and he wonders how to let people know it is there. He is writing a book about Xiao, the Vigilant Yaksha, and collects evidence for the stories.

History: In Xiao's story quest Butterfly's Dream, Pervases performs the Mortal Lingering ritual with a censer and seven-star lamps to see modern Liyue, then permits the Traveler to take them, knowing that dispels his ritual. He senses the karmic burden Xiao bears, tells them the truth about himself and leaves a message for Xiao before going dormant. Starsnatcher, now Wang Ping'an, repents, repays his followers and later sets out to restore the temple. In Hereafter the Traveler buys grilled tiger fish near Wanmin Restaurant and brings a serving for Pervases. They find Wang Ping'an attacked by hilichurls and Treasure Hoarders and help him; across the three quests of the series the temple is rebuilt, and he stays on as its keeper. After Rex Lapis saves Xiao in The Chasm, Xiao returns to the temple to think about the fate of the Yakshas.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the temple stands restored in Lisha under Wang Ping'an's care.

No later canon changes it.

188.content: Pervases was a junior Yaksha under Rex Lapis, who gave him the name. He died during the Archon War and a thousand years later, on the anniversary, performed the Mortal Lingering ritual to see modern Liyue. His favourite food was grilled fish, and he is shown as a man with short slicked-back black hair or, in statue form, a crane. His spirit lies dormant in the statue at the temple.

189.comment: Pervases' Temple: Wang Ping'an and Starsnatcher
189.content: Wang Ping'an posed as the adeptus Starsnatcher, using a Sigil of Permission and an ornate mask, until Xiao's story quest exposed him as a fake. He repented, repaid his followers and, in Hereafter, rebuilt Pervases' temple. He remains there as its keeper and is writing a book on Xiao.

190.content:
Qiaoying Village (also: Qiaoying): Qiaoying Village is a mountain village in Chenyu Vale, north-western Liyue, close to the Fontaine border. It is known throughout Teyvat for high-quality tea, sold in Liyue Harbor and exported to other nations, and is home to the Chunming Teaworks. Its architecture is inspired by real-world Hui-style buildings.

Locals credit the blessing of the adepti on Chenyu Vale's land and water for the ideal tea-growing conditions. A special cauldron, said to be an adeptal mechanism, roasts the leaves and gives them their aroma.

Geography: Qiaoying sits in the Upper Vale of Chenyu Vale, the Liyue subregion around Mt. Yaojun, with significant numbers of tea trees planted around the village. It has docks. The vale is humid compared with the Hills of Barsom.

Places: The Chunming Teaworks is the best-known workshop: it combines methods passed down for thousands of years with the newest tea-drying and roasting machines, and its reputation extends well beyond the village. The Yanshang Teahouse employs an evaluator and hired muscle, and the docks have a handful of workers.

People: Ding Sr. and Ding Jr. work inside the Chunming Teaworks and Jin stands outside it. Hanquan (hired muscle) and Qianyun (evaluator) work at the Yanshang Teahouse. Other residents include Grandpa Lu, Uncle Luo, Leong, Moyan and Muli; the researcher Djarkutan is also in the village. Fujin, one of the vale's adepti, and Lingyuan appear here at times.

Culture: Tea is life here. Cultivars named in canon include Dipped Dew, Tianheng Bohea, Qiaoying floral tea, Sunglo Tea and Single-Origin Yauwan Tea. The village performs an annual tea-serving ceremony, using the wilted petals of Spiritscent Flowers to prepare floral tea.

History: Chenyu Vale's first human settlements were founded some 6,000 years ago by tribes fleeing the Chasm, guided by Fujin. Its tea later became famous in Liyue Harbor and elsewhere. Qiaoying itself is described mainly through its tea trade.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qiaoying is peaceful, with its tea quality restored.

Fujin remains in carp form after the repair, and some miasma lingers elsewhere in the vale.

191.content: A tea-processing workshop famous well beyond Qiaoying Village. It uses millennia-old methods alongside modern machines for drying and roasting, which may explain the village's renown. Ding Sr. and Ding Jr. work inside.

192.content:
Qingce Village (also: Qingce, Mt. Qingce, Mount Qingce): Qingce Village is a tranquil village at the foot of Mt. Qingce in Bishui Plain, at Liyue's northern edge, with clear water and terraced fields of flowers. Many younger residents have left for livelier places such as Liyue Harbor, so it has become something of a retirement spot. It is led, in all but title, by Granny Ruoxin.

According to legend, the serpent god Chi once nested here before Morax slew it and sealed its power. "Qingce" is said to be an ancient name of the Chi itself.

Geography: Houses are simply built, mostly of wood with blue roofs, on terraces cut into the mountain. The mountain is described as cradling the village and its croplands. Crescent-shaped water paddies sit between hills and bamboo forests, with cloud banks in the valleys, and the wind makes the paddy water ripple in many colours.

Places: The community centre is where Granny Ruoxin is found. Ms. Bai owns the mill, Pops Kai a tea shop and Master Lu the Fanmu Carpenter shop, and there is a market. The Qingce Village Bulletin Board carries local posts. The Vault of Qingce lies hidden to the north-west.

People: Granny Ruoxin is the community leader and not an official village chief; the name stuck. Others include Little Liu, Little Xing, Little You, Little Zuo and Little Yi, Pops Kai, Master Lu, Ms. Bai, the herb gatherer Zhi, Hanfeng, Jiangcheng, Dongdong, Chang the Ninth and Uncle Ghast.

Culture: Village life is gentle and slow, with food and water in plenty. The elderly raise their grandchildren while the young work in Liyue Harbor and beyond.

History: Thousands of years ago the Chi made its nest on Mt. Qingce and seized the region. Morax fought it at a great height and killed it, but its power seeped into the land, so he subdued each aspect of it in turn: spirit, bones, flesh, soul and form, bound in different directions. He taught the villagers to erect Geo statues to crush what remained. The magic formula of the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula is said to have bound it.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qingce Village is quiet, mostly elderly, and unchanged by recent main-story events.

Granny Ruoxin still lives in the village. The Chi remains a legend that few still remember.

193.content: Ruoxin leads Qingce Village's community centre. She grew up in Liyue Harbor, was an actress at the Heyu Tea House alongside Fan Er'ye, and came to the countryside seeking a simpler life. She wonders whether her lost lover would like the village and has stopped waiting, although she says she does not regret their love. She is kind, wry, and enjoys gossip and Genius Invokation. She is a gentle storyteller who remembers things most people have forgotten, like the old tale of the Geo Lord suppressing the Chi.

194.comment: Qingce Village: The Chi of Qingce
194.content: The Chi was a serpent god or dragon-like monster of Mt. Qingce, defeated by Morax. Its power seeped into the land afterward. Morax subdued it facet by facet, spirit in the north, bones south-east, flesh north-west, soul north-east, form south-west, and taught villagers to raise Geo statues. The Vault of Qingce, with a glowing orb and treasure rooms, contains no sign of the beast.

195.content:
Qingxu Pool (also: Qingxu's Forsaken Tower): Qingxu Pool is a ruined site in Lisha, Liyue: stone towers and pavilions standing around a rocky outcrop in a shallow pool. Legend says an evil god once ruled a city here, that the city was drowned under water until the Archon War ended, and that the ruins were exposed as the tides withdrew. Five hidden Geo seals guard a Nameless Treasure, and an underground ruin below plays a part in a Yelan story quest.

A nearby settlement is the home of Tieshan. The ruins have attracted treasure hunters, the Liyue Qixing and the Fatui.

Geography: A subarea of Lisha whose ruin entrance stands in the middle of a giant rocky outcrop rising from a shallow pool, surrounded by steep cliffs and several stone towers set among the natural scenery. Local specialties: Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade and Qingxin. The viewpoint, Qingxu's Forsaken Tower, describes a ruined tower amid a verdant field that still guards a bygone age.

Places: The ruin entrance on the outcrop; five pavilions with Geo seals; a stone tablet; the underground ruins reached only during a story quest.

History: Legend, as Roald records it, says the ruins were left by an evil god whose name has been wiped from the record and by that god's people. The self-serving god was defeated and the city submerged until the end of the Archon War, then exposed as the tides withdrew. Roald heard this from Soraya, a scholar from Sumeru he met at Wangshu Inn.

People: No one lives in the ruins, but Tieshan comes from a settlement around the area; he says his home is Qingxu Pool, not the city.

Quests: Hidden in Nameless Treasures (the five-seal puzzle) and, in Yelan's story quest Calculated Gambit, the Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins quest domain.

Dangers: Hilichurl berserkers and shooters, Treasure Hoarders, large Dendro slimes, Abyss mages and Blazing Axe Mitachurls.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the pool is unchanged. The Fatui's excavation plot ended with Yusupov and Zhiyi's capture in Version 2.7, and no later story content was found that alters the ruins.

196.comment: Qingxu Pool: Qingxu Pool Redevelopment Plan
196.content: In Yelan's story quest the proposal to redevelop Qingxu Pool was Zhiyi's manifesto item, pushed with Fatui backing, to use the Blackcliff Forge's secret explosive recipes to break into the sealed underground ruins. Yelan saw through it, and Zhiyi was exposed.

197.content:
Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins (also: Underground Ruins of Qingxu Pool, Qingxu Pool treasure vault, Qīngxū-pǔ Dìxià Yíjì): The Qingxu Pool Underground Ruins are old chambers beneath Qingxu Pool in Lisha, Liyue, reached through a workers' entrance left over from an abandoned excavation. Rumour says treasure lies below. In the 2.7 Story quest "Foregone Conclusion" the Liyue investigator Yelan and the Traveler follow the conspirators Zhiyi and the Fatui ambassador Yusupov down here and expose them.

The site is the dramatic climax of Yelan's quest chain, not a place anyone visits in ordinary life. Qingxu Pool itself is a monster-infested ruin field that most people avoid, which is exactly why the conspirators chose it.

Geography: A stone labyrinth under Qingxu Pool: lifts and gates, flooded passages, sliding walls, rooms with grooves for water, and statues that can be pushed onto light spots. Part of it is a construction workers' emergency access route, built when the earlier excavation was attempted. The deepest chamber is a hidden room used as a meeting place.

History: Legend, as relayed by the Qingxu Pool wiki, says the ruins predate the Archon War: an evil god ruled the city, was defeated, and the city lay underwater until the war ended. The Liyue Qixing once approved a dig for the rumoured treasure, but the ruins were sealed and the technology to blast through the rock did not exist, so the project stopped. Many groups, including the Fatui, never gave up on the rumour.

Quests: In Foregone Conclusion (2.7), Yelan announces Zhiyi as her pick for Tianshu to lull him, has him followed, and learns that Yusupov has left the Fatui embassy alone for Qingxu Pool. Yelan leads the Traveler to a workers' entrance. Below, they overhear Zhiyi drinking with Yusupov and admitting he poisoned his teacher, Uncle Tian, using a slow-acting poison delivered in fish soup. Zhiyi then poisons Yusupov's wine, intending to burn the evidence and collapse the ruins with explosives, with Yusupov's undercover agents shut in the next room. Yelan and her Millelith appear before he can light it. Zhiyi tries to talk his way out, then is taken away. The next morning the physician Baizhu confirms Uncle Tian's poison is gone, with recovery expected to take time.

Dangers: Fire-throwing Pyro Abyss Mages, hilichurl fighters and shooters, a Blazing Axe Mitachurl, young Geovishaps and a Stonehide Lawachurl guard the route, according to the domain page. Water and collapse are further dangers; Zhiyi's explosive charge would have buried everything.

Atmosphere: Dim stone halls, dripping water and the glow of fire orbs; behind the sealed gate, the clink of cups and a quiet, self-satisfied conversation that the party overhears.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ruins have not been revisited in story content found for this entry. The explosives were removed by Yelan's people, and the treasure, if any, is still not proven to exist.

198.content:
Qingyun Peak (also: Moon Carver's Abode): Qingyun Peak is the home of the adeptus Moon Carver, one of the great peaks of Jueyun Karst in Minlin. He appears as a stag, a disciple of Rex Lapis and, according to a tablet at the foot of the steps, the kindest of all the adepti. His abode is sealed from the world, and high above the peak a small island of Plaustrite called the Dwelling in the Clouds floats, reached only by solving a puzzle.

Moon Carver is the first adeptus the Traveler meets in Jueyun Karst in the Archon Quest.

Geography: Qingyun Peak is a tall, cloud-ringed mountain in the adeptal highlands of Jueyun Karst. A stone staircase leads from the teleport waypoint up to a monument at the top. At the foot of the steps are tablets and a censer; the winding path east of the peak leads to another tablet.

Places: - The foot of the steps: tablets, one reading "Black clouds too shall pass, just as silver linings end", and a censer where the Traveler meets Moon Carver.
- Moon Carver's abode: a sealed cave past the censer behind a barrier.
- The stairs and the Three Cranes puzzle, ending at the Dwelling in the Clouds.

People: Moon Carver, a stag adeptus; in human form he appears as Houzhang, a middle-aged man with a streak of olive green in brown hair. Qilang, an herb gatherer, can be found on the peak. The Millelith pursued the Traveler here in the Archon Quest.

Culture: Jueyun Karst is considered sacred and mortals rarely climb here. The Qingyun tablets praise Moon Carver and carry short verses about the view above the changing weather.

History: Moon Carver was among the adepti Morax gathered to fight in the Archon War. He and Mountain Shaper are two of the three adepti who helped seal the dragon Azhdaha.

Atmosphere: Remote and windy, above a sea of clouds, with stone steps and tablets leading toward a sealed cave. At night the wind above the clouds is cold and relentless, in Roald's account.

Dangers: Slimes, Treasure Hoarders and whopperflowers roam the peak's paths. The adepti dislike intruders; the Millelith that followed the Traveler here were driven off.

Travel: From Qingyun Peak's waypoint, a staircase climbs to the monument. The puzzle that opens the way to the Dwelling in the Clouds is solved by finding three shining crane statues and turning them to face the monument.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qingyun Peak is still Moon Carver's mountain. No content from 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes it.

Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper still keep their peaks. Xianyun, the Cloud Retainer, lives in Liyue Harbor but retains care of the Dwelling in the Clouds.

199.content: Moon Carver is an adeptus with a stag form; his tablets call him Rex Lapis' disciple and the kindest of the adepti. The Traveler met him when fleeing the Millelith with a Sigil of Permission; he was enraged by Rex Lapis' apparent death and the Qixing's treatment of foreigners. In later Lantern Rites he is often seen with Mountain Shaper and wears a human form as Houzhang, a man with olive-green hair streak.

200.content:
Qiongji Estuary (also: Qiongji, Qióngjī-yě): Qiongji Estuary is the quiet eastern coastal area of Liyue where the Bishui River reaches the sea. Its heart is the Guili Plains, once the center of the Guili Assembly, the ancient civilisation that the gods Guizhong and Morax ruled together before the Archon War destroyed it. Around them lie Mingyun Village, an emptied mining hamlet, Luhua Pool with its bright terraced ponds and two watching statues, and the Yaoguang Shoal's gentle shallows.

The land is open and still. Most of what happened here is now only ruins, tablets and legend.

Geography: Flat plains, ponds and shoreline in eastern Liyue. The Bishui River's second arm (the one that does not end near Dawn Winery) flows through Qiongji Estuary into the Sea of Clouds. Yaoguang Shoal lies south of Mingyun Village and east of Guili Plains. Guili Plains lies near Liyue Harbor, reached by the road that runs through the Mt. Tianheng range north of the city.

Places: Guili Plains: ruins of the old Assembly, with Jade Plates and stone tablets. Mingyun Village: a ghost of a mining village with three small mines. Luhua Pool: a "unique landscape" of brightly colored pools watched by two giant statues. Yaoguang Shoal: a shallow, sandy shoal.

History: When Morax first came down, much of western Liyue was under the sea; he lowered the tides and raised Mt. Tianheng. Guizhong later joined his settlement north of the mountain with her people, and together they built the Guili Assembly. About 3,700 years ago, in the Archon War, Guizhong was slain in a battle that laid waste to Guili Plains and Dihua Marsh; a great flood followed, and Morax moved his people south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor.

Travel: The Plains lie near Liyue Harbor; Mingyun Village sits at the Assembly's old eastern edge, with Yaoguang Shoal south of it. The Bishui River's mouth is here.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Qiongji Estuary is a quiet, nearly empty coastal region, with the Assembly's ruins untouched.

No Qiongji-specific events appear in 6.x-7.1 content.

201.comment: Qiongji Estuary: The Guili Assembly and Guili Plains
201.content: The Guili Assembly was an ancient civilisation in Liyue founded and ruled by Guizhong, God of Dust, and Morax, God of Geo, with Marchosius the God of the Stove and the adepti in support. Its center was the Guili Plains, which Liyue Harbor's founders tried to expand into before Guizhong died. The Plains' viewpoint text, "Ruins of Guili," calls it a thriving city where a flower bloomed in abundance, consumed by war so that its people scattered again.

202.content: Mingyun Village is home to several scattered mining deposits, but most have dried up and the few remaining ores cannot sustain the village, so its people have left for Liyue Harbor and the Chasm. Hilichurls now use the leftover facilities. The adventurer Zhiqiong was born here and remembers its mines with fondness.

203.comment: Qiongji Estuary: Luhua Pool and Yaoguang Shoal
203.content: Luhua Pool is a unique landscape of brightly colored pools overlooked by two statues, with ruins hidden beneath. A legend says a deep, pure affection filled the ancient garden here and made the pool. Yaoguang Shoal, south of Mingyun Village and east of Guili Plains, is named for the bioluminescent sea creatures that once appeared after dusk like fallen stars swimming to shore; they are now gone, taken by lovers, though the shore may still have things to give.

204.content:
Ridge Watch: Ridge Watch is an ancient ruined site at Stone Gate, in the mountains where Mondstadt and Liyue meet. The domain description likens it to a boundary marker looking north and south, over mountain and river. Those who endure its trial can win artifacts.

It is a domain of blessing, so its place in the world is as a ritual and proving ground, not a settlement.

Geography: Ridge Watch stands at the start of the ridge in the Stone Gate area of Bishui Plain, on the mountainous route linking Mondstadt and Liyue. The in-game blurb describes ancient city ruins that overlook both north and south.

Atmosphere: A stern, wind-swept stronghold of old stone. The text speaks of toughness of spirit and body and of not fearing pain: whoever conquers the trial gains the protection of the ritual site and the power to pursue far-off dreams.

Dangers: The domain is guarded by Pyro slimes, hilichurl berserkers, fire-wielding Mitachurls and Geovishap. Its Ley Line Disorder (a gameplay effect) sends backlash shockwaves at attackers who strike a shielded character, which is why the levels are all titled "Unyielding".

History: No named historical event is attached to the ruins. Their apparent role as a boundary watchpost is an impression from the domain text, not a stated fact.

Status as of 7.1: Added in 1.5 and unchanged as of 7.1.

key: Roots of the Valley of Life
205.comment: Roots of the Valley of Life
205.content:
Roots of the Valley of Life: The Roots of the Valley of Life (an unofficial name) is a point of interest in The Chasm's Main Mining Area, in Liyue. The hidden exploration objective Seed from the Valley of Life takes place here.

Climbing the branches on the tree's southern side lets the player enter a Mine Passageway to Sumeru, near a mushroom growing on the tree.

Travel: The passageway is a shortcut between the underground mines of Liyue and Avidya Forest in Sumeru. The pages consulted give no in-world explanation of how it came to exist.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is simply an explorable site and travel link; no lore beyond the hidden objective is given.

206.content:
Sal Terrae (also: Salt of the Earth, Salt Temple, Havria's domain, Of Mysteries and Salt): Sal Terrae is a salt-crusted ruin on the Bishui Plain in Liyue, the last sanctuary of Havria, the gentle God of Salt, who refused to fight in the Archon War and gave her people shelter. Her own king killed her with a sword and the city turned to salt. Today a sealed domain holds her remains, a single salt flower, and the broken sword. It is the setting of the first act of Zhongli's story quest.

Since 5.7 the surface ruins also host Stygian Onslaught, a recurring ley line disturbance that the Millelith sealed off and the Traveler helps quell.

Geography: A low plateau of ruined walls and sunken foundations beside the Bishui River. Roald's diary says most of the ancient city sank into the riverbed, leaving the temple's foundation. A sealed ruin lies beneath, guarded by a stele reading that salt seals the ruin within and none uninvited may enter, and opened by Geo, Electro and pressure-plate mechanisms. Local specialties include Cor Lapis, Noctilucous Jade and Violetgrass; the nearby area holds Hilichurl camps and a Stonehide Lawachurl.

People: No residents now. Wanyan, of Yinyuan Hall, who in fact reveres Havria, and Kliment, a Fatuus archaeologist, entered the ruin with Zhongli; Treasure Hoarders had already looted much of the surface.

Culture: Havria's people honoured a goddess of kindness who handed out flowers as a blessing or comfort; Liyue's Flower Ball custom is said to have come from this. Her relics were a chalice that never ran out of salt and a ruler that turned land to salt for harvest, plus the broken sword of her death.

History: Havria was a weak, gentle god who refused to fight in the Archon War and instead conceded land after land to other gods, finally settling in a tiny holding at Sal Terrae. The city stood for centuries until its first and last king killed her with a sword. Her body dissipated into a salt flower (the "sal flore") and her released power turned everyone nearby into salt. A few outside the blast fled to Liyue Harbor.

Dangers: Hilichurls with Pyro and Electro bows; the Stonehide Lawachurl; a Fatui Pyro Agent (Kliment) in the sealed ruin; Pyro Abyss Mages in the sealed ruin; and, during Stygian Onslaught, powerful bosses spawned by the disturbance.

Quests: "Sal Flore" (Zhongli's Historia Antiqua Chapter, Act I): "Shadow of Yore", "Vortex's Wake", "A Ruin Under Lock and Key", "Farewell, Sweet Salt" and "A Record of All Things". The domain is "Of Mysteries and Salt". "Tumult Subduer" (5.7) opens Stygian Onslaught.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the sealed ruin is open, the relics are gone, and the surface hosts the recurring Stygian Onslaught disturbance. No new Sal Terrae canon appears in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

207.comment: Sal Terrae: Havria, God of Salt
207.content: Havria was a gentle god of the Archon War era, weak in power, who fled the fighting and made countless concessions to protect her followers. Her relics were a self-refilling salt chalice and a ruler that turned land into salt. Her kindness is the reason she could not defend herself against her own king. See her entry for her story.

key: Realm of Resounding in Sea and Living in Rosy Clouds
208.content:
Sea Gazer's Abode (also: Abode of Sea Gazer, Realm of Resounding in Sea and Living in Rosy Clouds): Sea Gazer's Abode is the hidden treasure house of Sea Gazer, an adeptus of Liyue who died long ago, located in the Lisha area. Abandoned and forgotten, it still runs on adeptal energy, which keeps its guardian mechanisms and the monsters inside active. It appears only in the Interlude quest Seagaze Sunset (Version 2.4), when the Traveler, Paimon and Shenhe enter it to fetch a huge piece of Sunset Vermillionite for the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber.

The abode is a quest domain, a pocket space reached through a waterfall once Shenhe lifts the adepti art that conceals it. Inside, false clouds hide the lower levels and the party must break the mechanisms keeping the illusion up in order to descend.

Geography: The entrance is hidden around Lisha and is revealed when Shenhe performs an adepti art that turns the weather rainy and removes the concealment; a Seelie then leads the party to a waterfall, which is the way in. Inside, the abode is three levels: floating islands above a sea of clouds, a lower cloud-wrapped level, and a deepest level with a pool of water, a maze of movable stone walls and Seelie courts.

People: Nobody lives in the abode and its builder, Sea Gazer, is long dead. The party inside consists of Paimon and Shenhe, who knows adepti arts and whose master is Cloud Retainer.

History: According to Xingqiu, citing the book "Records of Drifting Clouds", Sea Gazer built the abode to store his rarest and most exquisite treasures, among them Sunset Vermillionite. After he died the abode was abandoned and its location was lost to time. Xingqiu worked out that it lay in Lisha by cross-referencing a stack of folk-history books that make oblique references to it.

Dangers: Because the abode is abandoned, its adepti defences treat visitors as intruders. Ancient Array Cores release pulses that deal Physical damage, and each is protected by waves of monsters (slimes of several elements, hilichurls, Mitachurls, a Lawachurl, a Geovishap and Ruin Guards, per the domain's enemy lists). An inactive Ruin Guard on the lower levels awakens and smashes the ground during the descent.

Travel: Entry requires removing the concealing adepti art at the marked spot in Lisha and then following the Seelie to the waterfall. Within the abode movement is by gliding on wind currents, using Plaustrite platforms and pushing stone walls.

Quests: Seagaze Sunset, part 2 of Act I (The Crane Returns on the Wind) in the Interlude Chapter, is the only quest set here. After Xingqiu's briefing at the Feiyun Commerce Guild, the party reaches the abode, descends through its levels and finds the huge Sunset Vermillionite. Shenhe lifts it alone and carries it to the Jade Chamber worksite, where Ningguang's secretary Baiwen rates it the finest Plaustrite received so far and says it will go into the Jade Chamber's foundation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the abode is a finished quest location. Its treasure, the Sunset Vermillionite, was removed in 2.4 and is meant for the Jade Chamber's foundation.

The wiki lists no later appearance, and nothing in canon through 7.1 says what became of the remaining defences or the second Seelie in the court. Its builder remains dead and only sparsely described.

209.comment: Sea Gazer's Abode: Sea Gazer's Abode (Seagaze Sunset)
209.content: The abode is where the Traveler and Shenhe find the Sunset Vermillionite for the Jade Chamber: a hidden treasure house of the dead adeptus Sea Gazer in Lisha, with cloud-veiled levels, Ancient Array Cores, movable stone walls and a guiding Seelie.

210.content:
Sea of Clouds (also: Cloud-Coming Sea, Yunlai Sea): The Sea of Clouds ("Cloud-Coming Sea") is the southern coastal area of Liyue and the nation's gateway to the world. It holds Liyue Harbor, the great trading city where "a thousand ships" drop anchor and goods from all seven nations change hands under contract; the mountain barrier of Mt. Tianheng that shelters the city from the west; and the island spires of Guyun Stone Forest, where Rex Lapis is said to have pinned a sea god. Its Geo boss is the Geo Hypostasis.

The area is Liyue at its most public: crowded wharves, banks and guilds, and a cliff-backed city under the watch of the Qixing and Millelith. Beyond the quay, the sea is old and quiet around the stone islands.

Geography: Coastline, harbor and mountains in one view. Liyue Harbor sits on the sea with Mt. Tianheng rising to its west and north, making a natural shield; the road north leads out to Guili Plains and the Bishui River's mouth. Out on the water lies Guyun Stone Forest, an archipelago of seven large islands.

Places: Liyue Harbor has three districts: Feiyun Slope, the prosperous merchant district at the northern entrance; Chihu Rock, the lower-class district on an island to the southeast; and Yujing Terrace, the wealthy cliffside residential quarter in the west. Above the city floated the Qixing's Jade Chamber. Guyun Stone Forest lies offshore.

History: Before the Archon War, Rex Lapis led his people south of Mt. Tianheng and founded what is now Liyue Harbor. They tried to extend the city to Guili Plains, but after Guizhong died in the war they came back to the harbor. In the same war Rex Lapis defeated the sea god Osial at Guyun and pinned him to the sea floor with stone spears, whose broken remnants are the jagged cliffs there.

Travel: Roads lead north to Guili Plains and the Bishui country and east toward Qiongji Estuary. Ships dock at the harbor from every nation.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Liyue Harbor is thriving and the Qixing still govern; the Jade Chamber has been rebuilt.

Rex Lapis lives on as Zhongli. The 7.1 anomaly of the Celestial Nails is centered on the Chasm, not the harbor.

211.comment: Sea of Clouds: Osial and Guyun Stone Forest
211.content: Osial, the Overlord of the Vortex, was an ancient sea god who clashed with Morax in the Archon War. At Guyun Stone Forest Rex Lapis pinned him to the sea floor with stone spears, and the jagged cliffs there are the remnants of those lances. Osial could raise tsunamis as tall as Liyue's mountains. In Archon Quest Chapter I the Fatui unleashed him to lure out Rex Lapis and steal his Gnosis; Ningguang crushed him with the Jade Chamber. Locals call Guyun a forest of tombstones for the old gods.

212.comment: Sea of Clouds: Skybracer and Mt. Tianheng
212.content: Mt. Tianheng shields Liyue Harbor from the west. In a Lantern Rite telling, during the Archon War an enemy god's blow nearly toppled the peak onto a village at its foot, so the adeptus Skybracer had his antlers chopped off and wedged under the mountain, raising it higher. He fought on until his lifeblood ran out, and that blood became the Bishui River.

213.comment: Sea of Clouds: The founding of Liyue Harbor
213.content: Before the Archon War, Rex Lapis brought his people south of Mt. Tianheng to found Liyue Harbor. They later tried to move the city out to the Guili Plains, the central area of the Guili Assembly ruled by Guizhong, God of Dust, and Morax, but after Guizhong died in the war they returned to the harbor. The harbor launched Liyue's seafaring trade and is called Teyvat's largest market harbor.

214.content:
Second Life (also: Second Life shop, Rongfa Shangpu, 荣发商铺): Second Life is a small general goods shop in the main plaza of Chihu Rock, Liyue Harbor. Its owner, Dongsheng, is a former adventurer who left the road after a serious accident in Dihua Marsh, where a masked adeptus rescued him. He named the shop to remember that day.

It sells ordinary cooking ingredients such as salt, pepper, onion, milk, rice and tofu, and its stock is refreshed daily. The wiki says that high Liyue reputation earns a discount.

Places: One shop on the plaza of Chihu Rock, open day and night.

People: Dongsheng runs the shop. He used to be an adventurer who travelled everywhere, and has stayed put since being rescued. He calls his current life a simple one, and says the life he has was given to him by the adeptus.

Culture: The shop's name plays on a Liyue adage, 'a withered tree lives again', which Dongsheng uses for the idea of a life given back. The Chinese name takes the last part of the saying, meaning something like '(re-)flourishment'.

Atmosphere: A modest corner shop where the owner is polite and unhurried and the slogan is plain: satisfaction guaranteed.

Travel: In the central plaza of Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: Open as of 7.1, as far as the sources show.

215.content: Dongsheng is the owner of Second Life. A former adventurer injured in Dihua Marsh, he was rescued by a masked adeptus, after which he stopped travelling and opened a shop. He tells the story only to customers who ask.

216.content:
Spiritstone (also: the Chasm Nail, Wishstone): The Spiritstone is the Celestial Nail at the bottom of the Chasm in Liyue, a vast sky-blue crystal pillar. It was sent from the heavens to purify Abyssal corruption in the ancient civilisation of Lang-Gan. Zibai held it back long enough for many of Lang-Gan's people to flee, and its impact is said to have made the Chasm.

Geography: The nail hangs high in the Court of Pillars, the deepest point of the Chasm: Underground Mines, a vast cavern of old stone and glowing crystal. A viewpoint note attributed to Zhiqiong calls it a huge sky-blue crystal pillar that could only have come from the heavens, whose shade it shares. A crater surrounds the point of impact. A fragment, called the Wishstone, was found in the Stony Halls.

Places: Wishstone site (Stony Halls): where miners touched a fragment and began seeing their desires granted.

Court of Pillars: the cavern where the main body hangs, with five crystal mechanisms that feed into the nail.

Space beneath the nail: during the limited-time Perilous Trail event (2.7), the Chasm's Bed lay under it. See the Chasm's Bed entry.

History: Celestia sent the nail to purify the Abyssal taint in Lang-Gan. In the Realm of Rocks cinematic (Lantern Rite event, Luna IV) Istaroth tells Zibai that all places tainted by the Abyss must be purified and that this includes Lang-Gan. Zibai, who was a god of Lang-Gan, replies that she will die among its people. She raises a canopy of jade light under the falling nail, buying time for people to escape. Istaroth catches her as she falls and splits her soul into three. The survivors went on to Chenyu Vale, where their descendants live today, according to the wiki.

Atmosphere: A cathedral-like cavern, cold and silent, where a pale blue pillar hangs overhead. The nail seems to belong to another place entirely.

Dangers: Abyssal power once bound the nail, and the beings guarding it are Abyss Mages, an Abyss Herald and Khaenri'ahn rifthounds. The Khaenri'ahn Ruin Serpent Haftvad the Worm emerged when the Traveler released the nail.

Travel: Reached only by descending through the Chasm: Underground Mines, beyond the gate Zhiqiong identified near the camp. The Qixing had closed the Chasm after the Wishstone's effects on the miners.

Quests: Wherefore Did the Spiritstone Descend? (2.6), part six of the Chasm Delvers world quest series. The Traveler purifies five crystal mechanisms with a charged Lumenstone Adjuvant, drawing out Haftvad the Worm. Yelan shoots the nail with a Hydro-infused arrow, dropping it onto the serpent and subduing it, after which it floats back up lower than before.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the nail still hangs in the Chasm. The sources read do not record any Spiritstone-specific change from 6.x or 7.0-7.1.
